children.title: Frank-Wolfe Algorithm
children.top_down_role: Canonical method family organized by linearized search, feasible segments, and atomic iterates.

children.title: Conditional-Gradient Direction Model
children.top_down_role: Direction generation from the feasible-region linear model.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Gradient Direction Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Frank-Wolfe direction generated by the feasible-region linear model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, let \(f\) be differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\), and take \(x_t\in C\). Compute
\[
s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle,
\qquad d_t=s_t-x_t.
\]
Then \(d_t\) minimizes the first-order model increment over all feasible chords from \(x_t\):
\[
d_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in C-x_t}\langle\nabla f(x_t),d\rangle.
\]
The Frank-Wolfe gap is \(g_t=\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle=-\langle\nabla f(x_t),d_t\rangle\ge0\). If \(g_t=0\), output \(x_t\) as first-order stationary; otherwise use \(d_t\) as the update direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the gradient’s linear model over the feasible set, subtract the current iterate, and use the resulting chord as the Frank-Wolfe direction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
\(x_t\in C\).

notation.meaning: Linear-minimization oracle point at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction construction, chord formulation, and gap identity are mathematically consistent and algorithm is the correct role. No Frank-Wolfe source is supplied for the construction or the constrained first-order stationarity conclusion.

children.title: Feasible-Segment Update Geometry
children.top_down_role: Feasibility preservation through segments joining current iterates and oracle atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Segment Update Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility preservation along the Frank-Wolfe chord.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be convex and let \(x_t,s_t\in C\). For any step size \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\), the conditional-gradient update
\[
x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t(s_t-x_t)=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t
\]
belongs to \(C\). Thus the entire segment \([x_t,s_t]\) is feasible, no projection or feasibility restoration is required, and \(d_t=s_t-x_t\) is feasible for step lengths in \([0,1]\). The conclusion can fail for \(\gamma_t\notin[0,1]\), because extrapolation beyond either endpoint need not remain in a general convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex combination of the current feasible iterate and the oracle point remains feasible; extrapolated steps need not remain in the domain.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex.
\(x_t,s_t\in C\).

notation.meaning: Closed segment joining the iterate and oracle point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-segment feasibility statement is precise, agrees across plain text and LaTeX, and property fits the leaf. It nevertheless lacks the required inspectable source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Atomic Iterate Representation
children.top_down_role: Iterates maintained as convex combinations of discovered atoms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-bounded recompression of an atomic Frank-Wolfe iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=\dim(\operatorname{aff}C)\). Every \(x_t\in C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) admits a representation \[x_t=\sum_{a\in B_t}\theta_a a,\qquad \theta_a\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a\in B_t}\theta_a=1,\qquad |B_t|\le r+1.\] This is an existence statement: an uncompressed classical recursion may store up to \(|A_0|+t\) atoms, explicit recompression is needed to enforce the dimension bound, and atomic representations can be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every iterate can be recompressed to at most affine-dimension plus one atoms, although the stored representation may grow linearly and need not be unique.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\subset\mathbb R^n\).
\(x_t\) has a finite convex representation by atoms in \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Caratheodory Recompression
Atomic Iterate Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive convex-combination representation of classical Frank-Wolfe iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), initialize \(x_0\in\operatorname{conv}(A_0)\) for a finite \(A_0\subset\mathcal A\), and let each oracle output satisfy \(s_t\in\mathcal A\). Under
\[
x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t,
\qquad \gamma_t\in[0,1],
\]
every iterate admits a finite atomic representation
\[
x_t=\sum_{a\in A_t}\lambda_{t,a}a,
\qquad \lambda_{t,a}\ge0,
\qquad \sum_{a\in A_t}\lambda_{t,a}=1,
\]
where \(A_t\subseteq A_0\cup\{s_0,\ldots,s_{t-1}\}\). Without aggregation or deletion, at most one new atom is introduced per iteration, so \(|A_t|\le |A_0|+t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iterate is a convex combination of initial and previously returned atoms, with at most one new atom added by each classical iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) and \(x_0\) has a finite atomic representation.
Every oracle output \(s_t\) belongs to \(\mathcal A\).
Every step size \(\gamma_t\) lies in \([0,1]\).

notation.meaning: Finite active set used to represent the iterate.
Convex coefficient of atom a at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive convex-combination representation and support-size bound are consistent with the stated assumptions, and representation is the correct kind. No source supports the atomic-iterate and active-set accounting claims.

children.title: Single-Oracle Iteration Model
children.top_down_role: The classical accounting model centered on one linear-minimization call per iteration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource convention for completed classical Frank-Wolfe iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A completed classical Frank-Wolfe iteration belongs to the single-oracle model when it evaluates \(
abla f(x_t)\), makes exactly one query \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x_t),sangle\), and forms \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\), without another linear-minimization query for stepsize selection or certification. Hence, excluding initialization and separately requested checks, \(T\) completed iterations satisfy \(N_{
abla f}(T)=N_{\mathrm{LMO}}(T)=T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the single-oracle convention, every completed classical Frank-Wolfe iteration uses one gradient evaluation and one linear-minimization query.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\in C\) and \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\).
Each completed iteration makes exactly one point-valued LMO query.
Initialization and additional certificate queries are charged separately.

notation.meaning: Gradient evaluations in T completed iterations.
Linear-minimization queries in T completed iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Oracle Accounting Convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oracle Counts Do Not Determine Runtime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between the single-call convention and total computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identities \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}=N_{\nabla f}=T\) do not imply a runtime bound unless gradient evaluation, the LMO, stepsize selection, stopping checks, and representation maintenance have controlled costs in a declared computational model. Exact line search, in particular, can have implementation-dependent objective-evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One gradient and one LMO call per iteration do not price line search, representation work, or total runtime.
assumptions_latex: The model counts primitive calls but supplies no uniform cost bounds for primitives or auxiliary work.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Counts Do Not Determine Runtime
Single-Oracle Iteration Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration resource count for the classical Frank-Wolfe scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the classical Frank-Wolfe iteration, \(\nabla f(x_t)\) is evaluated once, one linear-minimization query produces \(s_t\), and one convex-combination update produces \(x_{t+1}\). Therefore, after \(T\) completed iterations,
\[
N_{\nabla f}=T,
\qquad N_{\mathrm{LMO}}=T,
\qquad N_{\mathrm{rep}}\le T,
\]
apart from initialization and any separately charged stopping checks. If \(\gamma_t\) is prescribed or obtained from curvature data, no objective evaluation is intrinsically required; exact line search may add multiple objective evaluations per iteration. Thus iteration complexity equals linear-oracle complexity only under this declared single-call convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical Frank-Wolfe uses one gradient and one linear-minimization call per iteration; line search and representation maintenance must be counted separately.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration makes exactly one point-valued linear-minimization query.
Gradient evaluation, line search, and representation work are charged separately.
The step-size rule does not make additional linear-minimization calls.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-LMO accounting claim fits the leaf and complexity_bound is appropriate, but it lacks a source. The meaning of N_rep must also be fixed before asserting N_rep at most T, and the objective-evaluation cost attributed to exact line search requires a declared computational model.

children.title: Convex Primal-Accuracy Certificates
children.top_down_role: Gap interpretations for convex objective accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Primal-Accuracy Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Frank-Wolfe gap as a convex primal-suboptimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable, and let \(x\in C\). Choose \(s(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle\) and define \(g_{m FW}(x)=\langle\nabla f(x),x-s(x)\rangle\). For \(f^*=\min_{y\in C}f(y)\), convexity gives \[0\le f(x)-f^*\le g_{m FW}(x).\] Hence the computable inequality \(g_{m FW}(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex differentiable objectives, the Frank-Wolfe gap upper-bounds primal suboptimality, so a gap at most epsilon certifies epsilon-optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and differentiable.
The linear minimization oracle is exact.

notation.meaning: Minimum objective value over the feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity Is Essential for Primal-Accuracy Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global-value certification without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without convexity, a zero Frank-Wolfe gap need not imply global optimality. On \(C=[-1,1]\), let \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\). At \(x=0\), \(\nabla f(0)=0\), hence \(g_{\rm FW}(0)=0\), while \(f(0)=1>0=\min_{y\in C}f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex stationary point can have zero Frank-Wolfe gap without being globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Is Essential for Primal-Accuracy Certification

children.title: Stationarity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Gap interpretations used for constrained first-order stationarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent variational and normal-cone formulations of a zero Frank-Wolfe gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a closed convex set \(C\) and \(x\in C\), define \(N_C(x)=\{v:\langle v,y-xangle\le0\  orall y\in C\}\). Whenever the Frank-Wolfe gap is finite, \[g_{m FW}(x)=0\iff \langle
abla f(x),y-xangle\ge0\  orall y\in C\iff-
abla f(x)\in N_C(x)\iff0\in
abla f(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero Frank-Wolfe gap is equivalent to the feasible variational inequality and normal-cone stationarity inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex.
\(x\in C\).
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\).
The Frank-Wolfe gap is finite.

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to C at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Form of Frank-Wolfe Stationarity
Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frank-Wolfe gap as a constrained first-order stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space and let \(f\) be differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\), without assuming convexity. Define \[g_{m FW}(x)=\max_{y\in C}\langle
abla f(x),x-yangle.\] Then \(g_{m FW}(x)\ge0\), and \(g_{m FW}(x)=0\) if and only if \(\langle
abla f(x),y-xangle\ge0\) for every \(y\in C\). Thus \(g_{m FW}(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\langle
abla f(x),y-xangle\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frank-Wolfe gap is zero exactly at constrained first-order stationary points and bounds every feasible first-order descent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).

notation.meaning: Maximum linearized feasible descent at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stationarity equivalence and approximate directional inequality are correct and fit the certificate container, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Termination-Progress Certificate Pair
children.top_down_role: Oracle-derived criteria for termination and progress assessment.

children.title: Stopping Certificates
children.top_down_role: Oracle-derived evidence used to support termination decisions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Stale Gap Is Not a Current-Iterate Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise validity boundary for Frank-Wolfe stopping certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computed value \(g_{\rm FW}(x_t)\) certifies only its query point \(x_t\). Without a justified residual-transfer bound, \(g_{\rm FW}(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) does not certify a different point \(x_{t+1}\). For example, on \(C=[0,1]\) with \(f(x)=x^2\), \(g_{\rm FW}(0)=0\), whereas \(g_{\rm FW}(1)=2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previously computed Frank-Wolfe gap cannot certify another iterate without a valid transfer bound.
assumptions_latex: The certificate is evaluated at \(x_t\), but termination is proposed at a different point \(x_{t+1}\).
No residual-transfer bound is available.
knowledge_statements.title: A Stale Gap Is Not a Current-Iterate Certificate
Stopping Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-based termination for convex accuracy or nonconvex stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an iterate \(x_t\in C\), compute an exact linear minimizer \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x_t),sangle\) and the gap \(g_t=\langle
abla f(x_t),x_t-s_tangle\). The test \(g_t\le\varepsilon\) is a verifiable stopping certificate. If \(f\) is convex, it certifies \(f(x_t)-f^*\le\varepsilon\). Without convexity, it certifies \(\langle
abla f(x_t),y-x_tangle\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(y\in C\), namely approximate constrained first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping when the exact Frank-Wolfe gap is small certifies convex objective accuracy or, without convexity, approximate constrained stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
The displayed linear minimizer is computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_t\le\varepsilon\) certifies either \(f(x_t)-f^*\le\varepsilon\) under convexity or \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity generally.

notation.meaning: Exact Frank-Wolfe gap at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stopping test correctly distinguishes convex primal accuracy from general constrained stationarity, but it has no supporting source or locator.

children.title: Progress Certificates
children.top_down_role: Oracle-derived evidence used to assess optimization progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimized one-step curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the curvature inequality in the seed, let \(C_f>0\) and choose \(\gamma_t=\min\{g_t/C_f,1\}\). Then \[f(x_t)-f(x_{t+1})\ge\begin{cases}g_t^2/(2C_f),&g_t\le C_f,\\g_t-C_f/2,&g_t>C_f.\end{cases}\] Exact line search over the same feasible segment attains an objective value no larger than the short-step trial point and therefore satisfies the same decrease lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing the curvature model yields the short step and an explicit lower bound on one-step objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has Frank-Wolfe curvature at most \(C_f>0\).
\(s_t\) is an exact LMO atom.
The update uses the short step or exact line search on the same segment.

notation.meaning: Exact Frank-Wolfe gap at iteration t.

knowledge_statements.title: Short-Step Decrease Certificate
Progress Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-based lower certificate for one-step objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) has Frank-Wolfe curvature at most \(C_f\) on \(C\). At \(x_t\), let \(s_t\) minimize \(\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\) over \(C\), set \(g_t=\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\), and update \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t(s_t-x_t)\) with \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\). Then \[f(x_t)-f(x_{t+1})\ge \gamma_t g_t-\frac{C_f}{2}\gamma_t^2.\] Whenever the right-hand side is positive, it is a computable certified lower bound on the iteration's objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current gap, step size, and curvature bound provide a certified lower bound on the objective decrease achieved by a Frank-Wolfe step.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable with Frank-Wolfe curvature bounded by \(C_f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature descent inequality is correct and is properly presented as a progress certificate, but an inspectable curvature-lemma citation is required.

children.title: Reliability under Inexact Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Certificate interpretation when oracle responses have controlled inaccuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Inexact Gap Can Falsely Trigger Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of the additive stopping correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(x=1\). The exact LMO returns \(s=0\), so \(g=1\). An additive-error oracle with \(\delta=1\) may return \(\widetilde s=1\), because \(1\le\min_{s\in C}s+1\). Its raw gap is \(\widetilde g=0\), although the exact gap and primal error equal one. Thus stopping on \(\widetilde g\le\varepsilon<1\) is unsound, while \(\widetilde g+\delta=1\) remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An allowed inexact LMO can report zero raw gap at a point with positive exact gap; the certified error correction is indispensable.
assumptions_latex: The LMO has certified additive error \(\delta=1\).

notation.meaning: Gap computed from the inexact atom.

knowledge_statements.title: Raw Inexact Gap Can Falsely Trigger Stopping
Reliability under Inexact Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive oracle errors enlarge stopping certificates by a known amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde s_t\in C\) satisfy \(\langle
abla f(x_t),\widetilde s_tangle\le\min_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x_t),sangle+\delta_t\), where \(\delta_t\ge0\) is known. Define \(\widetilde g_t=\langle
abla f(x_t),x_t-\widetilde s_tangle\) and let \(g_t\) denote the exact Frank-Wolfe gap. Then \[\widetilde g_t\le g_t\le\widetilde g_t+\delta_t.\] Consequently, \(\widetilde g_t+\delta_t\le\varepsilon\) is a reliable stopping test; for convex \(f\), it certifies \(f(x_t)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a known additive oracle error, adding that error to the computed gap restores a reliable stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
The linear oracle has known additive error \(\delta_t\ge0\).
\(f\) is differentiable; convexity is additionally assumed for primal accuracy.

notation.meaning: Gap computed from the inexact oracle output.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error inequalities and corrected stopping test are mathematically correct and fit the reliability container, but no source is cited.

children.title: Inexact-Oracle Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate families compatible with approximate linear minimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate correction under a verified multiplicative gap guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\max_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x),x-s\rangle\). Suppose an approximate oracle returns \(\widetilde s\in C\) with a verified constant \(\rho\in(0,1]\) such that \(\widetilde g(x):=\langle\nabla f(x),x-\widetilde s\rangle\ge\rho g(x)\). Then \(g(x)\le\widetilde g(x)/\rho\). Thus \(\widetilde g(x)/\rho\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity and, for convex \(f\), \(f(x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified relative gap guarantee yields a valid certificate after division by its approximation factor.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is differentiable.
\(\widetilde g(x)\ge\rho g(x)\) is verified for some \(\rho>0\).
Convexity is additionally required for primal accuracy.

notation.meaning: Gap computed from the approximate oracle atom.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Accuracy Linear-Oracle Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncertified Approximation Gives No Upper Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability boundary for approximate linear-minimization outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gap computed from an approximate atom need not upper-bound the exact Frank-Wolfe gap without a verified error relation. On \(C=[0,1]\), at \(x=1\) with \(\nabla f(x)=1\), returning \(\widetilde s=1\) gives \(\widetilde g=0\), whereas the exact minimizer is \(s=0\) and \(g=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small approximate gap is not a certificate unless the oracle supplies a verified additive or relative guarantee.
assumptions_latex: No accuracy relation is imposed on \(\widetilde s\).

notation.meaning: Gap computed using an uncontrolled approximate atom.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Approximation Gives No Upper Certificate
Inexact-Oracle Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected primal and stationarity certificates for additive approximate linear minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in C\), suppose an approximate linear oracle returns \(\widetilde s\in C\) and a certified error \(\delta\ge0\) such that \(\langle
abla f(x),\widetilde sangle\le\min_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x),sangle+\delta\). The corrected quantity \[U_\delta(x)=\langle
abla f(x),x-\widetilde sangle+\delta\] upper-bounds the exact Frank-Wolfe gap. Therefore \(U_\delta(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity; if \(f\) is convex, it also certifies \(f(x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\). The correction is valid only when \(\delta\) itself is a verified oracle-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate linear oracle yields a valid certificate after its verified additive error bound is added to the computed gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
The oracle supplies a certified additive error bound \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\rm FW}(x)\le U_\delta(x)\), with convex primal error also bounded by \(U_\delta(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The corrected quantity validly upper-bounds the exact Frank-Wolfe gap and supports both stated certificates, but the inexact-oracle model lacks a citation.

children.title: Frank-Wolfe Curvature Family
children.top_down_role: Curvature measures tailored to feasible chords and conditional-gradient progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-curvature boundary for convex differentiable objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex differentiable \(f\), every feasible-chord first-order remainder is nonnegative, so \(C_f\ge0\). Moreover, \[C_f=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f((1-\gamma)x+\gamma s)=(1-\gamma)f(x)+\gamma f(s)\] for all \(x,s\in C\) and \(\gamma\in[0,1]\), equivalently, \(f|_C\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex Frank-Wolfe curvature is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the objective is affine on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable and convex on a neighborhood of \(C\).
Curvature uses the v58 definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Curvature Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of curvature constants under restriction of the admissible chord family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible triple family \(\mathcal T\), let \(C_f(\mathcal T)\) be the curvature supremum restricted to \(\mathcal T\). If \(\mathcal T_1\subseteq\mathcal T_2\), then \[C_f(\mathcal T_1)\le C_f(\mathcal T_2)\le C_f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the admissible chord family can only decrease the curvature constant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(C\) satisfy the v58 curvature-definition assumptions.
\(\mathcal T_1\subseteq\mathcal T_2\) are explicitly declared families of admissible feasible-chord triples.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Curvature Monotonicity
Frank-Wolfe Curvature Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-invariant curvature along feasible Frank-Wolfe chords.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty compact convex set and let \(f\) be differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\). Its Frank-Wolfe curvature constant is \[C_f=\sup_{\substack{x,s\in C,\;\gamma\in(0,1]}}\frac{2}{\gamma^2}\Bigl(f(x+\gamma(s-x))-f(x)-\gamma\langle\nabla f(x),s-x\rangle\Bigr).\] Restricted curvature constants are obtained by taking the same supremum over a specified family of feasible chords or directions. Under an invertible affine reparameterization of \(C\) with the objective pulled back accordingly, the value of \(C_f\) is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frank-Wolfe curvature measures the worst quadratic remainder along feasible chords and is invariant under invertible affine reparameterization.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_f\) is the displayed feasible-chord remainder supremum and is affine invariant.

notation.meaning: Frank-Wolfe curvature constant of f over C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed curvature definition and affine-invariance claim fit the definition container, but neither the definition nor the claimed family of restricted constants has inspectable support.

children.title: Diameter-Based Smoothness Models

knowledge_statements.title: Diameter-Based Smoothness Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-dependent control of feasible-chord curvature by smoothness and diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) have diameter \(D=\sup_{x,y\in C}\lVert x-y\rVert\), and suppose \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) and its dual norm. Then for every \(x,s\in C\) and \(\gamma\in[0,1]\), \[f(x+\gamma(s-x))\le f(x)+\gamma\langle\nabla f(x),s-x\rangle+\frac{L D^2}{2}\gamma^2.\] Consequently, the Frank-Wolfe curvature satisfies \(C_f\le L D^2\). Unlike \(C_f\), the separate constants \(L\) and \(D\) depend on the selected norm and coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz gradient smoothness and feasible-set diameter imply the classical curvature bound C_f at most L times D squared.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex with diameter \(D\).
\(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in the chosen norm.

notation.meaning: Gradient Lipschitz constant in the chosen norm.
Diameter of the feasible set in that norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional equality family showing sharpness of the diameter-based curvature bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-D/2,D/2]\subset\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=Lx^2/2\), where \(L,D>0\). Then \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, \(\operatorname{diam}(C)=D\), and for \(x=-D/2\), \(s=D/2\), and every \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), \[\frac{2}{\gamma^2}\bigl(f(x+\gamma(s-x))-f(x)-\gamma f'(x)(s-x)\bigr)=LD^2.\] Therefore \(C_f=LD^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic on an interval attains the diameter-smoothness curvature bound exactly.
assumptions_latex: The Frank-Wolfe curvature uses the v58 normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Strong-Convexity Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A norm-dependent condition measure coupling objective curvature with polytope width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a compact convex polytope in a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex in that norm, and let \(w_{\rm pyr}(C)>0\) denote the pyramidal width of \(C\) in the same norm. Define the geometric strong-convexity scale and associated condition ratio by \[\mu_{\rm geom}=\mu\,w_{\rm pyr}(C)^2,\qquad \kappa_{\rm FW}=\frac{C_f}{\mu_{\rm geom}}.\] These quantities couple objective growth with feasible-set geometry; linear-rate bounds for away-step variants are expressed using constants of this form, subject to the precise pyramidal-width convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric condition scale multiplies objective strong convexity by squared polytope width, coupling function growth with feasible-set geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a compact convex polytope with positive pyramidal width.
\(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the same norm used for the width.
\(C_f<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_{\rm geom}=\mu w_{\rm pyr}(C)^2\) and \(\kappa_{\rm FW}=C_f/\mu_{\rm geom}\).

notation.meaning: Pyramidal width under a fixed convention and norm.

children.title: Classical Diminishing Schedules

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Diminishing Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical open-loop Frank-Wolfe schedule with reciprocal decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a differentiable objective \(f\), a compact convex feasible set \(C\), and \(x_0\in C\), for \(t=0,1,2,\ldots\) compute \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\), choose the predetermined step size \(\gamma_t=2/(t+2)\), and set \[x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t.\] Stop at a prescribed iteration budget and return the last iterate. The schedule is open loop because \(\gamma_t\) depends only on \(t\), satisfies \(\gamma_t\downarrow0\), \(\sum_t\gamma_t=\infty\), and \(\sum_t\gamma_t^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical Frank-Wolfe schedule uses gamma_t = 2/(t+2), producing feasible convex-combination iterates with diminishing but nonsummable steps.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).
An exact linear minimization oracle is available.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_T)-f^\star\le 2C_f/(T+2)\) for every \(T\ge1\), hence the linear-oracle complexity for primal error at most \(\varepsilon\) is \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\).

children.title: Averaging Schedules

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex, \(x_0\in C\), and \(s_i\in C\).
The updates satisfy \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\) with \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\).

notation.meaning: weight of the initial point after T updates
weight of oracle atom i after T updates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit convex-average weights induced by open-loop Frank-Wolfe updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(T\ge1\) updates, \[x_T=w_{T,-1}x_0+\sum_{i=0}^{T-1}w_{T,i}s_i,\qquad w_{T,-1}=\prod_{k=0}^{T-1}(1-\gamma_k),\qquad w_{T,i}=\gamma_i\prod_{k=i+1}^{T-1}(1-\gamma_k).\] These weights are nonnegative and sum to one. If \(\gamma_t=2/(t+2)\), then \(\gamma_0=1\), \(w_{T,-1}=0\), and \[w_{T,i}=\frac{2(i+1)}{T(T+1)},\qquad 0\le i<T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every open-loop Frank-Wolfe iterate is a product-weighted convex average of the initial point and past oracle atoms; the classical reciprocal schedule removes the initial point and gives linearly increasing atom weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Weight Averaging Representation
Averaging Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Open-loop iterates represented as explicit weighted averages of oracle atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\) with \(\gamma_t=2/(t+2)\) for \(t\ge0\). Since \(\gamma_0=1\), after \(T\ge1\) updates the iterate has the explicit averaging representation \[x_T=\sum_{i=0}^{T-1}\alpha_{T,i}s_i,\qquad \alpha_{T,i}=\frac{2(i+1)}{T(T+1)}.\] The coefficients are nonnegative and satisfy \(\sum_{i=0}^{T-1}\alpha_{T,i}=1\). Thus later oracle atoms receive linearly increasing weight while feasibility follows directly from convexity of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the classical open-loop schedule, the iterate is a convex average of past oracle atoms with weights increasing linearly in their indices.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and every \(s_i\) belongs to \(C\).
The update uses \(\gamma_t=2/(t+2)\) starting at \(t=0\).

notation.meaning: Weight of oracle atom i in iterate T.
Linear-oracle atom produced at iteration i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging representation and weights are correct for gamma_t = 2/(t+2), and representation is the proper content kind, but no supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Primal-Dual Schedules
children.top_down_role: Open-loop policies coordinated with primal-dual certificate behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled open-loop averaging of primal iterates and affine-minorant lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and differentiable on compact convex \(C\). At iteration \(t\), compute \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\) and the lower bound \(\ell_t=f(x_t)+\langle\nabla f(x_t),s_t-x_t\rangle\le f^*\). Given predetermined \(\gamma_t\in(0,1]\), update \[x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t,\qquad L_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)L_t+\gamma_t\ell_t,\] starting from any certified \(L_0\le f^*\). Then \(L_t\le f^*\), and \(f(x_t)-L_t\) is a computable primal-dual accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same open-loop weights can update feasible primal iterates and valid affine-minorant lower bounds, yielding a computable primal-dual gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and differentiable.
\(L_0\le f^*\) and \(\gamma_t\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_t\le f^*\le f(x_t)\), so \(f(x_t)-L_t\) certifies primal accuracy.

notation.meaning: Lower bound obtained by minimizing the affine model at x_t.

children.title: Certificate-Aware Schedule Comparisons

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Aware Schedule Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison through the best primal-dual Frank-Wolfe certificate generated by each open-loop schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex on a nonempty compact convex set \(C\). For iterates \(x_k\in C\), let \(s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_k),s\rangle\), \(U_t=\min_{0\le k\le t}f(x_k)\), and \(L_t=\max_{0\le k\le t}\{f(x_k)-g_k\}\), where \(g_k=\langle\nabla f(x_k),x_k-s_k\rangle\). The schedule certificate is \(\Delta_t=U_t-L_t\). Schedule \(A\) certificate-dominates schedule \(B\) through horizon \(T\) when \(\Delta_t^A\le\Delta_t^B\) for every \(0\le t\le T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare schedules by their best feasible value minus their strongest oracle-derived lower bound; one dominates when this computable certificate is never larger through the chosen horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(C\).
\(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Each linear minimization oracle is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U_t-f^\star\le\Delta_t\), so \(\Delta_t\) is a valid computable certificate for schedule comparison.

notation.meaning: best certified lower and upper bounds through iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate construction is mathematically plausible and the definition fits the comparison leaf, but no citation supports either the running lower-bound convention or the certificate-dominance relation. A source with a specific locator is required.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). Given \(x_t\in C\), compute \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\) and set \(d_t=s_t-x_t\). Choose any \(\gamma_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in[0,1]} f(x_t+\gamma d_t)\), then update \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\). Stop when \(g_t=\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\le\varepsilon\), and otherwise repeat. The output is the last iterate together with its computable Frank-Wolfe gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a nonnegative stopping tolerance, minimize the objective exactly along the feasible segment from the current iterate to the linear-oracle point, use the minimizing segment parameter, and stop when the Frank-Wolfe gap meets the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Frank-Wolfe Line Search

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1 General Structure of a Line-Search p. 71
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form exact Frank-Wolfe segment search for a convex quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+b^\top x+c\), \(Q\succeq0\), let \(d=s-x\), and set \(g=-\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle\ge0\). Along the segment, \[f(x+\gamma d)=f(x)-\gamma g+\tfrac12\gamma^2d^\top Qd.\] If \(d^\top Qd>0\), an exact parameter is \[\gamma^\star=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\frac{g}{d^\top Qd}\right).\] If \(d^\top Qd=0\) and \(g>0\), the unique minimizing endpoint is \(\gamma^\star=1\); if both quantities vanish, every \(\gamma\in[0,1]\) minimizes the restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic, exact Frank-Wolfe line search clips the unconstrained scalar minimizer to the unit interval, with explicit flat-direction cases.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+b^\top x+c\) with \(Q\succeq0\).
\(d=s-x\) is a Frank-Wolfe direction and \(g=-\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma^\star=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}(g/(d^\top Qd))\) when \(d^\top Qd>0\), with the stated flat-direction alternatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Quadratic Closed Form

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient scalar optimality conditions for convex exact Frank-Wolfe segment search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(\gamma)=f(x+\gamma d)\) be convex and differentiable on \([0,1]\). A parameter \(\gamma^\star\in[0,1]\) minimizes \(\phi\) if and only if \[0\in\phi'(\gamma^\star)+N_{[0,1]}(\gamma^\star).\] Equivalently, \(\phi'(\gamma^\star)=0\) for \(0<\gamma^\star<1\), \(\phi'(0)\ge0\) for \(\gamma^\star=0\), and \(\phi'(1)\le0\) for \(\gamma^\star=1\). For a Frank-Wolfe direction, \(\phi'(0)=-g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)\), so a positive Frank-Wolfe gap excludes \(\gamma^\star=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex exact segment minimizer satisfies the one-dimensional normal-cone condition; interior and endpoint solutions obey the corresponding directional-derivative conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\{x+\gamma d:0\le\gamma\le1\}\).
\(\phi(\gamma)=f(x+\gamma d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\phi'(\gamma^\star)+N_{[0,1]}(\gamma^\star)\), with the stated interior and endpoint alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Curvature Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive Frank-Wolfe step based on a backtracked local quadratic-curvature estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\tau>1\) and an initial estimate \(M_t>0\). Compute \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\), \(d_t=s_t-x_t\), and \(g_t=-\langle\nabla f(x_t),d_t\rangle\). For \(M=M_t,\tau M_t,\tau^2M_t,\ldots\), set \(\gamma(M)=\min\{g_t/(M\lVert d_t\rVert^2),1\}\) and accept the first \(M\) satisfying \(f(x_t+\gamma(M)d_t)\le f(x_t)-\gamma(M)g_t+M\gamma(M)^2\lVert d_t\rVert^2/2\). Set \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma(M)d_t\) and retain the accepted estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase a local curvature estimate until its quadratic model upper-bounds the trial objective, then use the corresponding model-minimizing feasible step.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable with locally Lipschitz gradient near the tested segments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies \(f(x_{t+1})\le f(x_t)-\gamma_t g_t+\tfrac{M\gamma_t^2}{2}\lVert d_t\rVert^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy is mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but its initialization, multiplicative updates, acceptance test, and estimate-reuse convention define a specific variant for which no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Driven Step Sizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible steps selected by minimizing a gap-calibrated quadratic upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_t\in C\), compute \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\), \(d_t=s_t-x_t\), and the computable gap \(g_t=-\langle\nabla f(x_t),d_t\rangle\). For a positive curvature scale \(B_t\), choose \(\gamma_t=\min\{g_t/B_t,1\}\) and set \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\). The scale must be selected or increased until \(f(x_t+\gamma_t d_t)\le f(x_t)-\gamma_t g_t+B_t\gamma_t^2/2\); stop when \(g_t\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the step directly with the computable Frank-Wolfe gap, capping it at one and validating the associated quadratic upper model.

\(f\) is differentiable on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saddle representation of constrained convex minimization using the indicator-support conjugate pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\sigma_C(y)=\sup_{s\in C}\langle y,s\rangle\). Since \(\delta_C=\sigma_C^*\), define \(\mathcal{L}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,x\rangle-\sigma_C(y)\). Then the constrained problem has the Lagrangian representation \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\mathcal{L}(x,y).\] For fixed \(x\), the supremum enforces membership in \(C\); it equals \(f(x)\) on \(C\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the constraint indicator as the conjugate of the support function, producing a saddle Lagrangian whose maximization enforces membership in the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expression of the linear minimization oracle and Frank-Wolfe gap through the support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty compact convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(\sigma_C(y)=\max_{s\in C}\langle y,s\rangle\). For any \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a linear minimization oracle returns \(s(y)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle y,s\rangle=\operatorname*{argmax}_{s\in C}\langle-y,s\rangle\), and its value is \(-\sigma_C(-y)\). Consequently, at \(x\in C\) with \(y=\nabla f(x)\), the Frank-Wolfe gap is \[g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)=\langle y,x\rangle+\sigma_C(-y)=\langle y,x-s(y)\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear minimization oracle evaluates the negative support function, and the Frank-Wolfe gap is the difference between the current linear value and that oracle value.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, let \(\delta_C\) be its convex indicator, and define \(\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{s\in C}\langle z,s\rangle\). For a proper closed convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), consider \(p^\star=\inf_x\{f(x)+\delta_C(x)\}\) and its Fenchel dual \(d^\star=\sup_y\{-f^*(y)-\sigma_C(-y)\}\). Assume \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(C)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(p^\star=d^\star\). For any \(x\in C\) at which \(f\) is differentiable, set \(y=\nabla f(x)\). Fenchel equality gives \(f(x)+f^*(y)=\langle y,x\rangle\), and hence \[f(x)-\bigl(-f^*(y)-\sigma_C(-y)\bigr)=\langle y,x\rangle+\sigma_C(-y)=g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an explicit relative-interior qualification, the constrained primal and Fenchel dual have equal optimal values. At a gradient-generated dual point, their objective difference equals the Frank-Wolfe gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality correspondence for the constrained primal and support-function dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) and dual \(\sup_y\{-f^*(y)-\sigma_C(-y)\}\), a finite-valued pair \((x,y)\) has zero primal-dual gap if and only if \[y\in\partial f(x),\qquad x\in\partial\sigma_C(-y),\] equivalently \(y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle y,s\rangle\). Any such zero-gap feasible pair is primal-dual optimal by weak duality. The relative-interior qualification in the accepted seed guarantees equality of optimal values and the standard strong-duality regime. If \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), then \(y=\nabla f(x)\), and the conditions are equivalent to zero Frank--Wolfe gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero Fenchel gap is equivalent to conjugate subgradient equality and an exact linear-minimization response; in the differentiable case it is equivalent to zero Frank-Wolfe gap.

\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of primal iterates, gradient-generated dual points, and certified optimality gaps from oracle outputs.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the primal and dual optimal values by \(p^\star=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) and \(d^\star=\sup_y\{-f^*(y)-\sigma_C(-y)\}\). Let a Frank-Wolfe iteration provide \(x_t\in C\), \(y_t=\nabla f(x_t)\), and \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle y_t,s\rangle\). Then \(x_t\) is primal feasible, \(y_t\) is feasible for the unconstrained Fenchel dual, and \[f(x_t)+f^*(y_t)+\sigma_C(-y_t)=\langle y_t,x_t-s_t\rangle=g_t.\] Thus the iterate-oracle pair yields primal and dual candidates together with a directly verifiable certificate. Under strong duality, if \(g_t\le\varepsilon\) for some \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then both the primal and dual objective errors are at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After explicitly defining the primal and dual optimal values, a Frank-Wolfe iterate, its gradient, and the oracle atom form primal and dual candidates whose objective difference is exactly the computable Frank-Wolfe gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and let \(F=f+h\), where \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable and \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\), assume that
\[
v(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}\bigl\{\langle\nabla f(x),z\rangle+h(z)\bigr\}.
\]
Define
\[
G_F(x):=F(x)-\inf_{z\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),z-x\rangle+h(z)\bigr\}
=\langle\nabla f(x),x-v(x)\rangle+h(x)-h(v(x)).
\]
Then \(G_F(x)\ge 0\), and for every minimizer \(x^\star\) of \(F\),
\[
0\le F(x)-F(x^\star)\le G_F(x).
\]
Thus \(G_F(x)\le\varepsilon\) is a computable certificate of \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality whenever the composite linear-minimization subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composite linearization gap is nonnegative and upper-bounds primal objective error, so a small gap certifies approximate optimality.

Define \(\widetilde G_F(x)=F(x)-m_x(\widetilde v)\). Then \[-\delta\le\widetilde G_F(x)\le G_F(x),\qquad F(x)-F^\star\le G_F(x)\le\widetilde G_F(x)+\delta.\] Therefore \(\widetilde G_F(x)+\delta\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Descent View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror descent for a support-function composite, in the form admitting a dual conditional-gradient interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset X^*\) be compact and convex, and minimize \(F(x)=h(x)+\sigma_C(x)\), where \(h\) is Legendre and \(\sigma_C(x)=\max_{y\in C}\langle x,y\rangle\). Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\) and steps \(\eta_k\in(0,1]\), choose
\[
y_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in C}\langle x_k,y\rangle
\]
and define \(x_{k+1}\) by
\[
\nabla h(x_{k+1})=(1-\eta_k)\nabla h(x_k)-\eta_k y_k.
\]
Equivalently, this is mirror descent with mirror map \(h\) and selected subgradient \(\nabla h(x_k)+y_k\in\partial F(x_k)\). Output the last iterate or a prescribed weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror descent on a support-function composite combines the current mirror coordinate with a maximizing support atom.

knowledge_statements.title: Signed Mirror-Coordinate Path Correspondence
Dual Conditional-Gradient View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact iterate correspondence for the support-function primal and its Fenchel dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem \(\min_x h(x)+\sigma_C(x)\), consider the dual minimization problem
\[
\min_{z\in C}q(z),\qquad q(z):=h^*(-z).
\]
Suppose \(z_k=-\nabla h(x_k)\in C\). Then \(x_k=\nabla h^*(-z_k)\) and
\[
\nabla q(z_k)=-x_k.
\]
Consequently, a conditional-gradient atom satisfies
\[
y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\langle\nabla q(z_k),y\rangle
=
\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in C}\langle x_k,y\rangle.
\]
The update \(z_{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)z_k+\eta_k y_k\) is therefore equivalent, under \(z_k=-\nabla h(x_k)\), to the mirror-coordinate update for the primal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional gradient on the conjugate dual generates exactly the support atoms used by primal mirror descent, with matching convex-combination updates.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X^*\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(h\) is Legendre and \(h^*\) is differentiable at every \(-z_k\).
\(z_0=-\nabla h(x_0)\in C\) and both methods use the same \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k=-\nabla h(x_k)\) is preserved, and the two methods select the same \(y_k\).

notation.meaning: Common dual atom and primal support subgradient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual objective, gradient identity, oracle correspondence, and preserved iterate relation are mathematically coherent and the duality content kind fits the leaf. However, no source is cited for the exact iterate-level mirror-descent/conditional-gradient correspondence, so the record requires an authoritative theorem or section locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Signed-Conjugate Subdifferential Chain Rule
Conjugate-Space Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-coordinate identification underlying mirror-descent and conditional-gradient equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be Legendre. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\) and \(z=-\nabla h(x)\), conjugacy gives
\[
x=\nabla h^*(-z),
\qquad
h(x)+h^*(-z)=\langle -z,x\rangle.
\]
If \(q(z)=h^*(-z)\), then
\[
\nabla q(z)=-\nabla h^*(-z)=-x.
\]
Hence minimizing the dual linearization \(y\mapsto\langle\nabla q(z),y\rangle\) over \(C\) is identical to maximizing \(y\mapsto\langle x,y\rangle\) over \(C\). This conjugate-coordinate identity converts a dual linear-minimization oracle into the support-subgradient selection required by the primal mirror step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Legendre conjugacy identifies primal mirror coordinates with negative dual variables and turns the dual linear oracle into primal support-subgradient selection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional.
\(h\) is proper, closed, and Legendre.
\(x\) and \(-z\) lie in the interiors of the corresponding conjugate domains.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the mirror potential.
Conjugate-space coordinate associated with the primal point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Legendre mirror function does not ensure that a dual conditional-gradient segment remains in the signed conjugate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h(x_1,x_2)=-\log x_1-\log x_2\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^2\). Then \[q(z):=h^*(-z)=-2-\log z_1-\log z_2,\qquad \operatorname{dom}q=\mathbb R_{++}^2.\] Set \(z_0=(1,1)\), \(y=(3,-1/10)\), and \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{z_0,y\}\). Since \(
abla q(z_0)=(-1,-1)\) and \(\langle
abla q(z_0),yangle=-29/10<-2=\langle
abla q(z_0),z_0angle\), the linear minimization oracle over \(C\) selects \(y\). The update \(z_+=(1-\eta)z_0+\eta y\) has second coordinate \(1-11\eta/10\), which is nonpositive for \(\eta\geq10/11\). Then \(q(z_+)\) is not finite and \(
abla q(z_+)\) is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for a Legendre mirror function, a valid dual linear-minimization atom can make a sufficiently long conditional-gradient update leave the signed conjugate domain.
assumptions_latex: h(x_1,x_2)=-\log x_1-\log x_2\text{ on }\mathbb R_{++}^2.
C=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(3,-1/10)\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of iterate equality when tied linear-oracle responses are not coupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(C=[-1,1]\), and \(q(z)=h^*(-z)=\tfrac12z^2\). At \(x_0=z_0=0\), both the primal support maximization and dual conditional-gradient linear minimization have response set \(C\). If the two implementations select \(y_0=1\) and \(\widetilde y_0=-1\), then for a common \(\eta_0\in(0,1]\) their next mirror coordinates are \(z_1=\eta_0\) and \(\widetilde z_1=-\eta_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tied oracle responses can make the two formulations follow different paths despite identical initialization and step sizes.
assumptions_latex: h(x)=\tfrac12x^2.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of iterate equality when corresponding formulations use different convex-combination parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(C=[-1,1]\), and \(q(z)=h^*(-z)=\tfrac12z^2\). Start from \(x_0=1\) and \(z_0=-1=-\nabla h(x_0)\). Both corresponding linear oracles select \(y_0=1\). \eta,\widetilde\eta\in(0,1].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: ReLU Potential Has No Global Conjugate-Gradient Bijection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Legendre obstruction to a single-valued signed conjugate-coordinate correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h(x)=\max\{0,x\}\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(h^*(u)=\delta_{[0,1]}(u)\), so \(q(z):=h^*(-z)=\delta_{[-1,0]}(z)\). The map \(
abla h\) is undefined at \(0\) and is constant on each of \(( -\infty,0)\) and \((0,\infty)\); moreover, \(q\) has no ordinary gradient at the boundary points \(-1\) and \(0\). Hence \(z=-
abla h(x)\) and \(x=
abla h^*(-z)\) do not define a global single-valued inverse correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ReLU potential is convex but non-Legendre: its gradient is noninjective or undefined, and its conjugate indicator has boundary points without an ordinary gradient.
assumptions_latex: h(x)=\max\{0,x\}\text{ on }\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No global single-valued conjugate-gradient bijection exists for }h.

knowledge_statements.title: ReLU Potential Has No Global Conjugate-Gradient Bijection
Equivalence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions whose loss makes the mirror and conditional-gradient correspondence set-valued or undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The iterate-level equivalence requires an invertible gradient correspondence \(z=-
abla h(x)\), matching exact support atoms, compatible initialization \(z_0=-
abla h(x_0)\in C\), and identical step sizes. If \(h\) is not Legendre, the correspondence can fail. For example, with \(h(x)=|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), one has \(h^*(z)=\delta_{[-1,1]}(z)\); thus \(
abla h\) is not injective and \(h^*\) is not differentiable on the boundary of its domain. The dual objective \(h^*(-z)\) then lacks the single-valued gradient required by ordinary conditional gradient, so no unique iterate correspondence follows without choosing generalized subgradients and compatible selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact equivalence fails without invertible Legendre coordinates, compatible initialization, matched steps, and matched oracle selections; a nonsmooth mirror potential gives a concrete obstruction.
assumptions_latex: The claimed equivalence is interpreted as equality of individual iterates, not merely equality of optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(h(x)=|x|\), the gradient-based mirror–conditional-gradient identification is not globally well-defined.

children.title: Column-Generation View
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of oracle atoms as newly generated optimization columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact fully corrective column generation over a finite atom set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be finite. In exact fully corrective column generation, a positive pricing gap implies that every exact pricing minimizer lies outside the current column set. Thus every nonterminal iteration adds a distinct column. Starting from nonempty \(S_0\subseteq A\), the method reaches a zero-gap globally optimal restricted-master solution after at most \(|A|-|S_0|\) column additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many atoms and exact solves, every nonterminal iteration adds a new column, giving termination after at most the number of initially missing columns.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite and \(S_0\subseteq A\) is nonempty.
The objective is convex and differentiable.
All restricted-master and pricing problems are solved exactly.

notation.meaning: Number of strict column-addition iterations before termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Column Termination Bound
Column-Generation View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully corrective conditional gradient expressed as restricted-master column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) for a compact atom set \(A\), and minimize a convex differentiable function \(f\) over \(C\). Initialize a finite nonempty set \(S_0\subset A\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master problem
\[
x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(S_k)}f(x),
\]
obtain a pricing column
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}\langle\nabla f(x_k),a\rangle,
\]
and compute \(g_k=\langle\nabla f(x_k),x_k-s_k\rangle\). If \(g_k\le\varepsilon\), output \(x_k\); otherwise set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{s_k\}\). The stopping test certifies \(f(x_k)-\min_C f\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation repeatedly solves a restricted convex master problem and adds the atom with minimum linearized cost until its pricing gap is small.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is compact and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
\(f\) is convex and differentiable on \(C\).
Restricted master problems and pricing problems attain their minima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm either adds \(s_k\) to the master or returns an \(x_k\) satisfying \(f(x_k)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of generated columns or atoms.
New column returned by the pricing oracle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted-master, pricing, and stopping steps form a coherent fully corrective column-generation algorithm, and algorithm is the correct content kind for this leaf. The gap certificate is also correctly stated under convexity, but the record has no source for the column-generation correspondence or stopping result.

children.title: Simplicial-Decomposition View
children.top_down_role: Interpretation through restricted optimization over discovered atoms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Carathéodory Compression of the Active Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-controlled representation of a simplicial-decomposition iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\). There exist \(T\subseteq S\), \(|T|\le n+1\), and weights \(\mu_a\ge0\), \(\sum_{a\in T}\mu_a=1\), such that \(x=\sum_{a\in T}\mu_aa\). Replacing only the stored representation by this compressed one preserves the iterate and objective value. By contrast, deleting \(S\setminus T\) from the domain of future full corrections can change subsequent restricted-master solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterate in n dimensions needs at most n+1 stored atoms, but compressing its representation is not equivalent to deleting columns from future optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite.
\(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Compressed support of the current representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory Compression of the Active Representation
Simplicial-Decomposition View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-simplex optimization with exact reoptimization over all discovered atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) and let \(S_k=\{a_1,\ldots,a_{m_k}\}\subset A\). Represent the iterate as \(x_k=\sum_{i=1}^{m_k}\lambda_i a_i\), where \(\lambda\) belongs to the probability simplex. Choose
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}\langle\nabla f(x_k),a\rangle,
\]
form \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{s_k\}\), and reoptimize
\[
\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda\ge0,\,\sum_i\lambda_i=1}
 f\!\left(\sum_{a_i\in S_{k+1}}\lambda_i a_i\right).
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=\sum_i\lambda_i^{k+1}a_i\); atoms receiving zero weight may be deleted. This is the fully corrective simplicial-decomposition form of conditional gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplicial decomposition discovers an atom by linear minimization and then reoptimizes all convex weights over the active simplex.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is compact and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
\(f\) is convex and differentiable on \(C\).
Each finite-dimensional active-simplex subproblem is solved exactly.

notation.meaning: Convex weights on the active atoms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-simplex reoptimization procedure is a valid fully corrective simplicial-decomposition form of conditional gradient, and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. An authoritative simplicial-decomposition source with a section, theorem, or page locator is missing.

children.title: Atom-Discovery Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Shared structural role of atom discovery across the two viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of exact restricted-master optimality for atom discovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_S\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)}f(x)\), where \(S\subset A\), and let \(s\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}\langle\nabla f(x_S),a\rangle\). If \(s\in S\), then \[\langle\nabla f(x_S),x_S-s\rangle=0.\] Hence the full Frank--Wolfe gap is zero and \(x_S\) is globally optimal over \(\operatorname{conv}(A)\). Equivalently, at a nonoptimal exact restricted-master solution every exact pricing minimizer lies outside \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an exact restricted-master solution, rediscovering an existing atom certifies zero global gap.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is compact and \(S\subset A\) is finite and nonempty.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable.
The restricted master and pricing problem are solved exactly.

notation.meaning: Exact minimizer over the current atom hull.
Exact minimum-linearization atom over the full atom set.

knowledge_statements.title: Existing-Atom Pricing Certificate
Atom-Discovery Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between conditional-gradient atoms and negative-reduced-cost columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x_k\in\operatorname{conv}(S_k)\), define the linearized reduced cost of an atom \(a\in A\) by
\[
r_k(a):=\langle\nabla f(x_k),a-x_k\rangle.
\]
A pricing oracle returns
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}r_k(a)
=
\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}\langle\nabla f(x_k),a\rangle,
\]
which is exactly the conditional-gradient linear-minimization oracle. Moreover,
\[
g_k:=\max_{a\in A}\langle\nabla f(x_k),x_k-a\rangle=-r_k(s_k).
\]
Thus \(r_k(s_k)<0\) identifies an improving column for the linearized master, while \(r_k(s_k)\ge0\) implies \(g_k=0\) and first-order optimality over \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frank-Wolfe atom is precisely the minimum-reduced-cost column, and the negative reduced cost equals the Frank-Wolfe gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) with \(A\) compact.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable at \(x_k\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\) is both the pricing column and conditional-gradient atom, with \(g_k=-r_k(s_k)\).

notation.meaning: Linearized reduced cost of atom a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost minimizer is exactly the conditional-gradient atom, and the identity \(g_k=-r_k(s_k)\) is correct. The property content kind fits the correspondence leaf, but no citation supports the pricing interpretation and gap identification.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Dual View

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Refinement of the Dual Support Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering and pointwise exactness of finite support-function models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite active sets \(S\subseteq T\subseteq A\), \[\sigma_S(p)\le\sigma_T(p)\le\sigma_A(p)\qquad(\forall p).\] Hence, with \(D_U(p)=-f^*(-p)-\sigma_U(p)\), \[D_S(p)\ge D_T(p)\ge D_A(p).\] If \(a^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in A}\langle p,a\rangle\), then \(\sigma_{S\cup\{a^+\}}(p)=\sigma_A(p)\): the added affine piece makes the support model exact at the queried point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding atoms raises the finite support model and lowers its relaxed dual objective; an oracle atom makes the model exact at the current query.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq T\subseteq A\).
The displayed conjugate and support values are finite at the queried point.

notation.meaning: Dual objective using support model generated by U.
Support-maximizing atom at the queried dual point.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Refinement of the Dual Support Model
Cutting-Plane Dual View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generated primal atoms become affine cutting pieces of the dual support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) and consider \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\). Under Fenchel duality its dual can be written
\[
\sup_p\{-f^*(-p)-\sigma_C(p)\},
\qquad
\sigma_C(p)=\max_{a\in A}\langle p,a\rangle.
\]
For a finite active set \(S\subset A\), replacing \(\sigma_C\) by \(\sigma_S(p)=\max_{a\in S}\langle p,a\rangle\) yields a restricted piecewise-affine model. Given a dual trial point \(p\), an atom
\[
a^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in A}\langle p,a\rangle
\]
adds the missing affine piece \(p\mapsto\langle p,a^+\rangle\). When \(p=-\nabla f(x)\), this atom is exactly a conditional-gradient minimizer of \(a\mapsto\langle\nabla f(x),a\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a primal atom is dual to adding an affine support-function cut; at matched primal-dual points both procedures use the same oracle.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is compact and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and Fenchel strong duality holds.
At matched points, \(f\) is differentiable and \(p=-\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Atom generation for the primal restricted master equals cutting-plane refinement of the dual support-function model.

notation.meaning: Support function of the full feasible hull.
Finite cutting-plane approximation formed from active atoms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Fenchel-dual support-function formulation and the equality between atom generation and adding an affine support piece are coherent under the stated strong-duality assumptions. Duality fits the terminal container, but the record lacks an authoritative source for this cutting-plane correspondence.

children.title: Primal Objective Rate Family

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Objective Rate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical curvature-based sublinear rate for exact Frank-Wolfe steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and differentiable on a compact convex set \(C\), with finite curvature constant \(C_f\). Starting from \(x_0\in C\), choose
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_k),s\rangle,
\qquad
x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{2}{k+2}(s_k-x_k).
\]
If \(f^*=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\), then for every \(k\ge1\),
\[
f(x_k)-f^*\le\frac{2C_f}{k+2}.
\]
The same order holds for exact line search. Consequently, achieving primal objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) requires \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\) exact conditional-gradient iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Frank-Wolfe achieves objective error proportional to the curvature constant divided by the iteration count.

children.title: Frank-Wolfe Gap Rate Family
children.top_down_role: Complexity for computable gap certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Frank-Wolfe Gap Rate Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate gap rate obtained by a standard descent phase followed by constant steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g_t=\max_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s\rangle\). Suppose an initial Frank-Wolfe phase produces \(x_m\) with \(f(x_m)-f^*\le2C_f/(m+2)\). Perform \(n\ge1\) further exact Frank-Wolfe updates with a constant step \(\gamma\in(0,1]\). Then
\[
\min_{m\le t<m+n}g_t
\le
\frac{2C_f}{(m+2)n\gamma}+\frac{\gamma C_f}{2}.
\]
Choosing \(\gamma=2/(n+2)\) and balanced phase lengths \(m\asymp n\asymp K/2\) gives
\[
\min_{0\le t<K}g_t=O(C_f/K).
\]
Hence an iterate with computable gap at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtainable in \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\) exact iterations under this schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-phase Frank-Wolfe schedule yields a best-iterate computable gap of order curvature divided by total iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable with finite curvature \(C_f\) on compact convex \(C\).
The first phase satisfies the stated primal-error bound.
All linear-minimization oracle calls are exact.

notation.meaning: Lengths of the primal-rate and constant-step phases.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-phase descent summation and resulting best-iterate \(O(C_f/K)\) gap rate are internally consistent, and complexity_bound fits the gap-rate leaf. Because the record asserts a particular finite-phase inequality and schedule without any citation, an authoritative locator supporting the constants and schedule is required.

assumptions_latex: The additive LMO is allowed to return \(s_k=\bar\delta\) at every iteration.
\(0<\gamma_k<1\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k=\infty\), and \(x_0\in[\bar\delta,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of exact convergence under a persistent additive linear-minimization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=[0,1]\) and \(f(x)=x\), the exact linear minimum is \(0\). An additive oracle with tolerance \(\bar\delta\in(0,1]\) may validly return \(s_k=\bar\delta\) because \(\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\rangle=\bar\delta\le\min_{s\in C}s+\bar\delta\). The update \(x_{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)x_k+\gamma_k\bar\delta\), with \(0<\gamma_k<1\), \(\sum_k\gamma_k=\infty\), and \(x_0\ge\bar\delta\), satisfies \(x_k\to\bar\delta\). Hence the objective error converges to \(\bar\delta\), not to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid fixed-error linear oracle can make Frank-Wolfe converge to a point whose objective error equals the oracle tolerance.

Approximate-Oracle Rate Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively inexact linear minimization for curvature-based Frank–Wolfe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be compact and convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable with curvature at most \(C_f\), and set \(h_k=f(x_k)-f^*\). Suppose \(s_k\in C\) satisfies \(\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\rangle\le \min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_k),s\rangle+\delta_k\), and \(x_{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)x_k+\gamma_k s_k\). Then \[h_{k+1}\le(1-\gamma_k)h_k+\gamma_k\delta_k+\frac{C_f}{2}\gamma_k^2.\] Consequently, with \(\gamma_k=2/(k+2)\) and \(\delta_k=O((k+2)^{-1})\), one has \(h_k=O(k^{-1})\). Thus controlled additive oracle errors preserve the classical order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual inverse-iteration objective rate survives when each linear-oracle error decays inversely with the iteration count.

assumptions_latex: \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing\). The objective has power sharpness of order \(r>0\) with constant \(\mu>0\) on \(S\subseteq C\) if \(f(x)-f^*\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^r\) for every \(x\in S\). The case \(r=1\) is weak sharpness. If \(S=C\), the condition is global; if \(S\) is only a neighborhood or level-set slice, it supports only a local or eventual rate unless entry into and invariance of \(S\) are separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power sharpness lower-bounds objective error by a power of distance to the solution set; local sharpness supports only local or eventual conclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=f(x)-f^*\), and let \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_{*,\operatorname{aff}(C)}\) denote the dual norm of the gradient restricted to directions parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\). For \(r>2\), after entry at iteration \(k_0\), \[h_k\leq\left(h_{k_0}^{-(r-2)/r}+a\frac{r-2}{r}(k-k_0)\right)^{-r/(r-2)}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\times[-1,1]\) and \(f(u,v)=u+\tfrac12v^2\). Then \(X^*=\{(0,0)\}\), \(f^*=0\), and \[f(u,v)\geq\tfrac12(u^2+v^2)=\tfrac12\operatorname{dist}((u,v),X^*)^2.\] For \(x_\tau=(\tau,0)\), \(0<\tau\leq1\), \[g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x_\tau)=\tau=f(x_\tau)-f^*,\qquad \frac{g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x_\tau)}{\sqrt{f(x_\tau)-f^*}}=\sqrt\tau\to0.\] Thus global quadratic sharpness alone gives no uniform square-root Frank-Wolfe-gap bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_k=f(x_k)-f^*\ge0\) be the primal error of a conditional-gradient sequence. Suppose a sharpness condition and the method's descent estimate imply, whenever \(h_k>0\), \[h_{k+1}\le h_k-a h_k^p\] for constants \(a>0\) and \(p\ge1\), with \(a h_k^{p-1}\le1\). If \(p=1\), then \(h_k\le(1-a)^k h_0\). If \(p>1\), then \[h_k\le\left(h_0^{1-p}+a(p-1)k\right)^{-1/(p-1)}.\] Thus the exponent produced by sharpness determines whether convergence is geometric or polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once sharpness yields a power decrease recurrence, exponent one gives geometric convergence and larger exponents give an explicit polynomial rate.

It does not create smoothness, compactness, neighborhood invariance, oracle accuracy, a Frank-Wolfe descent inequality, or a stepsize hypothesis required by a particular convergence theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Equivalence Does Not Automatically Transfer Rate Theorems
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Equivalence Does Not Automatically Transfer Rate Theorems
Growth-Regime Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between power growth and Hölder error-bound formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\), and fix \(r>0\) and \(\mu>0\). On any set \(S\subset C\), the power-growth condition \[f(x)-f^*\ge\mu\,\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^r\quad(x\in S)\] is equivalent to the Hölder error bound \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\mu^{-1/r}(f(x)-f^*)^{1/r}\quad(x\in S).\] Therefore larger growth near \(X^*\) means a smaller distance at a fixed objective error; any conditional-gradient rate theorem expressed using one formulation can be translated into the other by setting the error-bound exponent to \(1/r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power growth of order r and a Hölder error bound of exponent one over r are the same local condition written in opposite directions.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of minimizers over the feasible region
region on which the growth condition is asserted

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic equivalence on S is correct and representation is the right kind, but there is no citation. Moreover, translating an entire conditional-gradient rate theorem can require additional hypotheses beyond substituting the error-bound exponent 1/r.
