children.title: Linear-Oracle Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Complexity limitations for linear-minimization-based feasible-set access.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-model boundary for transferring atom-revelation lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support-growth lower bound applies when the algorithm's output must lie in the convex hull of vertices revealed by its linear-oracle calls. It does not by itself lower-bound a model that may construct arbitrary feasible points: for \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\) on \(\Delta_n\), such a model may output the known uniform minimizer \(\mathbf1/n\) without revealing its vertices individually. Transfer to a stronger model therefore requires an independent information restriction or simulation argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A revealed-atom lower bound does not transfer to arbitrary feasible-output models without another information restriction.
assumptions_latex: The seed model restricts outputs to convex combinations of oracle-revealed vertices.
The comparison model permits arbitrary feasible outputs obtained by other means.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The revealed-atom \Omega(1/\varepsilon) argument does not alone lower-bound stronger feasible-output models.
knowledge_statements.title: Revealed-Atom Model Boundary
Linear-Oracle Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case oracle-call lower bound in an atom-generating linear-minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider algorithms over \(\Delta_n\) that start from one vertex and, at each iteration, obtain at most one new vertex from a linear minimization oracle and return a point in the convex hull of all obtained vertices. For \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), the minimizer is \(x^*=\mathbf1/n\). After \(k\) oracle calls the output has support at most \(k+1\), so \[f(x_k)-f(x^*)\ge\frac{1}{2(k+1)}-\frac{1}{2n}.\] In dimensions \(n\ge2(k+1)\), this is at least \(1/(4(k+1))\); hence attaining error \(\varepsilon\) requires \(\Omega(1/\varepsilon)\) linear-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the atom-generating oracle model, a simplex quadratic forces at least order one over epsilon linear-minimization calls.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is the simplex \(\Delta_n\).
Each oracle call reveals at most one new vertex, and outputs use only revealed vertices.
The objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)-f^*\ge 1/(2(k+1))-1/(2n)\), implying \(\Omega(1/\varepsilon)\) oracle calls in sufficiently large dimension.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex calculation is plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits, but the restricted atom-generating oracle model and resulting oracle lower bound need a canonical source with a precise model statement and locator.

children.title: Sparse-Iterate Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Accuracy barriers for representations using few atoms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact simplex-quadratic value under an atomic support budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(1\le s\le n\),
\[\min_{\substack{x\in\Delta_n\\|\operatorname{supp}(x)|\le s}}\left(\frac12\|x\|_2^2-\frac1{2n}\right)=\frac1{2s}-\frac1{2n}.\]
Equality is attained by assigning weight \(1/s\) to every element of an \(s\)-element support, and every minimizer under the support budget has this form up to its support choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best s-atom simplex point is uniform on s vertices and has exact error \(1/(2s)-1/(2n)\).
assumptions_latex: \(1\le s\le n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Sparse-Simplex Approximation
Sparse-Iterate Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-accuracy obstruction for simplex points supported on few atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\Delta_n\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\). The unique minimizer is \(x^*=\mathbf1/n\), with \(f(x^*)=1/(2n)\). Every \(s\)-sparse point \(x\in\Delta_n\) satisfies \(\|x\|_2^2\ge1/s\), and therefore \[f(x)-f(x^*)\ge\frac{1}{2s}-\frac{1}{2n}.\] In particular, if \(n\ge2s\), every such representation has error at least \(1/(4s)\). Thus uniform accuracy \(f(x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\) requires \(s=\Omega(1/\varepsilon)\) atoms in sufficiently large dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex quadratic cannot be approximated to error epsilon by fewer than order one over epsilon active atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\Delta_n\) has at most \(s\) nonzero coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*\ge1/(2s)-1/(2n)\), and hence \(s=\Omega(1/\varepsilon)\) when \(n\) is sufficiently large.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse-simplex inequality is mathematically standard and matches the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports its use as the intended sparse-iterate lower-bound record.

children.title: Toward-Only Rate Barriers
children.top_down_role: Limits of the classical direction family near unfavorable boundary solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Toward-Only Rate Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-iteration barrier for updates that only move toward one newly selected atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Delta_n\), consider toward-only updates \(x_{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)x_k+\gamma_k v_k\), where \(v_k\) is a simplex vertex and \(0\le\gamma_k\le1\). Starting from a vertex, \(x_k\) has support at most \(k+1\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), whose minimizer is \(\mathbf1/n\), this implies \[f(x_k)-f^*\ge\frac{1}{2(k+1)}-\frac{1}{2n}.\] Hence, when \(n\ge2(k+1)\), no choice of toward vertices or step sizes can guarantee a rate asymptotically better than order \(1/k\) on this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because each toward-only step adds at most one atom, a simplex quadratic prevents any worst-case rate better than inverse iteration.
assumptions_latex: The method starts at a simplex vertex.
Every update moves toward a single simplex vertex without away or corrective steps.
The objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\).

notation.meaning: vertex selected for the toward step
minimum objective value on the simplex

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is appropriate and the support-growth argument is plausible, but the claimed worst-case toward-only barrier lacks a source defining the method class and quantifiers precisely.

children.title: Linear-Oracle Evaluation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Upper-bound regimes organized by the number of linear-oracle evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity with Decaying Additive LMO Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LMO evaluation complexity with inverse-linearly decaying additive oracle error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An additive-inexact Frank-Wolfe step obeys \[h_{k+1}\leq(1-\gamma_k)h_k+\gamma_k\delta_k+\frac{C_f}{2}\gamma_k^2.\] If \(\gamma_k=2/(k+2)\) and \(\delta_k\leq E/(k+2)\), then \[h_k=O((C_f+E)/k),\qquad N_{\mathrm{LMO}}(\varepsilon)=O((C_f+E)/\varepsilon).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive LMO errors decaying inversely with iteration preserve inverse-linear objective decay and inverse-accuracy LMO complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex with curvature at most \(C_f\) on compact convex \(C\).
The k-th LMO has additive error \(\delta_k\leq E/(k+2)\).
The update uses \(\gamma_k=2/(k+2)\) under a consistent indexing convention.

notation.meaning: Additive error of the k-th LMO call.

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity with Decaying Additive LMO Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical LMO evaluation bound derived from the smooth convex Frank-Wolfe rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex with Frank-Wolfe curvature at most \(C_f\) on compact convex \(C\). For the classical exact-LMO Frank-Wolfe method with the standard reciprocal stepsize convention, \[f(x_k)-f^*\leq\frac{2C_f}{k+2}\] after the initial full-step convention. Because each iteration makes one LMO call, \[N_{\mathrm{LMO}}(\varepsilon)=O(C_f/\varepsilon).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical smooth convex Frank-Wolfe needs order curvature divided by accuracy exact LMO calls for primal objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable with curvature at most \(C_f\).
Each iteration makes one exact LMO call.
The standard reciprocal stepsize and initial full-step indexing are used.

notation.meaning: LMO calls sufficient for objective error at most epsilon.

review_flags: The asymptotic call bound is invariant to the stated indexing convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-LMO Objective-Accuracy Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource convention for conditional-gradient LMO evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact LMO evaluation receives a linear functional \(d\) and returns \(s\in\arg\min_{z\in C}\langle d,z\rangle\). An additive-\(\delta\) evaluation may return \(s\in C\) satisfying \[\langle d,s\rangle\leq\min_{z\in C}\langle d,z\rangle+\delta.\] The count \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) charges each invocation once and excludes gradient calls, function evaluations, and internal arithmetic unless those resources are separately declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LMO complexity counts exact or approximate linear-minimization invocations separately from gradients, function values, and internal solver work.
assumptions_latex: A primitive linear-minimization oracle for \(C\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Minimization-Oracle Call Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of LMO complexity from line-search evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each of \(T\) outer iterations makes exactly one LMO call, then \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}=T\). This identity gives no bound on the number \(N_f\) of objective evaluations used by exact or approximate line search unless a line-search oracle and termination rule are separately specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One LMO call per iteration equates LMO and iteration counts but does not price line-search function evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Each outer iteration makes one LMO call.
The implementation cost of line search is not specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Evaluations Are Separately Charged
Linear-Oracle Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact-oracle complexity for smooth convex Frank–Wolfe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be compact and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable with Frank–Wolfe curvature at most \(C_f\). Run exact-oracle Frank–Wolfe with \(\gamma_k=2/(k+2)\), interpreting the first step as a full step. Then, for \(k\ge1\), \[f(x_k)-f^*\le\frac{2C_f}{k+2}.\] Each iteration uses one linear-minimization-oracle evaluation and one gradient evaluation. Consequently, at most \(\lceil2C_f/\varepsilon\rceil\) iterations, up to indexing constants, suffice to obtain primal error at most \(\varepsilon>0\); the linear-oracle evaluation complexity is \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth convex Frank–Wolfe needs order curvature divided by epsilon exact linear-oracle evaluations for epsilon primal accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex.
\(f\) is convex, differentiable, and has curvature at most \(C_f\).
Each iteration calls an exact linear minimization oracle once.

notation.meaning: number of linear-oracle evaluations required for epsilon primal accuracy
minimum objective value over the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind matches the evaluation-complexity leaf, but the exact 2C_f/(k+2) guarantee, first-step convention, and derived call count require a Frank–Wolfe theorem citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Certificate Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity guarantees organized around computable accuracy or stationarity certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified stopping with an additive-accuracy linear oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(s_\delta\in C\) satisfies
\[\langle\nabla f(x),s_\delta\rangle\le\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle+\delta.\]
For \(\widehat g_\delta(x)=\langle\nabla f(x),x-s_\delta\rangle\),
\[\widehat g_\delta(x)\le g(x)\le\widehat g_\delta(x)+\delta.\]
Consequently, for convex \(f\), \(\widehat g_\delta(x)+\delta\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the known linear-oracle error to the computed approximate gap gives a valid convex optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex.
The linear oracle satisfies the stated additive-error condition.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable at x.

notation.meaning: Point returned by the additive-error linear oracle.
Gap computed using the approximate oracle point.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Oracle Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frank–Wolfe gap complexity for a fully specified finite-horizon fixed-step iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_k),s\rangle\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\gamma(s_k-x_k)\) for \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\), with one fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1]\). If the Frank–Wolfe curvature is at most \(C_f\), then
\[\min_{0\le k<K}g(x_k)\le \frac{h_0}{K\gamma}+\frac{\gamma C_f}{2}.\]
For \(0<\varepsilon\le C_f\), choosing \(\gamma=\varepsilon/C_f\) and \(K\ge2C_fh_0/\varepsilon^2\) yields \(\min_{k<K}g(x_k)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specified fixed-step Frank–Wolfe run attains an epsilon gap in order \(C_fh_0/\varepsilon^2\) iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable on C with curvature at most \(C_f\).
Each iteration uses an exact linear minimization oracle.
The fixed step and horizon are chosen as stated.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Fixed-Step Gap Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between Frank–Wolfe stationarity and global optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable \(f\), \(g(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(\langle\nabla f(x),s-x\rangle\ge0\) for every \(s\in C\), hence to first-order stationarity. Convexity makes this sufficient for global optimality, but without convexity it need not be. For example, on \(C=[-2,2]\), \(f(t)=(t^2-1)^2+t/10\) has a strict local minimizer in \((0,2)\) with \(g=0\), while values near the negative well are smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero Frank–Wolfe gap characterizes first-order stationarity but need not certify global optimality without convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x)=0\text{ characterizes first-order stationarity; global optimality additionally requires convexity or another sufficient condition}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Optimality Boundary
Certificate Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of primal-error and Frank–Wolfe-gap stopping certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\max_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x),x-s\rangle\) be the Frank–Wolfe gap for convex differentiable \(f\). Then \(f(x)-f^*\le g(x)\), so \(g(x)\le\varepsilon\) is a verifiable \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate obtained from one exact linear-oracle call. Under curvature bound \(C_f\), the classical primal guarantee requires \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\) iterations. Independently, the descent inequality with a constant step chosen over a horizon \(K\) gives \[\min_{0\le k<K}g(x_k)=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{C_f h_0}{K}}+\frac{C_f}{K}\right),\] yielding a general gap-certificate complexity \(O(C_f h_0/\varepsilon^2+C_f/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal accuracy has the classical inverse-epsilon rate, while a directly verified gap certificate admits a general inverse-epsilon-squared complexity bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and convex, and \(f\) is convex and differentiable.
The Frank–Wolfe curvature is at most \(C_f\).
The linear minimization oracle is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(x)\le g(x)\); primal accuracy costs \(O(C_f/\varepsilon)\), while the stated generic gap regime costs \(O(C_fh_0/\varepsilon^2+C_f/\varepsilon)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gap certificate inequality is standard, but the horizon-dependent constant-step gap bound and its O(epsilon^{-2}) complexity depend on an algorithm and step-size schedule that are not fully specified or sourced.

children.title: Standard Away-Step Frank-Wolfe
children.top_down_role: The classical toward-or-away active-set method.

assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a a\) is an active representation.
\(s\in\arg\min_{u\in V}\langle g,u\rangle\) and \(v\in\arg\max_{a\in S}\langle g,a\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gain identity underlying the classical direction comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The gains satisfy \(g_{\mathrm P}=g_{\mathrm{FW}}+g_{\mathrm A}\). Both summands are nonnegative, so \(\max\{g_{\mathrm{FW}},g_{\mathrm A}\}\geq\tfrac12g_{\mathrm P}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pairwise gap is the sum of the toward and away gains, so the better classical direction captures at least half of it.
knowledge_statements.title: Toward-Away Gain Decomposition
Standard Away-Step Frank-Wolfe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set away-step method for smooth minimization over a compact polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an active representation \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_a^t a\), compute \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle 
abla f(x_t),sangle\) and \(v_t\in\arg\max_{v\in S_t}\langle 
abla f(x_t),vangle\). Define \(d_t^{\mathrm{FW}}=s_t-x_t\) and \(d_t^{\mathrm A}=x_t-v_t\). Choose the direction giving the larger predicted decrease: \(d_t=d_t^{\mathrm{FW}}\) if \(\langle-
abla f(x_t),d_t^{\mathrm{FW}}angle\geq\langle-
abla f(x_t),d_t^{\mathrm A}angle\), and otherwise choose \(d_t=d_t^{\mathrm A}\). Set \(\gamma_{\max}=1\) for a toward step and \(\gamma_{\max}=\alpha_{v_t}^t/(1-\alpha_{v_t}^t)\) for an away step. children.title: Decomposition-Invariant Away-Step Methods

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two supports select different away atoms and therefore different away directions, although \((C,x,g)\) is unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Dependence Counterexample

assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polytope and \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linear optimization over the vertices of \(F_C(x)\) is determined by \((C,x)\), independently of a convex decomposition of \(x\).

Vertex set of the face F.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic vertex representation of the current minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every face of a polytope is generated by the ambient vertices it contains, so \(F_C(x)=\operatorname{conv}(V\cap F_C(x))\) and \(V(F_C(x))=V\cap F_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current minimal face is generated exactly by its ambient vertices, so a face-based linear oracle is decomposition independent.

Decomposition-Invariant Away-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-face away steps requiring no maintained convex decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_t\in C\), let \(F_t=F_C(x_t)\) be its minimal face. Compute \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle
abla f(x_t),sangle\) and a face-away atom \(v_t\in\arg\max_{v\in V\cap F_t}\langle
abla f(x_t),vangle\). Compare \(d_t^{\mathrm{FW}}=s_t-x_t\) with \(d_t^{\mathrm A}=x_t-v_t\) by their inner products with \(-
abla f(x_t)\), and select the better direction. Let \(\gamma_{\max}=1\) for the toward direction and \(\gamma_{\max}=\sup\{\gamma\geq0:x_t+\gamma d_t^{\mathrm A}\in C\}\) for the away direction. Choose an admissible line-search step and set \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\). All oracle choices depend only on \(x_t\), \(C\), and \(
abla f(x_t)\), not on a decomposition of \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select away atoms from the current minimal face and determine feasibility geometrically, so the iteration does not depend on a stored convex decomposition.

\(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and optimization over \(V\cap F_C(x)\) is available.

Vertices belonging to the current minimal face.

children.title: In-Face Directions

assumptions_latex: The in-face direction-space representation holds.
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), and \(P_{L_F}\) is Euclidean orthogonal projection onto \(L_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_F\) is strict descent exactly when \(P_{L_F}\nabla f(x)\neq0\); otherwise \(x\) is first-order stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(F\).

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polytope, \(x\in C\), and \(F=F_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector admits a nontrivial two-sided segment in \(F\) through \(x\) exactly when it belongs to \(L_F\).

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of F.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-space representation of in-face directions at a minimal-face relative-interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\), for every \(d\in L_F\) there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(x+\tau d\in F\) for all \(|\tau|\leq\varepsilon\). Conversely, every direction admitting such a segment belongs to \(L_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a relative-interior point of its minimal face, the in-face directions are exactly the vectors parallel to that face.
knowledge_statements.title: In-Face Direction Space
In-Face Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible directions constrained to the current minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(x\in C\), let \(F_C(x)\) denote the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x\). A vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is an in-face direction at \(x\) if \(d\neq0\) and there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(x+\tau d\in F_C(x)\) for every \(\tau\in[0,\varepsilon]\). Equivalently, \(d\) belongs to the tangent cone \(T_{F_C(x)}(x)\) and admits a nontrivial feasible forward step. For differentiable minimization, an in-face descent direction additionally satisfies \(\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An in-face direction permits a positive feasible step that remains inside the minimal face containing the current point; it is descending when its gradient pairing is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) is in-face at \(x\) exactly when a nontrivial forward segment from \(x\) along \(d\) lies in \(F_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Minimal face of C containing x.
Tangent cone to F at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf. A source is required for the stated minimal-face definition and especially the tangent-cone equivalence under the given general closed-convex-set assumptions.

children.title: Away Directions
children.top_down_role: Directions reducing weight on selected active atoms.

assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a a\) with \(\alpha_a>0\) and \(\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a=1\).
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), and \(v\in\arg\max_{a\in S}\langle\nabla f(x),a\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(x;d^{\mathrm A})\leq0\), with strict inequality exactly when \(\langle\nabla f(x),v\rangle>\langle\nabla f(x),x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization of an active-support away direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d^{\mathrm A}=x-v\), \(f'(x;d^{\mathrm A})=\langle\nabla f(x),x-v\rangle\leq0\). Equality holds exactly when the selected atom and the active-set average have the same linearization value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst active atom gives a nonascent away direction, with strict descent exactly when it is worse than the active-set average.
knowledge_statements.title: Away-Direction Descent Identity
Away Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directions that reduce the contribution of an active or face atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(x=\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a a\) with \(\alpha_a>0\), and let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x\). An active-set away atom is any \(v\in\arg\max_{a\in S}\langle\nabla f(x),a\rangle\), and its away direction is \(d^{\mathrm A}=x-v\). The maximal coefficient-preserving step is \(\gamma_{m A}=\alpha_v/(1-\alpha_v)\) when \(\alpha_v<1\); for \(\alpha_v=1\), no nonzero away step exists. A face-based away direction uses \(v\in\arg\max_{a\in V\cap F_C(x)}\langle\nabla f(x),a\rangle\) and its maximal step is determined directly by feasibility in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An away direction points from a selected worst active or same-face atom toward the current point, thereby decreasing that atom’s contribution until feasibility becomes tight.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is a compact polytope, \(x\in C\), and \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the active-set form, \(x+\gamma d^{\mathrm A}\in C\) for every \(0\leq\gamma\leq\gamma_{m A}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the record combines decomposition-dependent and face-based away directions. An authoritative locator is needed to confirm both conventions and their maximal-step formulations.

children.title: Face-Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases governing retention, contraction, or departure from the current face.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex set, \(x,y\in C\), and \(0<\lambda<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y)\) is constant for \(0<\lambda<1\) and is the least face containing both endpoint minimal faces.

notation.meaning: Minimal face containing the set E.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-face behavior on a feasible segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(1-\lambda)x+\lambda y\), \(F_C(z)=F_C(\{x,y\})\). Hence if \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\) and \(y\in F\), each open-segment point has minimal face \(F\); if \(y\notin F\), it has a minimal face strictly containing \(F\). The endpoint \(y\in\operatorname{rbd}F\) may have a proper subface as its minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An open-segment point lies in the least face containing both endpoints; only an endpoint can collapse to a smaller face.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Face of an Open Segment
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Face of an Open Segment
Face-Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by whether an update preserves, enters, or leaves the current face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\), where \(F=F_C(x)\), and let \(d\) be feasible with \(\gamma_{m face}=\sup\{\gamma\geq0:x+\tau d\in F\text{ for all }\tau\in[0,\gamma]\}\). If \(0<\gamma<\gamma_{m face}\), then \(x+\gamma d\in\operatorname{relint}F\), so the minimal face is preserved. If \(\gamma=\gamma_{m face}<\infty\) and the endpoint remains in \(F\), then it lies on \(\operatorname{rbd}F\) and its minimal face is a proper subface of \(F\). If a feasible direction points outside \(F\), every sufficiently small positive step has a minimal face strictly containing \(F\). These are respectively face-preserving, face-dropping, and face-expanding transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step may remain in the relative interior of the current face, reach a proper subface at an endpoint, or move into a strictly larger face.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polytope, \(x\in C\), and \(F=F_C(x)\).
\(d\) admits a nonzero feasible forward step in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The new minimal face is respectively \(F\), a proper subface of \(F\), or a strict superface of \(F\) in the three stated regimes.

notation.meaning: Endpoint of the forward segment remaining in F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the terminal container, but the three-regime classification and its universal claims about endpoint and small-step minimal faces require a precise polyhedral-face source.

children.title: Pairwise Exchange Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Methods transferring weight directly between active and incoming atoms.

children.title: Pairwise Frank-Wolfe
children.top_down_role: The basic atom-exchange conditional-gradient family.

assumptions_latex: x=\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a a with \alpha_a\geq0 and \sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a=1.
s\in\arg\min_{a\in V}\langle g,a\rangle.
v\in\arg\max_{a\in S}\langle g,a\rangle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of the pairwise exchange gap with the ordinary Frank-Wolfe gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x=\sum_{a\in S}\alpha_a a be an active convex representation, let s minimize \langle g,a\rangle over V, and let v maximize \langle g,a\rangle over S. Define g^{\mathrm{PFW}}=\langle g,v-s\rangle and g^{\mathrm{FW}}=\langle g,x-s\rangle. Then g^{\mathrm{PFW}}\geq g^{\mathrm{FW}}\geq0. Consequently, g^{\mathrm{PFW}}=0 implies g^{\mathrm{FW}}=0 and, for convex differentiable f with g=\nabla f(x), certifies optimality of x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pairwise exchange gap dominates the ordinary Frank-Wolfe gap, so a zero pairwise gap certifies optimality in the convex differentiable setting.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Gap Domination
Pairwise Frank-Wolfe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set atom exchange using one global toward atom and one active away atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_a^t a\), compute \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\) and \(v_t\in\arg\max_{v\in S_t}\langle\nabla f(x_t),v\rangle\). Set the pairwise direction \(d_t=s_t-v_t\) and choose \(\gamma_t\in\arg\min_{0\leq\gamma\leq\alpha_{v_t}^t}f(x_t+\gamma d_t)\), or use another descent-valid step in this interval. Update \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\), \(\alpha_{v_t}^{t+1}=\alpha_{v_t}^t-\gamma_t\), and \(\alpha_{s_t}^{t+1}=\alpha_{s_t}^t+\gamma_t\), interpreting a previously inactive \(s_t\) as having coefficient zero. Leave all other coefficients unchanged and delete any zero-weight atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer weight directly from the active atom least aligned with descent to a globally selected Frank-Wolfe atom, without moving through the current point.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact polytope with finite \(V\).
\(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and a finite active representation of \(x_0\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in C\), because the update transfers exactly \(\gamma_t\) units of convex weight from \(v_t\) to \(s_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and weight-transfer update match Pairwise Frank-Wolfe, but no cited source verifies the oracle rules, feasible interval, or allowance for an unspecified alternative descent-valid step.

children.title: Swap-Step Methods
children.top_down_role: Exchange variants organized around replacement of active atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Swap-Step Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise exchange methods emphasizing complete replacement of an active atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_a^t a\). Select an entering atom \(s_t\in V\) and a leaving atom \(v_t\in S_t\), commonly by the pairwise Frank-Wolfe oracle rules, and set \(d_t=s_t-v_t\). Choose \(0\leq\gamma_t\leq\alpha_{v_t}^t\) and update \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\). The iteration is a swap step when \(\gamma_t=\alpha_{v_t}^t\): all weight of \(v_t\) is transferred to \(s_t\), so \(v_t\) leaves the active set unless \(s_t=v_t\). If \(0<\gamma_t<\alpha_{v_t}^t\), the iteration is a partial swap. A line search or prescribed descent rule determines \(\gamma_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A swap step transfers all weight of one active atom to an entering atom; a partial swap transfers only part of that weight.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is a compact polytope, and \(x_t\) has an active convex representation.
\(s_t\in V\), \(v_t\in S_t\), and the chosen step satisfies \(0\leq\gamma_t\leq\alpha_{v_t}^t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every swap or partial-swap update is feasible, and a full swap removes \(v_t\) whenever its resulting coefficient is zero.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the swap-step terminal, but the record mostly classifies full versus partial pairwise transfers and leaves the method's atom-selection and step rule variant-dependent. A specific source is required.

children.title: Blended Pairwise Conditional Gradients
children.top_down_role: Methods combining local pairwise improvements with global oracle calls.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Blended Conditional Gradients
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Blended Conditional Gradients

knowledge_statements.title: Blended Pairwise Conditional Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation between inexpensive active-set exchanges and global linear-oracle steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_a^t a\), compute active atoms \(a_t^-\in\arg\min_{a\in S_t}\langle
abla f(x_t),aangle\) and \(a_t^+\in\arg\max_{a\in S_t}\langle
abla f(x_t),aangle\), with local gap \(g_t^{m loc}=\langle
abla f(x_t),a_t^+-a_t^-angle\). If this gap passes the algorithm's acceptance threshold, line-search along \(a_t^--a_t^+\) over \([0,\alpha_{a_t^+}^t]\). Otherwise call the global linear minimization oracle for \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle
abla f(x_t),sangle\) and take a Frank-Wolfe step along \(s_t-x_t\). Update the convex coefficients and remove zero-weight atoms. Stop when the global Frank-Wolfe gap is at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a cheap exchange between active atoms when its local gap is adequate; otherwise call the global oracle and take a Frank-Wolfe step.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact polytope, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
A positive local-acceptance threshold rule and a target tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iterate remains in \(C\); termination with global gap \(g_t^{\rm FW}\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x_t)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\) when \(f\) is convex.

notation.meaning: Pairwise gap within the active set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal, but the defining blended acceptance rule is not stated precisely. The exact gap comparison, global-oracle branch, and stopping test must be tied to a specific BPCG source.

children.title: Corrective Simplicial Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Methods optimizing more extensively over the convex hull of discovered atoms.

children.title: Fully Corrective Frank-Wolfe
children.top_down_role: Full correction over the active hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inherited Curvature Rate of Exact Full Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard convex-smooth rate inherited from dominance over the Frank-Wolfe segment update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex with finite Frank-Wolfe curvature constant \(C_f\) on a compact convex set \(C\). If every iteration adds an exact linear-minimization atom and globally minimizes \(f\) over the enlarged active hull, then, for \(t\ge1\), \[f(x_t)-f^*\le \frac{2C_f}{t+2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact fully corrective Frank-Wolfe inherits the standard order-one-over-t curvature rate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(C\) with finite curvature constant \(C_f\).
The linear oracle and every enlarged active-hull master problem are solved exactly.
review_flags: The displayed indexing assumes the first enlarged-hull correction is indexed by t=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Curvature Rate of Exact Full Correction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Correction Dominance over the Frank-Wolfe Segment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective dominance supplied by exact global reoptimization over the enlarged active hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\in\operatorname{conv}(S_t)\), let \(s_t\in C\), and let \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(S_t\cup\{s_t\})}f(x)\). Then, for every \(\gamma\in[0,1]\), \[f(x_{t+1})\le f((1-\gamma)x_t+\gamma s_t).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact correction over the enlarged active hull is never worse than any ordinary Frank-Wolfe step toward the newly added atom.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\in\operatorname{conv}(S_t)\).
The enlarged active-hull problem has a global minimizer and is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Correction Dominance over the Frank-Wolfe Segment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical exact reoptimization over the hull of retained oracle atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a finite \(S_0\subseteq V\) and \(x_0\in\operatorname{conv}(S_0)\). At iteration \(t\), compute \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\), set \(\widehat S_{t+1}=S_t\cup\{s_t\}\), and choose \[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(\widehat S_{t+1})}f(x).\] A representing set \(S_{t+1}\subseteq\widehat S_{t+1}\) may then be obtained by deleting zero-weight atoms. For convex \(f\), the method may stop when \(\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add an exact linear-oracle atom, globally minimize over the enlarged active hull, and optionally prune zero-weight atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is compact.
\(f\) is differentiable on \(C\).
Every finite active-hull master problem attains a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: Active set immediately after adding the oracle atom.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Fully Corrective Frank-Wolfe Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order test for a convex active-hull master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite nonempty \(S\) and convex differentiable \(f\), a point \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\) minimizes \(f\) over \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) if and only if \[\langle\nabla f(x),v-x\rangle\geq0\qquad(v\in S).\] If \(x=\sum_{v\in S}\lambda_vv\), this is equivalent to the existence of \(\tau\) such that \(\langle\nabla f(x),v\rangle\geq\tau\) for every \(v\in S\), with equality whenever \(\lambda_v>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active-hull master is solved exactly when every active atom has nonnegative linearized displacement from the candidate solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
\(f\) is convex and differentiable on \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
\(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Hull Master Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Alone Does Not Give Segment Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for the fully corrective dominance property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\), \(f(z)=(z-1)^2\), \(x=0\), and let the newly added atom be \(s=1\). The feasibility-only choice \(x^+=0\in\operatorname{conv}\{x,s\}\) has \(f(x^+)=1\), while \[\min_{\gamma\in[0,1]}f((1-\gamma)x+\gamma s)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible but unoptimized active-hull update can be strictly worse than the best Frank-Wolfe segment step.
assumptions_latex: The correction is required only to remain in the enlarged active hull.
No exact or sufficient-decrease master condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Alone Does Not Give Segment Dominance
Fully Corrective Frank-Wolfe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reoptimization over the convex hull of all atoms selected so far.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with an atom \(x_0\in V\) and \(S_0=\{x_0\}\). At iteration \(t\), compute \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\), enlarge \(S_{t+1}=S_t\cup\{s_t\}\), and solve the master problem \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\min\{f(x):x\in\operatorname{conv}(S_{t+1})\}\). Any representation of \(x_{t+1}\) may be pruned by deleting zero coefficients, without changing the point. Stop when the Frank-Wolfe gap \(\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\) is at most a prescribed tolerance. The correction is full because every coefficient over the accumulated active hull is jointly reoptimized after each oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After adding a linear-oracle atom, exactly minimize the objective over the convex hull of every retained atom and prune atoms with zero optimal weight.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
Each finite active-hull master problem attains a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in C\) and \(f(x_{t+1})\leq f(x_t)\); for convex \(f\), the stopping gap bounds primal suboptimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and exact reoptimization over the accumulated active hull fit Fully Corrective Frank-Wolfe, but the master update and stopping convention lack an authoritative citation and locator.

children.title: Partially Corrective Frank-Wolfe
children.top_down_role: Restricted correction families balancing progress and correction cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Corrective Frank-Wolfe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact or restricted active-hull correction following a Frank-Wolfe atom addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_t\in\operatorname{conv}(S_t)\), obtain \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in V}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\) and set \(\widehat S_t=S_t\cup\{s_t\}\). A partially corrective step returns \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname{conv}(\widehat S_t)\) satisfying a prescribed correction condition weaker than exact master minimization, for example \(f(x_{t+1})\leq f(x_t+\eta_t(s_t-x_t))\) for a specified feasible reference step \(\eta_t\in[0,1]\), or a stated active-hull optimality residual bound. Update the representation of \(x_{t+1}\) and delete zero-weight atoms. Thus correction may use finitely many inner active-set iterations, restricted coefficient changes, or an inexact master solve, but its acceptance predicate must be fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a Frank-Wolfe atom, then improve over the enlarged active hull only enough to satisfy a stated decrease or residual condition, rather than solving exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is compact, \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and \(x_t\in\operatorname{conv}(S_t)\).
The correction subroutine has a specified, verifiable acceptance condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted point satisfies \(x_{t+1}\in C\) and the decrease or residual guarantee imposed by the chosen partial-correction criterion.

notation.meaning: Active set after adding the new oracle atom.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal, but the record combines several inequivalent notions of partial correction. A source must identify the intended family and justify the accepted decrease or residual condition.

children.title: Simplicial Decomposition Methods
children.top_down_role: Master-problem methods over successively enriched inner approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Decomposition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive inner approximation with exact or inexact master optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a finite \(S_0\subset C\) and solve the initial master problem over \(C_0=\operatorname{conv}(S_0)\). Given a master point \(x_t\in C_t\), obtain \(s_t\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle\). If \(\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\leq\varepsilon\), return \(x_t\). Otherwise form the enriched inner approximation \(C_{t+1}=\operatorname{conv}(S_t\cup\{s_t\})\), compute \(x_{t+1}\) by exact or prescribed-accuracy minimization of \(f\) over \(C_{t+1}\), and optionally discard generators while retaining \(x_{t+1}\) and the required master accuracy. For convex \(f\), the oracle gap supplies the stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly add a linear-oracle point to an inner polytope and solve a master problem over the enriched convex hull until the oracle gap is small.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
The linear minimization oracle and each finite master solve satisfy their stated accuracy requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every master point lies in \(C\), and termination at gap at most \(\varepsilon\) implies \(f(x_t)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Generators of the current master region.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the simplicial-decomposition terminal, but exact and inexact master variants are blended, and the optional generator-discard rule needs a precise accuracy convention and source.

children.title: Boosted Multi-Direction Variant Family
children.top_down_role: Methods enriching the classical direction through repeated or multi-atom oracle information.

children.title: Boosted Frank-Wolfe Methods
children.top_down_role: Direction-strengthening methods based on repeated atom selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Boosted Frank-Wolfe Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-oracle construction of a direction more aligned with the negative gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_t\in C\), initialize \(q_0=0\). For \(j=1,\ldots,m_t\), call a linear minimization oracle using a residual-derived linear objective, obtain an atom \(s_{t,j}\in C\), and update \(q_j\) within \(\operatorname{span}\{s_{t,1}-x_t,\ldots,s_{t,j}-x_t\}\) so that the alignment \(\langle-\nabla f(x_t),q_j\rangle/\|q_j\|\) satisfies the prescribed monotone improvement test. Stop the inner loop when the test fails, the target alignment is reached, or \(m_t\) calls have occurred. Set \(d_t=q_j\), choose \(\gamma_t\) over the maximal interval for which \(x_t+\gamma d_t\in C\), and return \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t d_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use repeated linear-oracle calls to combine atom directions into one direction better aligned with negative gradient, then line-search along its feasible segment.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
The inner construction preserves a nonzero feasible direction and uses a specified alignment-improvement rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer update remains in \(C\); when the accepted combined direction has positive alignment, it is a first-order descent direction.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of inner oracle calls at iteration t.
Direction accumulated after j inner selections.
Atom returned by the j-th inner oracle call.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the boosted-method terminal, but the residual oracle objective, construction of q_j, alignment test, and preservation of feasibility are defining details rather than optional implementation choices. The mathematical algorithm is unreliable without an exact source.

children.title: k-Atom Frank-Wolfe Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods using multiple candidate atoms in an iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: k-Atom Frank-Wolfe Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic corrective conditional-gradient iteration using up to k newly selected atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and convex, and fix \(k\geq 1\). Initialize \(x_0\in P\) with a finite active set \(S_0\subset V\) satisfying \(x_0\in\operatorname{conv}(S_0)\). At iteration \(t\), obtain distinct atoms \(B_t\subset V\), with \(|B_t|\leq k\), having the smallest available values of \(\langle\nabla f(x_t),v\rangle\). Set \(T_t=S_t\cup B_t\), choose \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname{conv}(T_t)\) by exact correction or another specified descent correction, and choose \(S_{t+1}\subseteq T_t\) representing \(x_{t+1}\). Stop when \(g_t=\langle\nabla f(x_t),x_t-s_t\rangle\leq\varepsilon\), where \(s_t\) minimizes the linearization over \(V\); output \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select up to k best linear-oracle atoms, add them to the active set, correct over their enlarged convex hull, and stop using the Frank-Wolfe gap.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is a compact polytope with finite vertex set \(V\).
\(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(P\).
The multi-atom oracle and correction subproblem are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in P\) for every \(t\), and termination at \(g_t\leq\varepsilon\) supplies the usual Frank-Wolfe optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: active atoms representing the current iterate
set of at most k newly returned atoms

knowledge_statements.title: Polytope-Width Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional pyramidal width used in affine-constrained Frank-Wolfe rate analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(x\in P\), let \(S_x\) range over finite subsets of \(V\) for which \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S_x)\). For a nonzero feasible direction \(r\in\operatorname{cone}(P-x)\), define the pyramidal directional width by \[\operatorname{PdirW}(V,r,x)=\min_{S_x}\ \max_{s\in V,\,v\in S_x}\left\langle\frac{r}{\|r\|},s-v\right\rangle.\] The pyramidal width of \(P\) is \[\operatorname{PWidth}(P)=\min_{F\in\mathcal{F}(P)}\ \min_{x\in F}\ \min_{0\neq r\in\operatorname{cone}(F-x)}\operatorname{PdirW}(V\cap F,r,x),\] where \(\mathcal{F}(P)\) denotes the nonempty faces of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pyramidal width is the smallest normalized directional separation between a forward atom and a possible active atom, minimized over faces, points, feasible directions, and representations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty compact polytope in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(V\) is the vertex set of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{PWidth}(P)\) is a representation-sensitive geometric condition measure used to control active-set Frank-Wolfe descent.

notation.meaning: collection of nonempty faces of P
cone of feasible displacements from x within F

children.title: Facial-Distance Measures
children.top_down_role: Distance-based condition measures associated with faces plus active atoms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite computation of facial distance from a true vertex representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible proper face \(F\), let \(I_F=\{i:v_i\in F\}\) and \(I_{\bar F}=\{1,\ldots,m\}\setminus I_F\). Its squared separation from the complementary vertex hull is \[d_F^2=\min_{\alpha\in\Delta(I_F),\,\beta\in\Delta(I_{\bar F})}\left\|\sum_{i\in I_F}\alpha_i v_i-\sum_{j\in I_{\bar F}}\beta_jv_j\right\|^2.\] Enumerating eligible proper faces, solving these convex quadratic programs exactly, and returning \(\min_F d_F\) computes \(\Phi(P)\). The procedure is finite, but naive face enumeration may be exponential in the input representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial distance is the minimum of one convex quadratic distance problem per eligible face; exhaustive face enumeration is finite but may be exponential.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) is positive-dimensional and the listed points are exactly its vertices.
Eligible proper faces can be enumerated.
The quadratic programs are solved exactly.

notation.meaning: indices of vertices lying in face F
probability simplex on index set I

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Quadratic-Program Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positivity and Euclidean similarity covariance for positive-dimensional polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every positive-dimensional polytope \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) with its true vertex set, each eligible proper face is strictly separated from the convex hull of the vertices outside it. Since a polytope has finitely many faces, \[0<\Phi(P)<\infty.\] Moreover, if \(Q=\lambda UP+b\), where \(\lambda>0\), \(U\) is orthogonal, and \(b\) is arbitrary, then \[\Phi(Q)=\lambda\Phi(P).\] For a zero-dimensional polytope the eligible face family is empty, so a value requires a separately declared convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial distance is positive for positive-dimensional polytopes, invariant under rigid motions, and homogeneous under uniform scaling; singleton polytopes need a separate convention.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) is a compact polytope of positive dimension.
\(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\).
Distance uses a fixed Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity and Similarity Covariance
Facial-Distance Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum Euclidean separation of a face from vertices outside that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(V\) is the vertex set of \(P\). Its facial distance is \[\Phi(P)=\min_{F\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{prop}}(P)}\operatorname{dist}\!\left(F,\operatorname{conv}(V\setminus F)\right),\] where \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{prop}}(P)\) contains the nonempty proper faces for which \(V\setminus F\neq\varnothing\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(A,B)=\inf\{\|a-b\|:a\in A,\ b\in B\}\). Thus \(\Phi(P)\) measures the smallest separation between any proper face and the convex hull of all vertices not belonging to that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial distance is the minimum distance between a proper face and the convex hull of all vertices outside that face.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty compact polytope with vertex set \(V\).
Distance is measured in a fixed Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(P)>0\) for every polytope \(P\) of positive dimension.

notation.meaning: eligible nonempty proper faces of P

review_flags: A primary-source locator is required to certify the intended facial-distance convention.

children.title: Condition-Measure Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Relationships among geometric constants used in linear-rate analyses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent comparison under Euclidean similarities for fixed Euclidean definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix Euclidean definitions of facial distance and pyramidal width based on distances and normalized directional inner products. If \(Q=\lambda UP+b\), where \(\lambda>0\), \(U\) is orthogonal, and \(b\) is arbitrary, then \[\Phi(Q)=\lambda\Phi(P),\qquad \operatorname{PWidth}(Q)=\lambda\operatorname{PWidth}(P).\] Their ratio, whenever defined, is therefore invariant under Euclidean similarities. This covariance does not itself establish equality of the two measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under fixed Euclidean conventions, facial distance and pyramidal width scale identically under similarities, so their ratio is similarity invariant.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a positive-dimensional compact polytope.
Both measures use fixed definitions with the same Euclidean norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Similarity Transformation Law
Condition-Measure Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of facial distance and pyramidal width under matched Euclidean conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) be a polytope, with \(V\) equal to its complete vertex set, and define both \(\Phi(P)\) and \(\operatorname{PWidth}(P)\) using the same Euclidean norm. Under the standard face-restricted definition of pyramidal width, the two condition measures coincide: \[\operatorname{PWidth}(P)=\Phi(P).\] Consequently, a linear-rate bound expressed using one measure can be rewritten using the other without changing its geometric constant. This identity need not survive unchanged if \(V\) contains redundant generators or if one definition omits the minimization over active representations or faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the standard definitions and the true vertex set, pyramidal width equals facial distance; redundant generating sets or altered conventions can invalidate the identity.

children.title: Objective-Growth Regimes for Linear Rates
children.top_down_role: Strong-convexity, error-bound, and structured-composition regimes supporting linear convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp logical boundaries among strong convexity, quadratic growth, and ordinary smooth convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(P=[-1,1]^2\), the function \(f(x,y)=x^2\) has \(X^*=\{0\}\times[-1,1]\) and \[f(x,y)-f^*=\operatorname{dist}((x,y),X^*)^2,\] so it has quadratic growth with \(\mu_q=2\), but it is not strongly convex because it is constant in the \(y\)-direction. Conversely, on \([-1,1]\), the smooth convex function \(q(x)=x^4\) has no positive quadratic-growth constant: \(x^4\geq(\mu_q/2)x^2\) fails for every \(\mu_q>0\) as \(x\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth can hold despite flat directions along the solution set, while a smooth convex quartic can fail quadratic growth near its minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Each example is restricted to the displayed compact convex feasible set.
Distance is Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Quadratic growth is strictly weaker than strong convexity, and smooth convexity alone does not imply quadratic growth.}

notation.meaning: solution set of the displayed example

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Growth Separation and Failure Examples

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic growth obtained from curvature in a linear image and an error bound for the optimal fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=g(Ax)\) on a compact polytope \(P\). If \(g\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(A(P)\), then all minimizers have a common image \(z^*\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq H\|Ax-z^*\|\) for every \(x\in P\), then \[f(x)-f^*\geq\frac{\mu}{2}\|Ax-z^*\|^2\geq\frac{\mu}{2H^2}\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^2.\] Hence \(f\) has quadratic growth with constant at least \(\mu/H^2\), even when \(A\) is not injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong curvature after a linear map gives quadratic growth when image error controls distance to the optimal fiber; injectivity is unnecessary.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
\(g\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(A(P)\).
\(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}g(Ax)\neq\varnothing\).
For some \(H<\infty\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq H\|Ax-z^*\|\) for all \(x\in P\), where \(z^*=Ax^*\) for \(x^*\in X^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\neq\varnothing\). Away-Step Linear Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract global linear rate obtained from good-step contraction and drop-step counting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_t=f(x_t)-f^*\) for away-step Frank-Wolfe on a polytope. Suppose every good iteration satisfies \(h_{t+1}\leq(1-\rho_A)h_t\) for some \(0<\rho_A<1\), while every drop iteration is nonincreasing in objective value. If a forward step introduces at most one atom and a drop step removes at least one atom, then among the first \(t\) iterations the number \(G_t\) of good steps obeys \(G_t\geq\lceil(t-|S_0|+1)/2\rceil\). Hence \[h_t\leq h_0(1-\rho_A)^{G_t}\leq h_0\exp(-\rho_A G_t).\] Thus \(O(\rho_A^{-1}\log(h_0/\varepsilon))\) iterations suffice, up to the active-set offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Away-step Frank-Wolfe converges geometrically when every non-drop step contracts the error and drop steps cannot outnumber atom-adding steps by more than an active-set offset.

children.title: Rate-Constant Comparisons

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Constant Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common accounting form for comparing active-set Frank-Wolfe linear rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active-set method \(m\), suppose good iterations contract objective error by \(h_{j+1}\leq(1-\rho_m)h_j\), all other iterations are nonincreasing, and \(G_m(t)\geq\alpha_m t-\beta_m\). Then \[h_t\leq h_0\exp\!\left(-\alpha_m\rho_m t+\rho_m\beta_m\right)\] whenever \(\alpha_m t\geq\beta_m\). Thus asymptotic guarantees are compared through the effective exponent \(\alpha_m[-\log(1-\rho_m)]\), not through \(\rho_m\) alone. A method with stronger per-good-step descent can have a weaker global guarantee if its good-step frequency is smaller; curvature, objective growth, polytope width, and exceptional-step accounting must therefore be normalized before rate constants are ranked.

children.title: Active-Set Step-Accounting Calculus

children.title: Drop-Step Accounting
children.top_down_role: Iteration accounting for steps that remove atoms from the active representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Drop-Step Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set cardinality bound on the number of atom-removing iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider iterations \(j=0,\ldots,t-1\) with nonempty finite active sets \(S_j\). Suppose a forward iteration increases active-set cardinality by at most one, a drop iteration decreases it by at least one, and every other iteration does not increase cardinality. If \(F_t\) and \(D_t\) count forward and drop iterations, respectively, then \[1\leq |S_t|\leq |S_0|+F_t-D_t.\] Consequently, \[D_t\leq F_t+|S_0|-1.\] In particular, if every iteration is either good or a drop step and each drop requires a preceding or initially available atom, drop steps cannot constitute more than approximately half of a long run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every drop consumes an active atom, while each forward step creates at most one; hence drops are bounded by forward additions plus the initial active-set surplus.
assumptions_latex: Every active set is finite and nonempty.
Forward steps add at most one active atom.
Drop steps remove at least one active atom.

notation.meaning: number of forward atom-adding steps before t
number of drop steps before t

review_flags: No relevant source locator was supplied for the active-set accounting lemma.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the accounting leaf and the cardinality inequality is precise under the stated update assumptions. Nevertheless, the record contains no citation or specific locator for this nontrivial active-set accounting lemma.

children.title: Swap-Step Accounting
children.top_down_role: Iteration accounting for steps exchanging active weight between atoms.

assumptions_latex: A swap transfers all weight of one active atom to a previously inactive atom.
The active set records precisely the atoms having positive weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S_{t+1}|=|S_t|\) on a swap, so active-set cardinality alone yields no finite swap-count bound.

notation.meaning: positive-weight active set before iteration t

review_flags: No relevant source locator was supplied for the pairwise swap-step limitation.
The malformed escape following the cardinality expression was repaired; all TeX commands in statement_latex are now inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why active-set cardinality alone cannot bound pairwise swap iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In pairwise Frank-Wolfe, a maximal step may remove one active atom while simultaneously introducing one previously inactive atom. Such a swap satisfies \(|S_{t+1}|=|S_t|\). Therefore the cardinality potential \(|S_t|\), which bounds drop steps, gives no upper bound on the number of swap steps: any finite sequence of swaps is compatible with a constant active-set size. A global linear-rate proof for pairwise updates must instead establish an independent bound on swap frequency, use a richer combinatorial or geometric potential, or count only good steps. Treating every maximal pairwise step as a cardinality-decreasing drop step is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A swap removes one atom and adds another, leaving active-set size unchanged; consequently, drop-step cardinality accounting cannot control how many swaps occur.
knowledge_statements.title: Swap-Step Accounting

children.title: Good-Step Accounting
children.top_down_role: Iteration accounting for steps producing quantifiable objective progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Good-Step Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of per-good-step contraction into an iteration-indexed rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t\) and \(B_t\) denote the numbers of good and exceptional iterations among indices \(0,\ldots,t-1\), so that \(t=G_t+B_t\). Suppose exceptional iterations satisfy \(B_t\leq G_t+b_0\) for a constant \(b_0\geq0\). Then \[G_t\geq\left\lceil\frac{t-b_0}{2}\right\rceil_+.\] If every good step satisfies \(h_{j+1}\leq(1-\rho)h_j\), with \(0<\rho<1\), and exceptional steps do not increase \(h_j\), then \[h_t\leq h_0(1-\rho)^{G_t}\leq h_0\exp\!\left(-\rho\left\lceil\frac{t-b_0}{2}\right\rceil_+\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exceptional steps never outnumber good steps by more than a fixed offset, at least about half the iterations contract, yielding a global geometric rate.
assumptions_latex: Every iteration is classified as good or exceptional.
\(B_t\leq G_t+b_0\).
Good steps contract error by \(1-\rho\), and exceptional steps are nonincreasing.

notation.meaning: number of good steps before t
number of exceptional steps before t

children.title: Iteration-Class Balance
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial relationships among exceptional-step counts plus progress-bearing iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Class Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set cardinality accounting for away-step Frank–Wolfe iterations over a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_t\) be the active set after iteration \(t\), with redundant zero-weight atoms removed. During the first \(T\) iterations, let \(A_T\) count steps that introduce one new atom, \(D_T\) count drop steps that remove one atom, and suppose all remaining steps leave active-set cardinality unchanged. Then
\[
|S_T|=|S_0|+A_T-D_T,
\qquad
D_T\leq A_T+|S_0|-1.
\]
Consequently, if \(S_0\) is a singleton and each atom-adding step belongs to the good-step class, then \(D_T\leq G_T\), where \(G_T\) is the number of good steps, and at least half of the first \(T\) iterations are non-drop steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set cardinality implies that drop steps cannot outnumber atom additions, up to the initial active-set surplus; from singleton initialization, at least half the iterations are non-drop steps.
assumptions_latex: S_t is finite and nonempty for every t.
Each counted addition or drop changes |S_t| by exactly one.
All other iteration classes preserve |S_t|.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_T\leq A_T+|S_0|-1; in particular, |S_0|=1 and A_T\leq G_T imply D_T\leq G_T.

notation.meaning: active atom set after iteration t
numbers of atom-addition and drop steps through iteration T
number of good steps through iteration T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-set identity and resulting drop-step bound are mathematically consistent and fit the Iteration-Class Balance container. The final half-iteration claim additionally relies on atom additions being non-drop iterations and on the good-step and drop-step classes being disjoint. No inspectable source is supplied for the away-step classification conventions.

Optimal-Face Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification under convergence, strict face separation, and persistent deletion of excluded atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a polytope, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and convex, and let \(F_*\) be the minimal face containing the solution set \(X_*\). Consider active-set iterates \(x_t\to x_*\in\operatorname{relint}(F_*)\). Suppose strict complementarity separates every vertex outside \(F_*\), and the update rule eventually neither inserts a strictly separated vertex nor retains such a vertex indefinitely. Then there exists a finite \(K\) such that, for every \(t\geq K\), the active set satisfies \(S_t\subseteq\operatorname{vert}(F_*)\), hence \(x_t\in F_*\). If the rule maintains a representation spanning \(F_*\), it identifies \(F_*\) itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent active-set method finitely enters the optimal face when strict complementarity separates outside vertices and the update rule eventually rejects or deletes every separated atom.

children.title: Strict-Complementarity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complementarity settings supporting stable active-face recognition.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertexwise strict complementarity relative to the minimal optimal face of a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a polytope, let \(x_*\) minimize a differentiable convex function \(f\) over \(C\), and let \(F_*\) be the minimal face containing \(x_*\). Strict complementarity at \(x_*\) relative to \(F_*\) means that some \(\delta>0\) satisfies
\[
\langle\nabla f(x_*),v-x_*\rangle=0
\quad\text{for every }v\in\operatorname{vert}(F_*),
\]
and
\[
\langle\nabla f(x_*),v-x_*\rangle\geq\delta
\quad\text{for every }v\in\operatorname{vert}(C)\setminus F_*.
\]
Thus the exposed face minimizing the linearization at \(x_*\) is exactly \(F_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity makes every optimal-face vertex tie in the optimal linearization while every vertex outside that face has a uniformly larger linearized value.
assumptions_latex: C is a polytope.
f is differentiable and convex on C.
x_* is a minimizer and F_* is its minimal containing face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_*),x\rangle=F_*, with a positive vertexwise separation margin outside F_*.

notation.meaning: minimal face of C containing x_*
vertex set of the polytope C

children.title: Face-Separation Margins
children.top_down_role: Geometric margins distinguishing solution faces from competing atoms or faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Separation Margins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative separation between optimal-face and excluded vertices in the optimal linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a polytope, \(F_*\) a face, and \(x_*\in F_*\). For differentiable \(f\), define the face-separation margin
\[
\Delta_{F_*}(x_*):=
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(C)\setminus F_*}
\langle\nabla f(x_*),v-x_*\rangle
-
\max_{u\in\operatorname{vert}(F_*)}
\langle\nabla f(x_*),u-x_*\rangle.
\]
When \(F_*\) is the exposed minimizer face of the linearization, the second term equals zero. A positive margin \(\Delta_{F_*}(x_*)>0\) quantitatively separates every excluded vertex from every vertex of \(F_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The face-separation margin is the smallest linearization-value gap between excluded vertices and optimal-face vertices; positivity gives uniform atom separation.
assumptions_latex: C is a polytope and F_* is a face of C.
f is differentiable at x_*\in F_*.
The excluded vertex set is nonempty; otherwise the margin is +\infty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta_{F_*}(x_*)>0 exactly expresses uniform vertexwise separation of F_* from \operatorname{vert}(C)\setminus F_* under the linearization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of face selection when additive oracle error is smaller than the current face-versus-outside gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a face of a polytope \(C\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \[m:=\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(C)\setminus F}\langle g,v\rangle-\min_{u\in\operatorname{vert}(F)}\langle g,u\rangle>0.\] If \(s\in\operatorname{vert}(C)\) satisfies \[\langle g,s\rangle\le\min_{z\in C}\langle g,z\rangle+\delta,\qquad 0\le\delta<m,\] then \(s\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error linear oracle selects the distinguished face whenever its error is strictly smaller than the face-versus-outside gap.

Stable Atom Discrimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of face-versus-nonface oracle ordering near a strictly complementary solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a compact polytope of diameter \(D\), and suppose \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(C\). If the face-separation margin at \(x_*\) is \(\Delta>0\), then every \(x\in C\) satisfying \(2LD\|x-x_*\|<\Delta\) obeys

children.title: Post-Identification Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local rate families after entry into the relevant face.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a restricted-face contraction to the original active-set iteration after finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_*\) be an optimal face and suppose an active-set method identifies it at iteration \(K\), so \(x_t\in F_*\) for every \(t\geq K\). Assume its restricted update on \(F_*\) satisfies, for some \(q\in(0,1)\),
\[
f(x_{t+1})-f_*\leq q\bigl(f(x_t)-f_*\bigr),
\qquad t\geq K.
\]
Then the original sequence has the post-identification linear rate
\[
f(x_t)-f_*\leq q^{t-K}\bigl(f(x_K)-f_*\bigr),
\qquad t\geq K.
\]
Any sharper rate proved for the restricted problem likewise applies from iteration \(K\) onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once the method remains on the optimal face, any contraction established for the face-restricted algorithm becomes the local convergence rate of the original sequence.
assumptions_latex: The method finitely identifies F_* at iteration K.
The objective minimum over F_* equals the global value f_*.
The restricted update contracts objective error by q\in(0,1).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x_t)-f_*\leq q^{t-K}(f(x_K)-f_*) for every t\geq K.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Iterating the assumed contraction gives the displayed post-identification rate, and the property fits the container. A source is still required to certify that the original algorithm's updates after identification coincide with the asserted face-restricted method. The sentence claiming transfer of any sharper rate also needs the corresponding restricted-method hypotheses rather than an unqualified rate transfer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space. A smooth-plus-structured convex model is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\ \Phi(x):=f(x)+h(x),
\]
where \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and continuously differentiable on \(\operatorname{dom}h\), while \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Generalized conditional-gradient access means that, for each query \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\), one can compute

\bigl\{\langle\nabla f(x),v\rangle+h(v)\bigr\}.
\]
The effective feasible region is \(\operatorname{dom}h\).

\(h\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex for \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-dual characterization of oracle regularity induced by strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conjugate \(h^*:X^*\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable with \(\mu^{-1}\)-Lipschitz gradient, and the structured oracle is \(v(p)=\nabla h^*(-p)\). Conversely, for proper closed convex \(h\), this conjugate smoothness is equivalent to \(\mu\)-strong convexity under the same norm-dual-norm convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity of the structured term is equivalent to smoothness of its conjugate, and the oracle is the conjugate gradient at the negative coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity-Conjugate Smoothness Equivalence
Strongly Convex Composite Terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness and stability of the generalized oracle induced by strong convexity of the structured term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), where \(\mu>0\). For every dual vector \(p\), the oracle problem
\[
v(p):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in X}\{\langle p,v\rangle+h(v)\}
\]
has at most one minimizer; whenever minimizers exist for \(p\) and \(q\), they satisfy
\[
\|v(p)-v(q)\|\leq \frac{1}{\mu}\|p-q\|_*.
\]
Thus the generalized conditional-gradient direction \(v(\nabla f(x))-x\) is single-valued and stable wherever the oracle is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity makes the generalized linearized composite oracle unique and Lipschitz in its dual linear coefficient, stabilizing generalized conditional-gradient directions.
assumptions_latex: h is proper, closed, and \mu-strongly convex.
The oracle minima at p and q are attained.
The dual norm \|\cdot\|_* corresponds to \|\cdot\|.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|v(p)-v(q)\|\leq \mu^{-1}\|p-q\|_*, and v(p) is unique whenever it exists.

notation.meaning: structured oracle minimizer with linear coefficient p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniqueness and 1/mu Lipschitz estimate are standard consequences of strong convexity and fit the container, but X and its dimensional/topological setting are not introduced in this record. More importantly, no source is supplied for the strong-convexity convention and the resulting dual-to-primal oracle stability bound.
