children.title: Simplex Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-vertex domains with inexpensive linear-minimization access.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate form of the conditional-gradient certificate on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\Delta_d\) and a differentiable convex function \(f\), \[g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)=\max_{s\in\Delta_d}\langle
abla f(x),x-sangle=\langle
abla f(x),xangle-\min_{1\le i\le d}
abla_i f(x).\] It is nonnegative, satisfies \(f(x)-\min_{y\in\Delta_d}f(y)\le g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)\), and vanishes exactly when \(x\) satisfies first-order optimality for minimizing \(f\) over \(\Delta_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the simplex, the Frank-Wolfe gap is the gradient average under x minus the smallest gradient coordinate; for convex objectives it bounds suboptimality and vanishes at optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(\Delta_d\)
\(x\in\Delta_d\)
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Linearization-Gap Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case coordinate-access cost of exact simplex linear minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicitly stored dense vector \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), an exact simplex linear oracle is implemented by finding an index in \(\arg\min_i g_i\). A sequential scan uses \(d\) coordinate inspections and at most \(d-1\) comparisons. In the unrestricted coordinate-access comparison model, every exact worst-case algorithm must inspect all \(d\) coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact dense simplex oracle is a minimum-coordinate scan, using linear time and d-1 comparisons in the standard comparison model.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in\mathbb R^d\) is available through unrestricted coordinate access
The oracle must be exact in the worst case
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Simplex Linear-Oracle Cost
Simplex Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear minimization and atomic updates on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the simplex \(\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^d x_i=1\}\), the atoms are \(e_1,\ldots,e_d\). Given a cost vector \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), a linear minimization oracle returns \[i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le d}g_i,\qquad s=e_{i^*},\] because \(\min_{s\in\Delta_d}\langle g,s\rangle=\min_i g_i\). From \(x_t\in\Delta_d\), the conditional-gradient update \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t e_{i^*}\), with \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\), remains in \(\Delta_d\) and introduces at most one new coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the simplex, linear minimization selects a minimum-cost coordinate, and the conditional-gradient update mixes the iterate with that coordinate vertex.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(x_t\in\Delta_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s=e_{i^*}\) solves the simplex linear oracle and \(x_{t+1}\in\Delta_d\).

notation.meaning: Linear-oracle cost vector, typically a gradient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex linear-minimization rule and feasible conditional-gradient update are correct, and algorithm is an appropriate kind for this interface, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Combinatorial-Polytope Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral domains whose extreme points encode discrete structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial-Polytope Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-oracle interface for convex hulls of discrete feasible objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\subset\{0,1\}^d\) be a finite set encoding feasible combinatorial objects and let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(Z)\). Every \(x\in P\) admits a representation \(x=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_j z_j\), where \(z_j\in Z\), \(\lambda_j\ge0\), and \(\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_j=1\). For any \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), \[\min_{x\in P}\langle g,x\rangle=\min_{z\in Z}\langle g,z\rangle.\] Consequently, conditional-gradient access to \(P\) may be implemented by a combinatorial optimizer over \(Z\), while iterates are stored as convex mixtures of returned feasible objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combinatorial polytope is the convex hull of discrete feasible objects; its linear oracle reduces exactly to optimizing over those objects.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\subset\{0,1\}^d\) is finite and nonempty.
\(P=\operatorname{conv}(Z)\).
\(g\in\mathbb R^d\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the discrete feasible set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-hull representation and equality of linear minima fit the combinatorial-polytope interface, but the record has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Discrete-Atom Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Linear-oracle interfaces based on selecting structured discrete atoms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation-invariant relative accuracy for a discrete conditional-gradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\), \(x\in C\), \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), and \(\rho\in(0,1]\). A relative-gap oracle returns \(\widetilde a\in A\) satisfying \[\langle g,x-\widetilde a\rangle\ge\rho\sup_{a\in A}\langle g,x-a\rangle.\] This guarantees a \(\rho\)-fraction of the best available linearized decrease and is invariant under adding the same scalar offset to all linear-oracle costs. An atom-valued exact realization requires attainment of the best improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-gap oracle captures a fixed fraction of the best atom improvement and avoids the offset dependence of multiplicative approximation applied to raw costs.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) and \(x\in C\)
The best atom improvement is attained when an atom-valued maximizer is required
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Gap Discrete-Atom Oracle
Discrete-Atom Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and additive-approximate linear minimization over discrete atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty discrete atomic set and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\). Given \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), an exact discrete-atom oracle returns \(a_g\in A\) satisfying \[\langle g,a_g\rangle=\inf_{a\in A}\langle g,a\rangle.\] An additive \(\delta\)-approximate oracle returns \(\widetilde a_g\in A\) with \(\langle g,\widetilde a_g\rangle\le\inf_{a\in A}\langle g,a\rangle+\delta\), where \(\delta\ge0\). Since a linear functional has the same infimum over \(A\) and \(C\), either output supplies the corresponding exact or approximate conditional-gradient direction without constructing \(C\) explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete-atom oracle minimizes a linear cost over atoms exactly or within additive error, thereby implementing the convex-hull linear oracle.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty.
The displayed infimum is finite and attained for the exact oracle.
\(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}\langle g,x\rangle=\inf_{a\in A}\langle g,a\rangle\), with additive error at most \(\delta\) for the approximate oracle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact and additive-approximate oracle specifications fit the algorithm leaf and include the needed attainment assumption for the exact output, but no authoritative oracle source is cited.

children.title: Atomic-Norm Ball Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Norm and gauge domains encoding structured sparsity.

assumptions_latex: A=\{-1,2\}\subset\mathbb R.
\gamma_A is the gauge of \operatorname{conv}(A)=[-1,2].
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central symmetry is essential for an atomic gauge to be a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A=\{-1,2\}\subset\mathbb R, the convex hull is [-1,2] and its gauge satisfies \gamma_A(1)=1/2 while \gamma_A(-1)=1. Thus the spanning dictionary defines an asymmetric gauge rather than a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spanning dictionary {-1,2} gives different gauge values at 1 and -1, so spanning alone does not produce an atomic norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric-Dictionary Gauge Boundary

assumptions_latex: A\subset\mathbb R^d is compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning.
\operatorname{conv}(A) is the unit ball of \|\cdot\|_A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x\|_A=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m|c_i|:m\in\mathbb N,\ a_i\in A,\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\right\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite atomic-decomposition representation of the atomic norm in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\subset\mathbb R^d be compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning. Then for every x\in\mathbb R^d, \[\|x\|_A=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m|c_i|:m\in\mathbb N,\ a_i\in A,\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\right\}.\] Equivalently, \|x\|_A\leq\tau exactly when x has a finite signed atomic decomposition with coefficient mass at most \tau.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The atomic norm is the least total absolute coefficient mass among finite atomic representations of the point.
knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Decomposition Formula
Atomic-Norm Ball Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge, convex-hull, and linear-oracle descriptions of atomic domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning, and define the atomic norm by \(\lVert x\rVert_A=\inf\{t>0:x\in t\operatorname{conv}(A)\}\). Its unit ball is \(\operatorname{conv}(A)\), and its dual norm is \[\lVert y\rVert_A^*=\sup_{a\in A}\langle y,a\rangle.\] For radius \(\tau>0\), a linear minimization oracle over \(C=\{x:\lVert x\rVert_A\le\tau\}\) may return \(s=-\tau a_y\), where \(a_y\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in A}\langle y,a\rangle\). It then satisfies \(\min_{x\in C}\langle y,x\rangle=-\tau\lVert y\rVert_A^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atomic norm has the atomic convex hull as unit ball; its dual maximizes correlation with an atom, which also implements linear minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning.
The dual maximizer \(a_y\) is selected from \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\lVert x\rVert_A\le\tau}\langle y,x\rangle=-\tau\lVert y\rVert_A^*\), attained at \(-\tau a_y\).

notation.meaning: Gauge of the atomic convex hull.
Atom of maximum correlation with y.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under compactness, central symmetry, and spanning, the gauge, dual norm, and linear-oracle identities are consistent and duality is the correct content kind. The record nevertheless lacks a supporting source and locator.

children.title: Spectral Matrix-Domain Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Matrix domains with singular-vector or eigenvector linear oracles.

children.title: Nuclear-Norm Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Low-rank matrix domains governed by nuclear-norm constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear-Norm Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic and linear-minimization representation of a matrix nuclear-norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For matrices in \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(\mathcal A=\{uv^{\mathsf T}:\|u\|_2=\|v\|_2=1\}\). The nuclear-norm ball of radius \(\tau>0\) satisfies \[\{X:\|X\|_*\leq \tau\}=\tau\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup-\mathcal A).\] Consequently, for any cost matrix \(G\), a linear minimizer is \[S\in\arg\min_{\|X\|_*\leq\tau}\langle G,X\rangle=-\tau uv^{\mathsf T},\] where \(u,v\) are unit left and right singular vectors associated with the largest singular value of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nuclear-norm ball is the convex hull of signed rank-one unit atoms, and its linear oracle returns a scaled leading singular-vector outer product.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\)

notation.meaning: nuclear norm, the sum of singular values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and linear-oracle formula are mathematically standard and fit the Nuclear-Norm Interfaces leaf, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator. The displayed argmin sentence should also avoid syntactically equating an argmin set with a matrix value.

children.title: Spectrahedral Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Positive-semidefinite matrix domains with trace-type constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\)

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of the symmetric cost matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-at-most PSD variant and its distinction from the fixed-trace spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), let \(\mathcal B_\tau=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\operatorname{tr}(X)\le\tau\}\). Then \[\mathcal B_\tau=\tau\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{uu^{\mathsf T}:\|u\|_2=1\}\bigr)\] and, for every \(G\in\mathbb S^n\), \[\min_{X\in\mathcal B_\tau}\langle G,X\rangle=\tau\min\{\lambda_{\min}(G),0\}.\] If \(\lambda_{\min}(G)<0\), an optimizer is \(\tau uu^{\mathsf T}\) for a minimum-eigenvalue unit eigenvector \(u\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(G)>0\), the unique optimizer is \(0\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(G)=0\), the optimizers are exactly the feasible matrices whose range lies in \(\ker G\), including \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trace-bounded PSD spectrahedron is the convex hull of zero and scaled rank-one projectors; its linear minimizer is rank one only when the cost has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Bounded Spectrahedral Variant
Spectrahedral Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear minimization over the trace-bounded positive-semidefinite spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb S_+^n\) be the cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices and let \(\tau>0\). For the spectrahedron \(\mathcal D_\tau=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\operatorname{tr}(X)=\tau\}\), \[\mathcal D_\tau=\tau\operatorname{conv}\{uu^{\mathsf T}:u\in\mathbb R^n,\ \|u\|_2=1\}.\] For every symmetric cost matrix \(G\), if \(u\) is a unit eigenvector corresponding to \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\), then \(S=\tau uu^{\mathsf T}\) solves \(\min_{X\in\mathcal D_\tau}\langle G,X\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-trace spectrahedron is generated by rank-one projectors; its linear oracle requires a minimum-eigenvalue eigenvector.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\)

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite matrices with trace equal to tau

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-trace positive-semidefinite representation and minimum-eigenvector oracle are mathematically coherent, and representation is an appropriate content kind for this leaf. No supporting source reference or locator is supplied.

children.title: Singular-Vector Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Linear-minimization access through extremal singular-vector information.

assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)

notation.meaning: returned leading left and right singular vectors
operator norm of the cost matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact access to a maximizing singular-vector pair, including its nonuniqueness conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact singular-vector oracle queried with \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) returns unit vectors \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \[u^{\mathsf T}Gv=\sigma_{\max}(G)=\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}.\] The simultaneous sign change \((u,v)\mapsto(-u,-v)\) is equivalent, and the oracle may return any maximizing pair when the leading singular value is multiple. If \(G=0\), every pair of unit vectors is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular-vector oracle returns any unit left-right pair attaining the largest singular value; sign changes, multiplicity, and the zero matrix can make the response nonunique.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Singular-Vector Access Contract
Singular-Vector Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-minimization oracle for a nuclear-norm ball using leading singular vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a cost matrix \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), radius \(\tau>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Compute unit vectors \(u,v\) satisfying \(u^{\mathsf T}Gv\geq\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}-\varepsilon/\tau\), after changing one sign if necessary. Return \(S=-\tau uv^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(S\) is feasible for \(\{X:\|X\|_*\leq\tau\}\) and obeys \[\langle G,S\rangle\leq\min_{\|X\|_*\leq\tau}\langle G,X\rangle+\varepsilon.\] With \(\varepsilon=0\), leading singular vectors give an exact oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate leading singular vectors produce an additive-accuracy linear minimizer over a nuclear-norm ball.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
\(\varepsilon\geq0\)

notation.meaning: approximate leading left and right singular vectors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error calculation is coherent and algorithm is the correct role for singular-vector oracle access. The approximate singular-vector condition and resulting oracle guarantee have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Eigenvector Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Linear-minimization access through extremal eigenvector information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear minimization over a PSD trace ball, including the zero-matrix branch absent from a fixed-trace spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_{\le\tau}=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)\le\tau\}\), where \(\tau>0\). For \(G\in\mathbb S^n\), \[\min_{X\in\mathcal D_{\le\tau}}\langle G,X\rangle=\tau\min\{\lambda_{\min}(G),0\}.\] If \(\lambda_{\min}(G)<0\), a minimizer is \(\tau uu^{\mathsf T}\) for a unit minimum eigenvector \(u\); if \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\ge0\), the zero matrix is a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a PSD trace-inequality ball, the oracle uses a minimum eigenvector only when the minimum eigenvalue is negative; otherwise it returns zero.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Inequality Eigenvector Oracle
Eigenvector Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate linear minimization over a trace spectrahedron using an extreme eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(G\in\mathbb S^n\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Compute a unit vector \(u\) satisfying \(u^{\mathsf T}Gu\leq\lambda_{\min}(G)+\varepsilon/\tau\), and return \(S=\tau uu^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(S\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{tr}(S)=\tau\), and \[\langle G,S\rangle\leq\min_{X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=\tau}\langle G,X\rangle+\varepsilon.\] Thus a minimum-eigenvector routine implements the exact oracle when \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate minimum eigenvector yields an additive-accuracy linear minimizer over the fixed-trace positive-semidefinite spectrahedron.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(\varepsilon\geq0\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probability-Measure Oracle Nonattainment on an Open Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a Dirac probability-measure minimizer without compactness or an equivalent attainment assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta=(0,1)\), \(a(\theta)=\theta\), and minimize \(-\int_\Theta\theta\,d\mu(\theta)\) over Borel probability measures on \(\Theta\). The infimum is \(-1\), but every such probability measure has \(\int\theta\,d\mu<1\), so no probability measure and no Dirac atom attains the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open parameter interval, probability measures can approach but need not attain the best atom value.
assumptions_latex: \(a(\theta)=\theta\)
\(\mu\in\mathcal P(\Theta)\)
knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Measure Oracle Nonattainment on an Open Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed-measure analogue of the probability-measure barycenter interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be compact, \(\varphi\in C(\Theta)\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\mathcal M_\tau=\{\mu:\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\tau\}\). Then \[\min_{\mu\in\mathcal M_\tau}\int_\Theta\varphi\,d\mu=-\tau\|\varphi\|_\infty.\] If \(\|\varphi\|_\infty>0\) and \(\theta_*\in\arg\max_\theta|\varphi(\theta)|\), a minimizer is \(-\tau\operatorname{sgn}(\varphi(\theta_*))\delta_{\theta_*}\); if \(\varphi\equiv0\), the zero measure is a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear minimization over a signed total-variation ball selects a signed Dirac mass at a maximum-magnitude score, with the zero measure covering the identically-zero score.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact
\(\varphi\in C(\Theta)\)

notation.meaning: total-variation norm of a finite signed measure

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Variation Measure Linear Oracle
Measure Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability measures represent points in the closed convex hull of an infinite atom family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(a:\Theta\to E\) be continuous. Every probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\Theta\) defines \(x_\mu=\int_\Theta a(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta)\), and \[\{x_\mu:\mu\in\mathcal P(\Theta)\}=\operatorname{conv}(a(\Theta)).\] For a linear functional \(g\in E^*\), minimizing \(\langle g,x_\mu\rangle\) over probability measures reduces to choosing any \(\theta_*\in\arg\min_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle g,a(\theta)\rangle\) and returning the Dirac measure \(\delta_{\theta_*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barycenters of probability measures describe the convex hull of a continuous atom family, while linear minimization reduces to a Dirac atom.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact
\(E\) is finite-dimensional
\(a:\Theta\to E\) is continuous

children.title: Kernel Interfaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an exact kernel-section linear oracle on a noncompact parameter set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta=(0,1)\) and \(k(\theta,\eta)=\theta\eta\). Its RKHS consists of functions \(h_c(\eta)=c\eta\), with \(k(\theta,\cdot)=h_\theta\). For \(g=h_{-1}\), \(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle g,k(\theta,\cdot)\rangle_{\mathcal H}=\inf_{\theta\in(0,1)}(-\theta)=-1\), but no section attains this value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous kernel dictionary on an open parameter interval can have an unattained linear-oracle infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(k(\theta,\eta)=\theta\eta\)
\(g(\eta)=-\eta\) in the associated one-dimensional RKHS

notation.meaning: RKHS function eta mapped to c eta

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Oracle Nonattainment Without Compactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite coefficient storage and evaluation for points in a symmetric kernel-section hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be the RKHS of a positive-semidefinite kernel \(k\), let \(\Theta\ne\varnothing\), and let \(\mathcal D=\tau\operatorname{conv}\{\pm k(\theta,\cdot):\theta\in\Theta\}\). Every finite convex representation in \(\mathcal D\) has the form \(f=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i k(\theta_i,\cdot)\) with \(\sum_i|c_i|\le\tau\). Moreover, \(f(\theta)=\sum_i c_i k(\theta_i,\theta)\) and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H}^2=\sum_{i,j}c_ic_jk(\theta_i,\theta_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite signed mixtures of kernel sections are stored by centers and coefficients; evaluation and RKHS norm computation reduce to kernel evaluations and a Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is positive semidefinite with RKHS \(\mathcal H\)
\(\Theta\ne\varnothing\)
\(f\) has a finite convex representation in \(\mathcal D\)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Kernel-Section Expansion Interface
Kernel Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel sections form an infinite dictionary whose linear oracle is a scalar parameter search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel on a compact set \(\Theta\), with reproducing-kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and suppose \(\theta\mapsto k(\theta,\cdot)\) is norm-continuous. For \(\tau>0\), define \[\mathcal D=\tau\operatorname{conv}\{\sigma k(\theta,\cdot):\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\in\{-1,1\}\}.\] For every \(g\in\mathcal H\), a linear minimizer is \(s=-\tau\sigma_*k(\theta_*,\cdot)\), where \((\theta_*,\sigma_*)\) maximizes \(\sigma g(\theta)\). Hence kernel evaluation converts the infinite-dimensional linear oracle into optimization of \(-\tau|g(\theta)|\) over \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric convex hull of kernel sections, linear minimization selects the signed section where the current functional has largest magnitude.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact
\(k\) is positive semidefinite
\(\theta\mapsto k(\theta,\cdot)\) is norm-continuous

notation.meaning: scaled symmetric convex hull of kernel sections

Continuous-Dictionary Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-gradient access to a compact continuously parameterized atom dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional inner-product space, \(\Theta\) a compact topological space, and \(a:\Theta\to E\) continuous. For \(\mathcal D=\operatorname{conv}(a(\Theta))\) and any \(g\in E\), compactness ensures that \[\min_{s\in\mathcal D}\langle g,s\rangle=\min_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle g,a(\theta)\rangle.\] Thus a conditional-gradient linear-minimization oracle may operate directly on the parameter space: choose \(\theta_*\in\arg\min_{\theta\in\Theta}\langle g,a(\theta)\rangle\) and return the single atom \(s=a(\theta_*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear minimization over the convex hull of a compact continuous dictionary reduces to minimizing the linear score over its parameter space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compression of a finite atomic representation without changing the represented iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i a_i\), where \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), and the atoms lie in an affine subspace of dimension at most \(q<\infty\). If \(r>q+1\), affine-dependence elimination can remove a positive-weight atom while preserving the coefficient sum and barycenter. Repetition produces an exact representation of \(x\) using at most \(q+1\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine-dependence elimination compresses a finite atomic representation in affine dimension q to at most q+1 atoms without moving the represented point.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i a_i\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Finite-Support Bound in Infinite Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of dimension-independent Carathéodory compression for general infinite-dimensional atomic domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\ell_2\), let \(\mathcal A=\{e_i:i\ge1\}\) and \(x^{(m)}=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m e_i\). Then \(x^{(m)}\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), and every convex representation of \(x^{(m)}\) by atoms from \(\mathcal A\) uses exactly the atoms \(e_1,\ldots,e_m\). Thus no point-independent finite support bound exists for arbitrary infinite-dimensional atom families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The average of the first m coordinate atoms in l2 requires m support points, so unrestricted infinite-dimensional atomic hulls have no uniform finite-support bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A=\{e_i:i\ge1\}\subset\ell_2\)

Finite-Support Iterate Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support preservation for conditional-gradient iterates over an infinite atomic domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), where \(\mathcal A\) may be infinite. Suppose \(x_0\) is a convex combination of at most \(r_0\) atoms and the conditional-gradient update is \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\), with \(s_t\in\mathcal A\) and \(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\). Then \(x_t\) has a convex representation supported on at most \(r_0+t\) atoms. Equivalently, the associated atomic measure remains finitely supported, and each forward step adds at most one new support point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from finite atomic support, each conditional-gradient step adds at most one atom, so the support after t steps has size at most r0+t.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) has support size at most \(r_0\)
\(s_t\in\mathcal A\)
\(\gamma_t\in[0,1]\)

children.title: Atom-Cache Search
children.top_down_role: Reuse of stored atoms as inexpensive candidate directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cache improvement is a one-sided lower certificate for the improvement available from the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear functional \(a_t\), current point \(x_t\in D\), and nonempty finite cache \(C_t\subseteq D\), define \[m_t^C=\min_{s\in C_t}\langle a_t,s\rangle,\quad m_t^D=\inf_{s\in D}\langle a_t,s\rangle,\] \[g_t^C=\langle a_t,x_t\rangle-m_t^C,\qquad g_t^D=\langle a_t,x_t\rangle-m_t^D.\] Then \(m_t^D\leq m_t^C\), hence \(g_t^C\leq g_t^D\). Consequently, \(g_t^C\geq\eta\) certifies \(g_t^D\geq\eta\). No nonnegativity of \(g_t^C\) follows unless the cache contains a point whose linear value is no greater than that of \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best cached improvement cannot exceed the full feasible-set improvement, so passing a cache threshold is valid, although the cached gap may be negative.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is nonempty}.
\varnothing\ne C_t\subseteq D\text{ is finite}.
x_t\in D.
m_t^D\text{ is finite}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cache Rejection Is Not a Full-Oracle Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of cache rejection to certify absence of a useful uncached atom.

Thus for every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(g_t^C<\eta\) while \(g_t^D>\eta\). A failed cache test can trigger broader search or a full oracle call, but cannot certify that no sufficiently improving feasible atom exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cache may fail its threshold even though an uncached feasible atom offers substantially greater improvement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold guarantee when the best cached atom is found only approximately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in D\), let \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq D\) be finite, and suppose \(\widehat s\in C\) satisfies \[\langle a,\widehat s\rangle\leq\min_{s\in C}\langle a,s\rangle+\epsilon_C.\] Define \(\widehat g_C=\langle a,x-\widehat s\rangle\), \(g_C=\langle a,x\rangle-\min_{s\in C}\langle a,s\rangle\), and \(g_D=\langle a,x\rangle-\inf_{s\in D}\langle a,s\rangle\). Then \[g_C-\epsilon_C\leq\widehat g_C\leq g_C\leq g_D.\] Hence \(\widehat g_C\geq\eta\) certifies \(g_D\geq\eta\), whereas \(\widehat g_C<\eta\) is inconclusive for \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximately best cached atom gives a valid one-sided global improvement certificate with quantified cache-scan loss.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{s_1,\ldots,s_m\}\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty finite cache. An exhaustive scan for \(s^C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle a,s\rangle\) evaluates \(m\) pairings and uses at most \(m-1\) value comparisons. With dense vectors and unit-cost scalar arithmetic, the scan costs \(O(md)\) arithmetic and dense cache storage costs \(O(md)\). The scan itself issues no external linear-minimization-oracle request.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cached atoms provide inexpensive candidate directions before a full linear-oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact feasible set \(D\), a finite cache \(C_t\subseteq D\), cost vector \(g_t\), and acceptance tolerance \(\eta_t\geq0\), compute \(s_t^C\in\arg\min_{s\in C_t}\langle g_t,s\rangle\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any cache-first routine that invokes a full linear-minimization oracle whenever no cached point meets its threshold, and without assumptions linking future query directions to cached atoms, query sequences may make every cache test fail. No recurrence, distributional, or geometric assumption links successive queries to the cache.

review_flags: A quantitative saving requires additional assumptions or a named method-specific analysis.
knowledge_statements.title: No Universal Full-Oracle Saving from Lazy Branching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-separation branching when the fallback linear oracle is additively approximate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_D(g,x)=\sup_{v\in D}\langle g,x-v\rangle\). Suppose an additive \(\delta\)-LMO returns \(s_\delta\in D\) with \[\langle g,s_\delta\rangle\leq\inf_{v\in D}\langle g,v\rangle+\delta,\] and put \(\widehat G=\langle g,x-s_\delta\rangle\). Then \[G_D(g,x)-\delta\leq\widehat G\leq G_D(g,x).\] For \(\tau>0\), if \(\widehat G\geq\tau\), return \(s_\delta\) as an improving atom; if \(\widehat G<\tau-\delta\), certify \(G_D(g,x)<\tau\); otherwise refine the response or use another oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate LMO supports positive and negative weak-separation decisions outside an uncertainty band of width delta.
assumptions_latex: x\in D.
\tau>0.
\delta\geq0.
\inf_{v\in D}\langle g,v\rangle\text{ is finite}.
s_\delta\text{ is an additive }\delta\text{-LMO response}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_D(g,x)-\delta\leq\widehat G\leq G_D(g,x),\text{ with uncertainty band }[\tau-\delta,\tau).

notation.meaning: Improvement reported by the approximate LMO

review_flags: This trichotomy does not prescribe a refinement schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-LMO Weak-Separation Trichotomy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-or-negative weak separation with an explicit boundary convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in D\), linear functional \(g\), and threshold \(\tau>0\), define \(G_D(g,x)=\sup_{v\in D}\langle g,x-v\rangle\). An exact weak-separation call must return either (i) a point \(s\in D\) satisfying \(\langle g,x-s\rangle\geq\tau\), or (ii) the certificate \(G_D(g,x)<\tau\). Equality belongs to the positive branch. When the linear minimum is attained, one exact LMO call realizes this interface by testing an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact weak separation either returns a feasible atom meeting the threshold or certifies that the full-domain gap is strictly below it.
assumptions_latex: x\in D.
\tau>0.
G_D(g,x)\text{ is finite}.
The one-call realization additionally assumes attainment of the queried linear minimum.
review_flags: Other sources may assign equality to a different branch; this record fixes the convention explicitly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected exact positive-or-negative weak-separation interface; supersedes the prior version that allowed an unattained threshold supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in D\), a linear functional \(g\), and \(\tau>0\), let \(G_D(g,x)=\sup_{v\in D}\langle g,x-v\rangle\). Assume this supremum is finite and attained. An exact weak-separation call returns either (i) \(s\in D\) with \(\langle g,x-s\rangle\geq\tau\), or (ii) the certificate \(G_D(g,x)<\tau\). Equality belongs to the positive branch. An exact linear-minimization oracle realizes the interface by testing an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With attainment, exact weak separation returns an atom meeting the threshold or certifies that the full-domain gap is strictly smaller.
assumptions_latex: x\in D.
\tau>0.
G_D(g,x)<\infty.
\sup_{v\in D}\langle g,x-v\rangle\text{ is attained}.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Weak-Separation Interface with Attainment
Lazy Weak Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak separation accepts a sufficient cached improvement and calls exact minimization only when necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_t\in D\), cost vector \(g_t\), target gap \(\Phi_t>0\), weakness parameter \(K\geq1\), and cached candidates \(C_t\subseteq D\), search for \(s\in C_t\) satisfying \(\langle g_t,x_t-s\rangle\geq\Phi_t/K\). If found, return \(s\). Otherwise call an exact linear-minimization oracle to obtain \(v_t\in\arg\min_{v\in D}\langle g_t,v\rangle\). Return \(v_t\) if its gap is at least \(\Phi_t/K\); if not, return the certificate \(\max_{v\in D}\langle g_t,x_t-v\rangle<\Phi_t/K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak-separation routine reuses cached directions meeting a gap threshold and invokes exact linear minimization only when cache search fails.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is compact and nonempty
\(x_t\in D\)
\(\Phi_t>0\) and \(K\geq1\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated branching logic is internally plausible and algorithm fits the leaf, but weak-separation threshold and certificate conventions vary and require a matching source. No citation or locator is supplied, and the ambient space for \(g_t\) and the pairing is not specified.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected form of the interface because its strict negative branch and equality convention are not exhaustive without attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: G_D(g,x)<\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\bigl[\exists s\in D:\langle g,x-s\rangle\geq\tau\bigr]\ \lor\ \bigl[G_D(g,x)<\tau\bigr].

\tau>0.
G_D(g,x)<\infty.

children.title: Linear-Oracle Warm Starting
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior oracle state across related linear subproblems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm Starting Does Not Imply a Universal Speedup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates preservation of oracle validity from solver-dependent computational improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reusing internal state from the solve for g_t when solving \min_{s\in D}\langle g_{t+1},s\rangle preserves the outer method's guarantees if the returned point independently satisfies the prescribed oracle condition for g_{t+1}. Without assumptions relating the successive costs, retained state, and internal solver, no reduction in iterations, work, or time follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starting is correctness-neutral after revalidation, but it has no solver-independent speedup guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The returned atom satisfies the current feasibility and oracle-accuracy requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{current oracle validity is preserved; computational speedup is not implied}\)
knowledge_statements.title: Warm Starting Does Not Imply a Universal Speedup
Linear-Oracle Warm Starting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable internal oracle state may accelerate consecutive linear subproblems without changing their validity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let the linear oracle solve \(\min_{s\in D}\langle g_t,s\rangle\) using internal state \(z_t\). A warm-started implementation initializes the next solve at \(z_t\) rather than a fixed default and returns \(s_{t+1}\in D\). The returned point is valid only if it independently satisfies the required oracle condition, for example \[\langle g_{t+1},s_{t+1}\rangle\leq\min_{s\in D}\langle g_{t+1},s\rangle+\varepsilon_{t+1}.\] Reusing \(z_t\) changes computational work but does not relax feasibility or the prescribed accuracy for the new cost vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize each linear-oracle solve from prior internal state, but certify the same feasibility and accuracy required for the new linear objective.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonempty
\(g_t\) and \(g_{t+1}\) define successive linear subproblems
\(\varepsilon_{t+1}\geq0\)

notation.meaning: reusable internal state of the oracle solver

children.title: Active-Set Management
children.top_down_role: Representation maintenance mechanisms shared across active-set variants.

children.title: Active-Atom Removal Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for discarding inactive, negligible, or redundant atoms.

children.title: Inactivity-Based Atom Pruning
children.top_down_role: Pruning policies based on sustained inactivity within the active representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-based candidate selection for active-set reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an inactivity horizon \(L\). An atom that has not been selected or had its maintained coefficient explicitly modified during the last \(L\) iterations may be nominated for removal. Inactivity is only a trigger: deletion is exact without re-representation when its maintained coefficient is zero; deletion of a positive-weight atom requires a separate certified representation-preserving operation, and otherwise changes the maintained iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inactivity policy nominates long-unused atoms, but inactivity alone does not make a positive-weight atom safe to delete.
assumptions_latex: A finite atomic convex representation is maintained.
The usage history and current coefficients are available.
Exact preservation is distinguished from heuristic approximate pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactivity-Triggered Pruning Policy
Inactivity-Based Atom Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inactivity alone does not certify that deleting a positive-weight atom preserves the represented iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a maintained representation be \(x=\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i a_i\), where \(\alpha_i\geq0\), \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and an atom is called inactive when it has not been selected or reweighted for \(L\) iterations. Deleting an inactive atom \(a_j\) with \(\alpha_j>0\) and merely renormalizing the remaining coefficients generally changes \(x\). For example, with \(a_1=0\), \(a_2=1\), and \(x=(a_1+a_2)/2\), deleting either atom changes the represented point. Exact pruning is safe only when the removed contribution is zero or an alternative convex representation of the same \(x\) is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A long-unused atom can still carry essential positive weight; deleting it is unsafe unless the iterate is exactly re-represented or its contribution is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i a_i\) is the maintained convex representation
\(\alpha_j>0\)
inactivity records usage history only

notation.meaning: maintained convex coefficient of atom i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that inactivity alone does not permit exact deletion, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. The claimed safety condition must say that the removed coefficient is zero, not merely that the vector contribution is zero: an atom \(a_j=0\) with positive coefficient can have zero vector contribution while renormalizing the remaining coefficients still changes the represented point. No source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Negligible-Weight Atom Removal
children.top_down_role: Removal policies for atoms whose representation weights have become negligible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-atom family attaining the uniform displacement bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{u,v\}\), where \(\lVert u-v\rVert=D\), and let \(x=(1-\rho)u+\rho v\) with \(0<\rho<1\). Removing \(v\) gives \(x^+=u\) and \(\lVert x^+-x\rVert=\rho D\). Hence no bound \(\lVert x^+-x\rVert\le c\rho D\) with a universal \(c<1\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-atom segment attains the removed-mass diameter bound exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert u-v\rVert=D>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Diameter Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact barycentric identity and sharp diameter certificate for negligible-weight deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\rho=\sum_{i\in R}\alpha_i<1\), define \(x^+=(1-\rho)^{-1}\sum_{i\notin R}\alpha_i v_i\) and \(x_R=\rho^{-1}\sum_{i\in R}\alpha_i v_i\). Then \(x=(1-\rho)x^++\rho x_R\), so \(x^+-x=\rho(x^+-x_R)\). If the atoms lie in a set of diameter \(D\), then \(\lVert x^+-x\rVert\le \rho D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement equals the discarded mass times the separation between the retained and discarded barycenters, and is at most the discarded mass times the atom-set diameter.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i v_i\) is a finite convex representation.
\(0<\rho=\sum_{i\in R}\alpha_i<1\).
The atoms lie in a set of finite diameter \(D\) in the chosen norm.
review_flags: This sharpens the valid but looser deferred-seed certificate involving \(\rho D/(1-\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Removal Displacement Identity
Negligible-Weight Atom Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold rule for pruning a convex active-set representation with controlled point perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) have diameter \(D<\infty\), and let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i v_i\) with \(v_i\in C\), \(\alpha_i\ge 0\), and \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\). For a removal set \(R\), put \(\rho=\sum_{i\in R}\alpha_i<1\) and \(x^+=(1-\rho)^{-1}\sum_{i\notin R}\alpha_i v_i\). The atoms in \(R\) are negligible at tolerance \(\varepsilon_x\) whenever \(\rho D/(1-\rho)\le\varepsilon_x\); then \(\lVert x^+-x\rVert\le\varepsilon_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove atoms whose total weight is small enough that renormalizing the retained convex combination moves the represented point by at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and has finite diameter \(D\).
\(x\) is represented by finitely many atoms with convex weights.

notation.meaning: Set of active atoms selected for removal.
Total convex weight assigned to removed atoms.
Diameter of the feasible set in the chosen norm.

Exact perturbation threshold requires source certification.

children.title: Redundancy-Based Atom Elimination
children.top_down_role: Elimination of atoms whose contribution is duplicated by the retained representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic test for point-preserving elimination from a positive-support representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i v_i\) with \(\alpha_i>0\), let \(\widetilde A=[(v_1,1)\ \cdots\ (v_m,1)]\). A point-preserving feasible weight shift can eliminate a support atom if and only if \(\ker\widetilde A\ne\{0\}\). Equivalently, the positive support is irreducible by affine-dependence pivots if and only if \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\) are affinely independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-support representation is exactly reducible precisely when its augmented atom matrix has a nonzero null vector.
assumptions_latex: The listed support is finite.
Every listed weight is strictly positive.

notation.meaning: Augmented atom matrix whose nullspace contains affine dependences.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Support Affine-Independence Criterion
Redundancy-Based Atom Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of an affinely redundant atom from the positive support of a finite convex representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i v_i\), where \(\alpha_i>0\) for every \(i\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i=1\). If a nonzero vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \(\sum_{i=1}^m c_i v_i=0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^m c_i=0\), choose its sign so that some \(c_i>0\), set \(t=\min_{i:c_i>0}\alpha_i/c_i\), and define \(\alpha_i^+=\alpha_i-tc_i\). Then \(\alpha_i^+\ge0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i^+=1\), \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i^+v_i\), and \(\alpha_j^+=0\) for at least one index \(j\) with \(\alpha_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine dependence among positive-support active atoms permits a weight shift that preserves the represented point while driving at least one positive weight to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has a finite convex representation whose listed active weights are strictly positive.
The listed atoms admit a nonzero affine dependence \(c\).

notation.meaning: Largest feasible step along the chosen weight direction.

review_flags: A specific Carathéodory or affine-dependence elimination source and locator remain required.

children.title: Removal-Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where aggressive removal can damage representation quality or later progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes current-point control from preservation of future active-hull corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S'\subseteq S\), then \(\operatorname{conv}S'\subseteq\operatorname{conv}S\) and \(\inf_{z\in\operatorname{conv}S'}f(z)\ge\inf_{z\in\operatorname{conv}S}f(z)\). The hulls are equal if and only if every deleted atom lies in \(\operatorname{conv}S'\). Small current-point displacement does not ensure this: for \(S=\{0,1\}\), \(x=\rho\) with representation \(x=(1-\rho)0+\rho1\), and \(f(z)=(z-1)^2\), deleting atom \(1\) moves the point only by \(\rho\), but changes the restricted optimum from \(0\) to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deletion can barely move the current point while destroying a useful future correction direction; hull preservation requires convex-hull redundancy of every deleted atom.
assumptions_latex: \(S'\subseteq S\) are finite atom sets.
The comparison uses optimization over their convex hulls.
In the counterexample, \(0<\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{z\in\operatorname{conv}S'}f(z)\ge\inf_{z\in\operatorname{conv}S}f(z)\), with hull equality exactly when \(S\setminus S'\subseteq\operatorname{conv}S'\).
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Hull Loss Boundary
Removal-Safety Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating safe approximate deletion from uncontrolled objective degradation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L_0\)-Lipschitz on a convex set \(C\), and let removal followed by renormalization replace \(x\) by \(x^+\). If \(\lVert x^+-x\rVert\le\varepsilon_x\), then \(f(x^+)\le f(x)+L_0\varepsilon_x\). Without a finite Lipschitz bound on the region joining \(x\) and \(x^+\), a small removed weight alone does not uniformly bound objective increase; likewise, deleting all positive weight makes renormalization undefined. Thus safe removal requires both \(\rho<1\) and a certified displacement-to-objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removal is safe only when retained weight remains positive and the induced displacement has a certified objective effect; small discarded weight alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and contains \(x\) and \(x^+\).
\(f\) is \(L_0\)-Lipschitz on the segment joining the two points.

notation.meaning: Objective Lipschitz constant on the relevant region.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses removal-safety guarantees.
Failure boundary combines standard Lipschitz control with active-set renormalization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Lipschitz implication and the renormalization boundary are coherent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but no source with a specific locator supports the combined safety claim.

children.title: Active-Set Compression
children.top_down_role: Exact and approximate reduction of maintained representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-free approximate compression in Hilbert geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_i\alpha_i v_i\) and suppose the atoms have diameter at most \(D\) in a Hilbert norm. Draw \(V_1,\ldots,V_k\) independently with \(\Pr(V_j=v_i)=\alpha_i\), and set \(\widehat x_k=k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^kV_j\). Then \(\mathbb E\widehat x_k=x\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert\widehat x_k-x\rVert^2\le D^2/(2k)\). Consequently, some convex combination supported on at most \(k\) original atoms satisfies \(\lVert\widehat x_k-x\rVert\le D/\sqrt{2k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling atoms according to their current weights yields a dimension-free approximate representation with inverse-square-root support error.
assumptions_latex: The norm is induced by a Hilbert-space inner product.
The atom set has finite diameter \(D\).
\(x\) has a finite convex representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\widehat x_k\text{ supported on at most }k\text{ atoms with }\lVert\widehat x_k-x\rVert\le D/\sqrt{2k}.\)

notation.meaning: Number of sampled atoms before repetitions are aggregated.
Empirical barycenter used as the compressed point.

review_flags: Standard approximate Carathéodory or Maurey-type sampling statement; no locator supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Carathéodory Compression
Active-Set Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or tolerance-controlled reduction of a maintained convex atomic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb{R}^d\), let \(\alpha_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i=1\), and let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i v_i\). An \(\varepsilon\)-compressed representation of \(x\), for \(\varepsilon\ge0\), consists of a set \(S\subseteq\{1,[0m\ldots,m\}\) and weights \(\beta_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in S}\beta_i=1\) and \(\left\lVert x-\sum_{i\in S}\beta_i v_i\right\rVert\le\varepsilon\). Compression replaces the stored representation by such a pair \((S,\beta)\) with fewer retained atoms. When \(\varepsilon=0\), affine-dependence elimination can produce an exact representation with \(\lvert S\rvert\le d+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed active representation is a smaller convex combination that preserves the represented point exactly or within a declared tolerance; in finite dimension, an exact representation can use at most d plus one atoms.
assumptions_latex: The maintained point has a finite convex atomic representation in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
The compression tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compressed point \(\widehat{x}=\sum_{i\in S}\beta_i v_i\) satisfies \(\lVert x-\widehat{x}\rVert\le\varepsilon\); for \(\varepsilon=0\), an exact choice with \(\lvert S\rvert\le d+1\) exists.
review_flags: A specific Carathéodory theorem locator is required for the exact cardinality guarantee.

children.title: Correction-Subproblem Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces for optimization over the active hull.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable first-order acceptance certificate for convex active-hull correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\beta\in\Delta_m\), let \(g=A^\top\nabla f(A\beta)\) and \(r(\beta)=\langle g,\beta\rangle-\min_i g_i=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}\langle g,\beta-\lambda\rangle\). If \(f\) is convex and differentiable on the active hull, then \(f(A\beta)-\min_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}f(A\lambda)\le r(\beta)\). Thus \(r(\beta)\le\eta\) certifies an \(\eta\)-correction, and \(r(\beta)=0\) is equivalent to exact active-hull optimality. Without convexity, zero residual certifies only first-order stationarity on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gap between the weighted gradient value and its smallest active-atom component certifies correction accuracy for a convex objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on the active hull.
\(\beta\in\Delta_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(A\beta)-\min_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}f(A\lambda)\le r(\beta)\), and \(r(\beta)=0\) exactly characterizes active-hull optimality.

notation.meaning: Gradient of the weight-space objective at \(\beta\).

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Correction Residual
Correction-Subproblem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-output contract for a solver optimizing the objective over the current active hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(A=(v_1,[0m\ldots,v_m)\) contain atoms \(v_i\in C\), and define \(\Delta_m=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\}\). Given current weights \(\alpha\in\Delta_m\) and a tolerance \(\eta\ge0\), a correction solver satisfies the interface when it returns \(\beta\in\Delta_m\) such that \(f(A\beta)-\min_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}f(A\lambda)\le\eta\). The outer method may then set \(x^+=A\beta\) and remove atoms with zero returned weight. Exact correction corresponds to \(\eta=0\), while partial correction uses a certified positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction-solver interface accepts the current active hull and returns feasible weights whose objective is within a declared tolerance of the hull-restricted optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
Every column of \(A\) belongs to \(C\).
The requested tolerance satisfies \(\eta\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Matrix or linear map whose columns are active atoms.
