children.title: First-Order Evaluation Cost
children.top_down_role: Accounting for objective and gradient information.

children.title: Objective-Evaluation Cost
children.top_down_role: Computational expense attributable to obtaining objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteration Count Does Not Determine Objective-Evaluation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of transferring accepted-update complexity to value-oracle complexity without an evaluation policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed number \(T\) of accepted updates, an implementation using no value-based test may make zero objective calls, whereas a trial-based implementation may make arbitrarily many rejected trial evaluations if no per-update trial bound is imposed. Hence \(T\) alone gives no finite upper bound on \(N_f\) without declared line-search, stopping-test, and internal-solver accounting rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same update count can entail zero or arbitrarily many objective calls, so objective complexity requires an explicit evaluation policy.
assumptions_latex: Rejected trials are not accepted outer updates.
No uniform bound on trial evaluations is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ alone does not determine or upper-bound }N_f.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Count Does Not Determine Objective-Evaluation Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-evaluation count induced by value-based step acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose accepted outer iteration \(t\) tests \(k_t\ge1\) trial points and each test requests one uncached objective value. If the initial value is already cached and no other objective requests occur, then after \(T\) accepted iterations \[N_f=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}k_t.\] Thus one-shot testing gives \(N_f=T\), while backtracking can give \(N_f>T\). An open-loop implementation making no value-based tests can instead have \(N_f=0\) for \(T>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-call complexity depends on step selection: one-shot testing uses one value per update, backtracking can use several, and open-loop steps can use none.
assumptions_latex: Every tested trial value is uncached and charged once.
No additional objective requests occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_f=\sum_{t<T}k_t\text{ for the stated trial-based policy, while }N_f=0\text{ is possible under open-loop steps.}

notation.meaning: Number of objective-valued trial points at accepted iteration t.

knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Point Objective-Call Decomposition
Objective-Evaluation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate accounting unit for calls returning objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution producing query points \(z_1,\ldots,z_q\), define the objective-evaluation cost by \(N_f=\#\{j: f(z_j)\text{ is requested and not already available from a cached joint evaluation}\}\). If evaluation costs depend on the point or requested accuracy, define the weighted cost \(T_f=\sum_{j\in J_f}c_f(z_j,\tau_j)\), where \(J_f\) indexes uncached objective requests and \(\tau_j\) is their accuracy. Line-search trial values and correction-solver calls are included unless explicitly assigned to another cost category.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-evaluation cost counts uncached requests for function values, including line-search and correction calls unless the accounting convention separates them.
assumptions_latex: An execution trace distinguishes requested, cached, and jointly returned values.
Each inexact request has a declared accuracy parameter when weighted cost is used.
review_flags: No supplied locator defines this multi-oracle accounting convention.
Treatment of internal solver calls must be standardized.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the cost leaf, but inclusion of line-search and correction-solver requests is a convention that lacks a cited source and inspectable locator.

children.title: Gradient-Evaluation Cost
children.top_down_role: Computational expense attributable to obtaining gradient information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Call Count Does Not Determine Evaluation Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between nominal gradient-query complexity and implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-call count represents work up to constants only under uniform per-call cost bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every charged gradient request has a finite nonnegative implementation cost.

notation.meaning: Implementation cost of the j-th charged gradient request.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Call Count Does Not Determine Evaluation Work
Gradient-Evaluation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate accounting unit for first-order oracle calls returning gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient cost counts uncached gradient requests; reusing a stored gradient does not add an oracle call, though it may add arithmetic work.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at every queried point.
The execution trace identifies cached and joint first-order evaluations.
review_flags: No supplied locator defines gradient-call accounting for conditional-gradient implementations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the cost leaf, but cache and joint-call treatment is an unsupported accounting convention without a cited locator.

children.title: Shared Evaluation Reuse
children.top_down_role: Cost reductions available when objective and gradient computations share intermediate work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost condition for retaining semantically valid shared intermediate state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over a common horizon, suppose retaining shared state costs \(c_{\mathrm{store}}\), later reuse costs \(c_{\mathrm{reuse}}\), and recomputing the required value-gradient information costs \(c_{\mathrm{recomp}}\). Under additive accounting and valid cache semantics, retention is cheaper exactly when \[c_{\mathrm{store}}+c_{\mathrm{reuse}}<c_{\mathrm{recomp}}.\] Equality makes the choices cost-equivalent; semantic invalidity precludes reuse regardless of cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid shared state is worth retaining when storage plus reuse costs less than recomputation; cost savings cannot override invalid cache semantics.
assumptions_latex: Cached and recomputed outputs are semantically interchangeable for the algorithm.
All costs use the same additive price model and horizon.

notation.meaning: Cost of retaining the shared intermediate state over the comparison horizon.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Benefit Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which stored first-order information is semantically reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached output may replace a requested evaluation only when the evaluation point, objective instance, derivative convention, requested accuracy, and all deterministic oracle parameters agree. For a stochastic oracle, a stored realization is not a fresh independent response and may alter conditional independence or variance assumptions. Reuse is therefore valid only when the algorithm permits the same stored realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cached information is reusable only under matching query semantics; a stored stochastic sample is not a fresh independent oracle response.
assumptions_latex: The query specification includes every parameter affecting output value, accuracy, or distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Matching the evaluation point alone is insufficient for semantic cache validity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Validity Boundary
Shared Evaluation Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-double-counting rule for cached or jointly computed objective and gradient information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint value-gradient call contributes to both logical counts but only one physical event; later reuse of cached outputs adds no oracle call.
assumptions_latex: Cached outputs remain valid only for the identical evaluation point and oracle parameters.
The accounting distinguishes logical outputs from physical evaluation events.
review_flags: No supplied locator establishes the logical-versus-physical counting convention.
Cache-validity conventions need explicit source support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical-versus-physical counting identity is internally consistent and property fits the leaf, but the cache-validity and joint-evaluation convention has no cited source.

children.title: Linear-Oracle Cost
children.top_down_role: Accounting for exact, approximate, cached, and block linear minimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nominal Call Counts Do Not Determine Precision-Weighted Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal linear-oracle call counts can conceal arbitrarily different costs when response cost depends on requested accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an approximate linear-oracle response requested at tolerance \(\delta\in(0,1]\) has implementation cost at least \(c(\delta)\), where \(c(\delta)\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). Two executions making the same number \(N\) of oracle calls can then have arbitrarily different total work: one may use \(\delta_t=1\), while another uses tolerances with \(\sum_{t=1}^N c(\delta_t)\) arbitrarily large. Hence \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) alone does not bound precision-weighted work without a tolerance-cost law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same number of linear-oracle calls can represent arbitrarily different work when accurate responses become increasingly expensive.
assumptions_latex: c:(0,1]\to[0,\infty)\text{ satisfies }c(\delta)\to\infty\text{ as }\delta\downarrow0.
Both executions make the same positive number N of actual oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{LMO}}\text{ alone does not upper-bound }\sum_{t=1}^N c(\delta_t).

notation.meaning: Implementation cost of an oracle response at tolerance delta
Nominal number of actual linear-oracle calls

review_flags: This is a conditional accounting boundary; a concrete implementation must supply its own tolerance-cost law.
knowledge_statements.title: Nominal Call Counts Do Not Determine Precision-Weighted Work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which reuse of a stored atom is excluded from the linear-oracle call count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached atom may be excluded from \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) only when no external linear-optimization request is issued and it is checked using already available data. If validation invokes the oracle, that invocation belongs to \(J_{\mathrm{LMO}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cache hit costs zero linear-oracle calls only when validation does not invoke that oracle.
assumptions_latex: The model distinguishes local cache operations from external linear-optimization requests.
A declared acceptance test determines whether a cached atom is usable.
review_flags: Local cache-search arithmetic remains a separate implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Cache-Hit Accounting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block Call Counts Require a Normalization Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity of linear-oracle counts when one request may solve one block or several blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let request \(t\) query a nonempty block set \(B_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Charging each request once gives \(N_{\mathrm{req}}=\sum_t1\), whereas charging each queried block gives \(N_{\mathrm{blk}}=\sum_t|B_t|\). Consequently, \[N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\mathrm{blk}}\leq mN_{\mathrm{req}}.\] Block-LMO complexity is therefore incomparable across implementations unless the atomic charging convention is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-block request may count as one request or several block calls, so block-oracle complexity requires an explicit atomic unit.
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\ne B_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ for every counted request }t.
m\geq1.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Call Counts Require a Normalization Convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified request, work, cache, precision, and block accounting for linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For requests indexed by \(t\), let \(J_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) contain exactly those indices at which an external linear-optimization oracle is invoked. A request specifies direction \(g_t\), tolerance \(\delta_t\geq0\), and nonempty queried block set \(B_t\). Define request count \(N_{\mathrm{req}}=|J_{\mathrm{LMO}}|\), block-normalized count \(N_{\mathrm{blk}}=\sum_{t\in J_{\mathrm{LMO}}}|B_t|\), and total implementation work \[T_{\mathrm{tot}}=T_{\mathrm{cache}}+T_{\mathrm{maint}}+\sum_{t\in J_{\mathrm{LMO}}}c_{\mathrm{resp}}(g_t,\delta_t,B_t;\mathcal R).\] Here \(\mathcal R\) fixes the representation and computational model. Exact calls have \(\delta_t=0\); validated cache hits issue no external request and contribute only their local search or validation work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete LMO ledger separately records external requests, queried blocks, tolerance-dependent response work, and local cache or maintenance work.
assumptions_latex: The atomic request and block charging conventions are declared.
c_{\mathrm{resp}}\text{ is defined under a fixed representation and implementation model }\mathcal R.
Cache hits are excluded from }J_{\mathrm{LMO}}\text{ only when validation makes no external LMO request}.

notation.meaning: Indices of actual external LMO invocations

review_flags: The ledger is a convention; concrete complexity requires a specified response-cost law.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Oracle Cost Ledger
Linear-Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified accounting for exact, approximate, cached, and block linear minimization calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), a linear minimization request with direction \(g_t\) and tolerance \(\delta_t\ge0\) returns \(s_t\in C\) satisfying \(\langle g_t,s_t\rangle\le\inf_{s\in C}\langle g_t,s\rangle+\delta_t\). Let \(J_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) contain requests actually sent to an oracle; cache hits are excluded. Define \(N_{\mathrm{LMO}}=\lvert J_{\mathrm{LMO}}\rvert\) and \(T_{\mathrm{LMO}}=\sum_{t\in J_{\mathrm{LMO}}}c_{\mathrm{LMO}}(g_t,\delta_t,B_t)\), where \(B_t\) identifies the queried block; an exact call has \(\delta_t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-oracle cost counts actual exact, approximate, or block oracle requests, excluding certified cache hits and optionally weighting calls by tolerance and block.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and each stated linear infimum is finite.
Every approximate response carries a declared additive tolerance.
Cache hits satisfy the same acceptance test used for fresh responses.

notation.meaning: Additive linear-oracle accuracy at iteration t.
Block or component queried by the oracle.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses linear minimization oracle accounting.
Approximate and cached-call conventions require a conditional-gradient source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the topic and the additive approximate-LMO condition is precise, but exact, approximate, cached, and block-call accounting is unsupported by any cited locator.

children.title: Active-Representation Maintenance Cost
children.top_down_role: Accounting for active-hull solves and representation maintenance.

children.title: Correction-Subproblem Cost
children.top_down_role: Computational expense of optimization over the current active representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-specific cost for projected gradient on a smooth convex active-hull objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_t(\lambda)=f(A_t\lambda)\) be convex with \(L_{\phi,t}\)-Lipschitz gradient on \(\Delta_{m_t}\). Projected gradient with step \(1/L_{\phi,t}\) satisfies \(\phi_t(\lambda_t^k)-\phi_t(\lambda_t^*)\le L_{\phi,t}\lVert\lambda_t^0-\lambda_t^*\rVert_2^2/(2k)\). Therefore \(I_t(\eta_t)=\left\lceil L_{\phi,t}\lVert\lambda_t^0-\lambda_t^*\rVert_2^2/(2\eta_t)\right\rceil\) iterations suffice for \(\eta_t>0\). If a gradient costs \(c_t^g\) operations and comparison-based Euclidean simplex projection costs \(O(m_t\log m_t)\), the call costs \(O(I_t(\eta_t)(c_t^g+m_t\log m_t))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth convex projected-gradient correction needs order \(L_\phi/\eta\) inner steps, each paying for an active-weight gradient and simplex projection.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_t\) is convex with \(L_{\phi,t}\)-Lipschitz gradient on the simplex.
Projected gradient uses step \(1/L_{\phi,t}\).
The target tolerance satisfies \(\eta_t>0\).
The stated arithmetic specialization uses comparison-based Euclidean simplex projection.

notation.meaning: Smoothness constant of the weight-space objective.

review_flags: Faster simplex-projection implementations may replace the displayed projection term.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Correction Cost
Correction-Subproblem Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for solving the active-hull correction problem to prescribed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For active-set size \(m_t\), let a correction solver require \(I_t(\eta_t)\) inner iterations to return \(\beta_t\in\Delta_{m_t}\) with \(f(A_t\beta_t)-\inf_{\lambda\in\Delta_{m_t}}f(A_t\lambda)\le\eta_t\). If one inner iteration uses at most \(c_t^{\mathrm{iter}}\) arithmetic operations and \(q_t^f,q_t^g\) objective and gradient evaluations, then over outer iterations \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), correction work is at most \(\sum_t I_t(\eta_t)c_t^{\mathrm{iter}}\), with corresponding evaluation counts bounded by \(\sum_t I_t(\eta_t)q_t^f\) and \(\sum_t I_t(\eta_t)q_t^g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total correction cost is the sum of inner-solver iterations times their per-iteration arithmetic and oracle costs at each requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Each correction call has a certified tolerance \(\eta_t\).
Uniform per-inner-iteration cost bounds are available for each outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{corr}}\le\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}I_t(\eta_t)c_t^{\mathrm{iter}}\), with analogous summed bounds for objective and gradient calls.

notation.meaning: Inner iterations needed for the requested correction accuracy.
Active-set size at outer iteration t.

review_flags: This is a compositional accounting bound, not a solver-specific rate.
No supplied locator supports correction-subproblem complexity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compositional bound is internally valid under the stated per-iteration bounds and complexity_bound fits the cost leaf, but no source supports the correction-cost model or its oracle accounting.

children.title: Active-Representation Storage Cost
children.top_down_role: Memory expense associated with retained atoms, coefficients, and auxiliary state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peak live storage under dense, sparse, and reconstructible atom encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If at most \(m_t\) atoms are active, each atom encoding uses at most \(s_t\) words, each weight and its metadata use \(O(1)\) words, and maintenance uses at most \(w_t\) temporary words, then \(M_t^{\mathrm{peak}}=O(m_t(s_t+1)+w_t)\). Dense atoms in \(\mathbb R^d\) give \(O(m_td+w_t)\); atoms with at most \(q\) stored nonzeros give \(O(m_t(q+1)+w_t)\); and constant-word identifiers with shared reconstruction state of size \(s_0\) give \(O(m_t+s_0+w_t)\). Identifier storage does not include reconstruction arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peak storage equals active-set size times the selected atom encoding plus weights, metadata, shared state, and temporary workspace.
assumptions_latex: At most \(m_t\) atoms are simultaneously active.
One atom encoding uses at most \(s_t\) words and per-atom weight and metadata use \(O(1)\) words.
Maintenance uses at most \(w_t\) additional simultaneously live words.

notation.meaning: Words used by one stored atom encoding.

review_flags: The bounds are conditional on the declared machine-word encoding and live-state model.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Dependent Peak Storage
Active-Representation Storage Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory required to store active atoms, weights, and optional cached metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_t\) atoms be active at iteration \(t\). If one explicitly stored atom requires \(s_v\) machine words, each weight requires one word, and cached metadata requires \(s_i\) words per atom plus \(s_0\) global words, then active-representation storage is \(M_t=m_t(s_v+1+s_i)+s_0\) words. Hence \(M_t=O(m_t(s_v+s_i+1))\). If atoms are stored by identifiers from which they can be reconstructed, replace \(s_v\) by the identifier and reconstruction-state storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Storage grows linearly with active-set size times the per-atom representation, weight, and metadata footprint, unless atoms are stored implicitly.
assumptions_latex: The representation stores \(m_t\) active atoms and one scalar weight per atom.
Per-atom and global metadata footprints are bounded by \(s_i\) and \(s_0\).

notation.meaning: Number of active atoms at iteration t.
Machine words needed to store one atom or its identifier.

review_flags: No supplied locator defines the representation-storage model.
Constants depend on explicit versus implicit atom storage.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The storage formula follows from the declared model and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but the representation and machine-word model has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Representation-Compression Cost
children.top_down_role: Computational expense incurred while reducing active-representation size.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic upper bound for exact compression of an explicitly represented active convex combination in reduced affine coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i a_i\), with \(\lambda\in\Delta_m\), and suppose reduced coordinates of the active atoms lie in an affine space of dimension at most \(r\). While more than \(r+1\) coefficients are positive, an affine dependence among any \(r+2\) active atoms permits a coefficient displacement that preserves \(x\), nonnegativity, and unit sum while setting at least one coefficient to zero. Thus at most \((m-r-1)_+\) eliminations produce a representation with at most \(r+1\) atoms. If one reduced-coordinate dependence solve costs \(O(r^3)\), the arithmetic cost is \(O((m-r-1)_+r^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated affine-dependence elimination exactly reduces an m-atom convex representation to at most r+1 atoms; with dense reduced-coordinate solves, its naive cost is O((m-r-1)+ r cubed).
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i a_i\) and \(\lambda\in\Delta_m\).
\(\operatorname{affdim}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\le r\).
Reduced affine coordinates are available and each dependence solve costs \(O(r^3)\).

notation.meaning: Affine-dimension bound in the supplied reduced coordinates.
Number of atoms remaining after compression.

review_flags: The bound is implementation-specific; forming reduced coordinates or reading ambient-coordinate atoms must be charged separately when not already available.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Exact Affine-Dependence Compression Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Output Cardinality Does Not Determine Compression Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates existence of a short representation from the work required to construct one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The existence of an equivalent representation with at most \(r+1\) atoms determines neither arithmetic work nor oracle cost. A compression bound additionally requires an input encoding, a method for finding affine dependencies, and a convention for charging coordinate formation and internal oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short representation may exist without being cheap to find; compression cost needs an explicit input and implementation model.
review_flags: The Builder's unconditional linear input-access lower bound was removed because it depends on whether the represented point or other sufficient state is separately supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Output Cardinality Does Not Determine Compression Cost
Representation-Compression Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting definition for arithmetic and oracle work attributable to active-representation compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose compression is invoked at outer-iteration indices \(t\in K\). Let \(m_t\) be the input active-set size, \(r_t\) the output size, \(\varepsilon_t\ge0\) the requested representation tolerance, and \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}(m_t,r_t,\varepsilon_t)\) the arithmetic work charged to that invocation. Define total compression work by \(W_{\mathrm{comp}}=\sum_{t\in K}C_{\mathrm{comp}}(m_t,r_t,\varepsilon_t)\). Objective, gradient, and linear-oracle calls made during compression are additionally entered in their respective oracle counts; a purely algebraic exact compression makes none of those oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation-compression cost is the sum of the arithmetic work charged to each reduction, while any oracle calls made internally are also charged to their corresponding oracle categories.
assumptions_latex: Every compression invocation declares its input size, output size, and tolerance.
Oracle calls internal to compression are identifiable in the execution trace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{comp}}=\sum_{t\in K}C_{\mathrm{comp}}(m_t,r_t,\varepsilon_t)\), with internal oracle calls charged separately.

notation.meaning: Outer iterations at which compression is invoked.
Arithmetic-cost model for one compression invocation.

review_flags: A source with a specific locator is required for the compression-cost accounting convention.

children.title: Maintenance Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes balancing correction quality, memory use, compression effort, and iteration expense.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified model-relative condition for eager, periodic, and lazy maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a maintenance action at time \(t\) cost \(K_t\), and let \(C_u^{\mathrm{skip}}\) and \(C_u^{\mathrm{act}}\) be predicted priced costs at future time \(u\) without and with the action. For horizon \(H\) and \(0<\delta\le1\), define \(B_t(H)=\sum_{u=t+1}^{H}\delta^{u-t}(C_u^{\mathrm{skip}}-C_u^{\mathrm{act}})\). Within this predictive model, acting has no larger total cost than skipping exactly when \(B_t(H)\ge K_t\). Eager policies test frequently, periodic policies restrict eligible times, and lazy policies wait for certification. Without common resource prices, crossed computation and memory vectors have no invariant scalar ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintenance is worthwhile when its priced future savings exceed its immediate cost; policy families differ in when this break-even test is permitted or evaluated.
assumptions_latex: All resource changes are converted to a common scalar cost using fixed nonnegative prices.
The action has immediate cost \(K_t\).
Predicted future costs with and without the action are specified.
\(0<\delta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{act at }t\iff\sum_{u=t+1}^{H}\delta^{u-t}(C_u^{\mathrm{skip}}-C_u^{\mathrm{act}})\ge K_t\) within the declared model.

notation.meaning: Discount or survival factor applied to predicted savings.

review_flags: This is an exact comparison within the declared predictive cost model, not a distribution-free performance theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Discounted Maintenance Break-Even Rule
Maintenance Tradeoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost regimes for maintaining an explicit atomic representation of conditional-gradient iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_{t,a}a\), where \(S_t\) is an active set and \(\alpha_{t,a}>0\) with \(\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_{t,a}=1\). If one iteration costs \(M(|S_t|)\) for representation maintenance and compression at iteration \(t\) costs \(K_t\), then total maintenance cost through iteration \(T\) is \[\mathcal C_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}M(|S_t|)+\sum_{t\in\mathcal K_T}K_t.\] Eager compression is preferable when its reduction of subsequent maintenance and storage costs exceeds \(K_t\); lazy maintenance is preferable when compression cost exceeds that reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressing an active representation is worthwhile exactly when its future maintenance and storage savings exceed the compression cost.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) for an atomic set \(\mathcal A\).
Each iterate has a finite convex representation supported on \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_T=\sum_{t<T}M(|S_t|)+\sum_{t\in\mathcal K_T}K_t\), with the regime determined by net downstream savings.

notation.meaning: active atoms representing the current iterate
per-iteration cost of maintaining a representation of size m

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accounting model and eager-versus-lazy tradeoff are plausible, but no source supports the conditional-gradient-specific model, and storage savings are invoked without being defined in the displayed cost.

children.title: Distributed Coordination Cost
children.top_down_role: Chapter-local cost interface for block and distributed implementations.

children.title: Communication Cost
children.top_down_role: Expense associated with transferring iterates, atoms, gradients, or oracle results.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Payload-based communication accounting for a distributed conditional-gradient implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(1,\ldots,p\) executing \(T\) distributed iterations, let \(E_t\) be the multiset of directed messages transmitted during iteration \(t\), and let \(b(m)\) be the encoded length of message \(m\) in bits. Define the total communication volume and message count by \[B_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{m\in E_t}b(m),\qquad N_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}|E_t|.\] If \(E\) is a fixed set of directed links and each iteration transmits one \(d\)-dimensional vector, encoded with \(q\) bits per coordinate, along every link in \(E\), then \[B_T=T|E|dq.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication cost is measured by total transmitted bits and message count. Sending one d-dimensional vector with q bits per coordinate along every link in a fixed link set E during each of T iterations transmits T|E|dq bits.
assumptions_latex: Messages have finite encoded bit lengths.
The accounting horizon contains \(T\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_T=\sum_{t<T}\sum_{m\in E_t}b(m)\) and \(N_T=\sum_{t<T}|E_t|\); under the stated fixed-link example, \(B_T=T|E|dq\).

notation.meaning: multiset of messages transmitted during iteration t
fixed set of directed communication links in the example
encoded bit length of message m

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Volume and Message Count Do Not Determine Wall Time
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on converting aggregate communication metrics into elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equal aggregate pairs \((B_T,N_T)\) need not produce equal communication time because messages can traverse links with different latency or bandwidth, contend for shared links, or overlap on disjoint links. Thus \((B_T,N_T)\) determines elapsed communication cost only after topology, routing, contention, overlap, and link-price conventions are specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical total bits and message counts can have different runtimes because placement, contention, and overlap matter.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Volume and Message Count Do Not Determine Wall Time

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarization of critical-path message count and payload under a declared nonoverlap model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For critical-path messages \(m\), suppose message \(m\) costs \(\alpha_m+\beta_m b(m)\), where \(\alpha_m\ge0\) is startup latency, \(\beta_m\ge0\) is time per bit, and \(b(m)\) is encoded length. If these critical-path charges do not overlap, \[T_{\mathrm{comm}}=\sum_{m\in\mathrm{CP}}\bigl(\alpha_m+\beta_m b(m)\bigr).\] Uniform prices give \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}=\alpha N_{\mathrm{CP}}+\beta B_{\mathrm{CP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latency–bandwidth model converts critical-path messages and transmitted bits into elapsed communication time.
assumptions_latex: The execution critical path, routing, and encoded message lengths are fixed.
Charged communications on the critical path do not overlap.

notation.meaning: Messages on the declared execution critical path.
Startup-latency and per-bit prices for message m.

knowledge_statements.title: Latency–Bandwidth Communication Time

children.title: Synchronization Cost
children.top_down_role: Waiting and coordination overhead imposed by synchronized execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier and waiting-time accounting for synchronous distributed iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(t\) requires every worker \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\) to finish local work of duration \(\tau_{t,i}\) before a barrier releases. The synchronization waiting cost at that barrier is defined by \[W_t=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\left(\max_{1\le j\le p}\tau_{t,j}-\tau_{t,i}\right).\] If the barrier itself has latency \(\beta_t\), the elapsed coordination cost through \(T\) iterations is \[S_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\left(\max_i\tau_{t,i}+\beta_t\right).\] Thus synchronous elapsed time is governed by the slowest worker at every barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization cost combines barrier latency with worker idle time, and each synchronous round lasts as long as its slowest worker.
assumptions_latex: All workers enter one blocking barrier per iteration.
Local durations and barrier latencies are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: worker i local computation time in iteration t
aggregate worker waiting time at the barrier

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Idle Time Is Not Critical-Path Delay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates processor-time waste from elapsed synchronization imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one barrier with worker durations \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_p\), let \(\tau_{\max}=\max_i\tau_i\). Aggregate idle processor-time is \(W=\sum_i(\tau_{\max}-\tau_i)\), whereas imbalance relative to mean local duration is \(D=\tau_{\max}-p^{-1}\sum_i\tau_i\). Hence \(W=pD\). The two quantities cannot be interchanged without specifying whether the metric is aggregate processor-time waste or critical-path imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total worker idle time is p times the slowest-worker imbalance relative to mean work, so aggregate waiting and elapsed delay are different metrics.
assumptions_latex: All \(p\) workers enter the same blocking barrier.
Worker durations are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Slowest-worker duration minus mean worker duration.

children.title: Asynchrony-Induced Overhead
children.top_down_role: Extra implementation cost arising from stale information and delayed coordination.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Staleness Does Not Bound Redundant Launches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of deriving oracle overhead from accepted-update delay alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M\ge1\), let \(M\) workers launch identical computations from one snapshot and finish before any update is accepted. Accept one result and discard the other \(M-1\). Every completed computation crosses zero intervening accepted updates, yet one accepted update incurs \(M\) launches and \(M-1\) discarded completions. Hence an accepted-update delay bound \(\tau\), without an independent launch or concurrency discipline, implies no bound \(N_{\mathrm{launch}}\le(\tau+1)N_{\mathrm{acc}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even zero staleness can coexist with arbitrarily many redundant computations when concurrent launches are unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: Delay is measured by intervening accepted updates.
Concurrent or duplicate launches are not independently bounded.

notation.meaning: Arbitrary number of duplicate concurrent computations.

review_flags: This corrects the insufficient-concurrency assumption in the immutable deferred seed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accepted, Discarded, and Outstanding Work Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon accounting identity for asynchronous computation overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition all computations launched by an observation horizon into accepted results, discarded or unused completed results, and still-outstanding computations. If their counts are \(N_{\mathrm{acc}},N_{\mathrm{disc}},N_{\mathrm{out}}\), then \[N_{\mathrm{launch}}=N_{\mathrm{acc}}+N_{\mathrm{disc}}+N_{\mathrm{out}}.\] Relative to a serial reference charging one completed computation per accepted update, \(N_{\mathrm{disc}}\) is realized redundant completed work; whether \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\) is charged depends on cancellation and horizon conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous launches partition into accepted, discarded, and outstanding work; discarded completions are realized redundant work, while outstanding tasks require a charging convention.
assumptions_latex: Every launched computation has exactly one stated status at the observation horizon.
The serial reference charges one completed computation per accepted update.

notation.meaning: Completed computations whose results are unused.
Computations unfinished at the observation horizon.

knowledge_statements.title: Accepted, Discarded, and Outstanding Work Decomposition
Asynchrony-Induced Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-call overhead caused by boundedly stale distributed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a serial conditional-gradient execution require \(T(\varepsilon)\) accepted updates to obtain objective error at most \(\varepsilon\). In an asynchronous execution, suppose each accepted update uses information delayed by at most \(\tau\) update events and triggers at most one oracle call. Counting every stale computation that can overlap an accepted update, the number of oracle calls satisfies \[N_{\mathrm{oracle}}(\varepsilon)\le (\tau+1)T(\varepsilon).\] Hence the excess oracle work attributable solely to bounded overlap is at most \(\tau T(\varepsilon)\). This accounting bound does not itself guarantee convergence under stale gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With delay bounded by τ, at most τ stale oracle computations can accompany each accepted update, giving at most (τ+1)T oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: Information delay is bounded by \(\tau\) update events.
Each computation issues at most one linear-minimization oracle call.
The serial accuracy target requires \(T(\varepsilon)\) accepted updates.

notation.meaning: accepted updates required by the serial reference execution
asynchronous oracle-call count to the target accuracy

children.title: Distributed Coordination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost-accounting distinctions across centralized, decentralized, synchronous, and asynchronous coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Coordination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost comparison among synchronous, asynchronous, and communication-avoiding coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the number of accepted distributed conditional-gradient updates, \(c_{\mathrm{msg}}\) the communication cost per round, \(c_{\mathrm{bar}}\) the barrier cost per round, and \(c_{\mathrm{stale}}(\tau)\) the expected extra work per accepted update under delay bound \(\tau\). The coordination costs are modeled by \[C_{\mathrm{sync}}=R(c_{\mathrm{msg}}+c_{\mathrm{bar}}),\qquad C_{\mathrm{async}}=R(c_{\mathrm{msg}}+c_{\mathrm{stale}}(\tau)).\] Synchronous coordination is cheaper exactly when \(c_{\mathrm{bar}}\le c_{\mathrm{stale}}(\tau)\); otherwise the asynchronous regime is cheaper under this additive model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under additive accounting, synchronous coordination wins when barrier cost is no larger than stale-work overhead; otherwise asynchronous coordination wins.
assumptions_latex: Both regimes produce the same number \(R\) of accepted updates.
Communication, barrier, and stale-work costs combine additively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{sync}}\le C_{\mathrm{async}}\) if and only if \(c_{\mathrm{bar}}\le c_{\mathrm{stale}}(\tau)\).

notation.meaning: per-update overhead from delay-bounded stale work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost condition for replacing coordinated rounds with additional local or approximation work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a baseline reaching a fixed target accuracy have total cost \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\). Suppose a communication-avoiding variant removes coordination cost \(G\ge0\) but adds total local, approximation, or convergence-inflation cost \(\Delta\ge0\), measured with the same additive prices. Then \(C_{\mathrm{avoid}}=C_{\mathrm{base}}-G+\Delta\), so communication avoidance is cheaper exactly when \(\Delta<G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication avoidance wins exactly when its added work is cheaper than the coordination cost it removes, at equal target accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Both regimes meet the same target guarantee.
Removed and added costs use one additive price model.

notation.meaning: Coordination cost removed by the communication-avoiding regime.
Additional local, approximation, or convergence-inflation cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Avoiding Crossover

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-vector comparison of coordinator-based and neighbor-based coordination patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a distributed regime by \(\mathcal C=(R,B,N,S,L)\): coordinated rounds, transmitted bits, messages, synchronization events, and local work. In a star pattern where each of \(p\) workers sends and receives one \(d\)-coordinate, \(q\)-bit vector per round, \(B=2Rpdq\) and \(N=2Rp\). In neighbor exchange over a fixed directed edge set \(E\), one such vector per edge and round gives \(B=R|E|dq\) and \(N=R|E|\). These profiles do not imply universal dominance because required rounds, local work, and critical-path congestion may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centralized and decentralized patterns have different message profiles, but neither is universally cheaper without their round, local-work, and network costs.
assumptions_latex: Messages are uncompressed.
Every declared star link or directed graph edge carries the stated vector once per round.

children.title: Boundary-Inertia Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Slow progress and representation inertia near boundary solutions.

children.title: Boundary-Optimum Zigzagging
children.top_down_role: Alternation among atoms near low-dimensional solution faces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classical Frank–Wolfe trajectory alternates indefinitely between the endpoints of an optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C=\operatorname{conv}\{p,q,r\}\subset\mathbb R^2 with p=(-1,0), q=(1,0), r=(0,1), and f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2. Start at x_0=r and apply classical Frank--Wolfe with an exact LMO and exact line search, breaking the initial tie in favor of q. Then x_1=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12). For any later x_t=(u_t,v_t) with u_t\ne0 and v_t>0, the LMO selects s_t=(-\operatorname{sign}(u_t),0). Writing \sigma_t=\operatorname{sign}(u_t) and D_t=(1+|u_t|)^2+v_t^2, exact line search gives u_{t+1}=-\sigma_t v_t^2/D_t and v_{t+1}=v_t(1+|u_t|)/D_t. Hence u_t changes sign at every iteration, the selected atoms alternate indefinitely between p and q, and x_t\to(0,0), the relative-interior minimizer of the bottom face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a triangular quadratic problem, exact-line-search Frank–Wolfe converges to a boundary optimum while alternating forever between the two endpoints of the optimal face.
assumptions_latex: Classical toward-only Frank--Wolfe uses an exact LMO and exact line search.
The initial LMO tie at \(x_0=(0,1)\) is resolved in favor of \((1,0)\).

notation.meaning: endpoints of the optimal bottom face
positive denominator in the exact line-search recurrence

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Exact-Line-Search Zigzagging
Boundary-Optimum Zigzagging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential atom switching near an optimum in a proper face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), whose minimizer \(x^*=(0,0)\) lies in the relative interior of the bottom edge. At an iterate \(x_t=(u_t,v_t)\) with \(v_t>0\), the classical Frank--Wolfe oracle minimizes \(\langle x_t,a\rangle\) over the three vertices. Whenever an edge vertex is selected, its first coordinate is \(-\operatorname{sign}(u_t)\). Consequently, sign changes of \(u_t\) force alternation between the two edge atoms, producing tangential zigzagging even while \(x_t\) approaches the optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a boundary optimum, changes in the tangential gradient sign can make the linear oracle alternate between opposite vertices of the optimal face.
assumptions_latex: Classical toward-only Frank--Wolfe directions are used.
The linear minimization oracle returns a minimizing vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(u_t\) changes sign and an edge vertex is selected, the selected edge atom alternates between \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle calculation is correct conditionally, but the record does not establish that a Frank–Wolfe trajectory undergoes the asserted sign changes while approaching the optimal face. A source or a fully specified established trajectory is needed for the failure phenomenon.

children.title: Toward-Only Atom Persistence
children.top_down_role: Retention of obsolete atoms by the classical direction family.

knowledge_statements.title: Toward-Only Atom Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical stored toward updates cannot delete a represented atom unless a full step or an explicit representation modification occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t=\sum_{a\in S_t}\alpha_{t,a}a\), where every \(\alpha_{t,a}>0\), and apply the classical toward update \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\) with \(s_t\in\mathcal A\) and \(0\le\gamma_t<1\). Without an intervening compression or re-representation step, the stored coefficient of every old atom \(a\in S_t\) becomes \[\alpha_{t+1,a}=(1-\gamma_t)\alpha_{t,a}+\gamma_t\mathbf 1_{\{a=s_t\}}>0.\] Thus no old atom can be removed by a non-full toward step, including an atom unnecessary for representing an optimum. Direct deletion requires a full step, explicit representation modification, or a direction permitting a negative coefficient change, such as an away direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every non-full classical Frank–Wolfe toward step preserves positive stored weight on every existing atom unless the representation is explicitly modified, so obsolete atoms cannot be directly deleted.
assumptions_latex: The iterate is stored as a finite convex combination with positive coefficients.
The step size satisfies \(0\le\gamma_t<1\).
No compression, merging, or alternative re-representation is performed during the coefficient update.

notation.meaning: toward atom returned by the oracle
indicator that the old atom a is also the selected toward atom

children.title: Geometric Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Rate degradation caused by narrow faces, degeneracy, and unfavorable representations.

children.title: Thin-Polytope Geometry
children.top_down_role: Poor active-set progress associated with narrow polyhedral geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit full-dimensional polytopes whose diameter stays fixed while minimum directional width vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\delta\leq1\), let \[C_\delta=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(0,0),\frac{(1,0)}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}},\frac{(1,\delta)}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}\right\}.\] Then \(C_\delta\) is a full-dimensional triangle with \(\operatorname{diam}_2(C_\delta)=1\). Its minimum directional width equals its smallest altitude, namely \[\inf_{r\ne0}w(C_\delta,r)=\frac{\delta}{1+\delta^2},\] which tends to zero as \(\delta\downarrow0\). Thus fixed diameter and full dimensionality do not imply a uniform positive directional-width bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasingly flat full-dimensional triangles can retain unit diameter while their minimum directional width tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\delta\leq1\).
Widths and diameters use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Diameter Thin-Triangle Family

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
Directions and widths use the Euclidean norm.
Active sets represent the current point with strictly positive coefficients, equivalently with the point in the relative interior of their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{PWidth}(A)=\min_F\inf_{x\in F}\inf_{0\ne r\in\operatorname{cone}(F-x)}\min_{S\in\mathcal S_x,\,S\subseteq F}\max_{s\in A\cap F,\,v\in S}\langle r/\|r\|_2,s-v\rangle\).

notation.meaning: active atom sets representing x with positive coefficients
pyramidal directional width on a face at a point and feasible direction
pyramidal width of the finite atom set

review_flags: The displayed maximum is equivalently obtained by choosing a forward atom maximizing the directional linear functional and an active atom minimizing it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set-sensitive polyhedral width governing away-step and pairwise progress constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\) for a finite atom set \(A\). For \(x\in C\), let \(\mathcal S_x\) contain the subsets \(S\subseteq A\) for which \(x\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}S)\). For a face \(F\) of \(C\), \(x\in F\), and nonzero \(r\in\operatorname{cone}(F-x)\), define \[\operatorname{PdirW}(F,r,x)=\min_{S\in\mathcal S_x,\,S\subseteq F}\max_{s\in A\cap F,\,v\in S}\left\langle\frac{r}{\|r\|_2},s-v\right\rangle.\] The pyramidal width is \[\operatorname{PWidth}(A)=\min_{F}\inf_{x\in F}\inf_{0\ne r\in\operatorname{cone}(F-x)}\operatorname{PdirW}(F,r,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pyramidal width is the worst directional separation between a forward atom and an active atom over all faces, points, feasible directions, and active representations.
knowledge_statements.title: Pyramidal Width

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\).
The directional and pyramidal widths use the Euclidean norm.
\(A_\delta\) is the vertex set of the accepted unit-diameter thin triangle.

notation.meaning: vertex set of the unit-diameter thin triangle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connection between ordinary thinness and the active-set geometric rate constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite atom set \(A\) with \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A)\), \[\operatorname{PWidth}(A)\leq\inf_{r\ne0}\left(\max_{x\in C}\left\langle\frac r{\|r\|_2},x\right\rangle-\min_{x\in C}\left\langle\frac r{\|r\|_2},x\right\rangle\right).\] Therefore the accepted unit-diameter thin-triangle family satisfies \(\operatorname{PWidth}(A_\delta)\leq\delta/(1+\delta^2)\to0\). Any active-set contraction factor proportional to \(\operatorname{PWidth}(A_\delta)^2\) consequently tends to zero despite fixed diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pyramidal width is no greater than minimum directional width, so the unit-diameter thin triangles also force active-set geometric rate constants to degenerate.
knowledge_statements.title: Thinness Forces Pyramidal-Width Degeneration
Thin-Polytope Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing directional width destroys geometry-independent active-set progress bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\), define its directional width in a nonzero direction \(r\) by \[w(C,r)=\max_{x\in C}\left\langle \frac{r}{\|r\|_2},x\right\rangle-\min_{x\in C}\left\langle \frac{r}{\|r\|_2},x\right\rangle.\] A family \((C_\delta)_{\delta>0}\) is thin if \(\operatorname{diam}(C_\delta)=1\) and \(\inf_{r\ne0}w(C_\delta,r)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). Any conditional-gradient progress estimate whose contraction factor is proportional to the square of such a width degenerates to zero on this family; no uniform positive contraction follows from diameter normalization alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polytopes can retain unit diameter while their minimum directional width vanishes, causing width-dependent conditional-gradient rates to degenerate.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_\delta\) is a compact full-dimensional polytope.
The relevant progress constant is bounded by a positive multiple of minimum squared directional width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\inf_{r\ne0}w(C_\delta,r)\to0\), then every proportional width-squared contraction factor tends to \(0\).

notation.meaning: width of C in direction r
a diameter-normalized family of increasingly thin polytopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric construction is plausible, but conditional-gradient linear-rate results generally use specific constants such as pyramidal width rather than unrestricted minimum directional width. A source is needed to identify the exact algorithm and geometric contraction factor.

children.title: Nonunique Atomic-Geometry Failures
children.top_down_role: Instability and ambiguity associated with nonunique atomic representations.

children.title: Degenerate-Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric pathologies associated with degenerate feasible faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine dependence of atoms contained in a feasible face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a polytope and let \(F\) be a nonempty face of \(C\). The atomic geometry of \(F\) is degenerate when there exist distinct atoms \(a_1,\ldots,a_k\in\mathcal A\cap F\) and coefficients \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\), not all zero, such that \[\sum_{i=1}^k z_i=0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k z_i a_i=0.\] Equivalently, the atoms of \(F\) are affinely dependent. Any strictly positive representation supported on these atoms admits sufficiently small coefficient perturbations along \(z\) that leave both the represented point and total weight unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is atomically degenerate when its atoms are affinely dependent, allowing coefficient changes that do not change the represented point.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is the convex hull of a finite atomic set.
\(F\) is a nonempty face of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy holds exactly when a nonzero \(z\) satisfies \(\sum_i z_i=0\) and \(\sum_i z_i a_i=0\).

children.title: Redundant-Atom Ambiguity

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Atom Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A redundant atom creates distinct atomic descriptions of the same feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\subset\mathbb R\) and use the redundant atomic set \(\mathcal A=\{0,\tfrac12,1\}\). The feasible point \(x=\tfrac12\) has the two distinct convex representations \[x=1\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac12\cdot0+\tfrac12\cdot1.\] Hence its active set may be either \(\{\tfrac12\}\) or \(\{0,1\}\), although the primal point is identical. Algorithms whose correction, storage, or away-step rule depends on the stored active set can therefore make different representation-level decisions at the same feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the redundant atom 1/2 lets the same point use either one atom or the two endpoints, making active-set decisions ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: Atomic representations are stored explicitly.
Algorithmic decisions may depend on the stored support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(x=\tfrac12\) has distinct supports \(\{\tfrac12\}\) and \(\{0,1\}\).

children.title: Representation Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of admitting multiple atomic representations for the same iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral structure of all convex representations of one point over a fixed finite atom list.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\mathcal R(x)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^m:A\alpha=x,\ \mathbf1^\mathsf T\alpha=1\}.\] Then \(\mathcal R(x)\) is a nonempty compact polytope. A vector \(\alpha\in\mathcal R(x)\) is an extreme point exactly when \(\{a_i:i\in\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\}\) is affinely independent. Consequently, every extreme representation uses at most \(d+1\) atoms, and representation nonuniqueness is equivalent to \(|\mathcal R(x)|>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex representations of a point form a compact coefficient polytope whose vertices are precisely the representations supported on affinely independent atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\).
\(x\in\operatorname{conv}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(x)\) is a nonempty compact polytope, and \(\alpha\in\mathcal R(x)\) is extreme if and only if its support atoms are affinely independent.

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns are the listed atoms
polytope of convex coefficient representations of x

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Fiber Polytope
Representation Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-space characterization of multiple convex representations over a fixed atom list.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\), and let \(x\in\operatorname{conv}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\). The atomic representation of \(x\) is nonunique precisely when there exist distinct vectors \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \[A\alpha=A\beta=x,\qquad \mathbf 1^\mathsf T\alpha=\mathbf 1^\mathsf T\beta=1.\] Equivalently, for some feasible coefficient vector \(\alpha\), there is a nonzero vector \(z\in\ker A\) with \(\mathbf 1^\mathsf Tz=0\) such that \(\alpha+z\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point has multiple atomic representations exactly when two distinct simplex coefficient vectors map to it, equivalently when a feasible null-space perturbation exists.
assumptions_latex: The atom list is finite.
Coefficient vectors are required to lie in the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Representation nonuniqueness is equivalent to the existence of feasible \(\alpha\) and nonzero \(z\) with \(Az=0\), \(\mathbf 1^\mathsf Tz=0\), and \(\alpha+z\ge0\).

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns are the atoms

children.title: Active-Set Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of active-set composition to small geometric or numerical changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discontinuous oracle-selected supports under arbitrarily small linear-objective perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{a_+,a_-\}\subset\mathbb R^2\), where \(a_+=(1,1)\) and \(a_-=(1,-1)\). For \(g_\delta=(-1,\delta)\), the linear minimization oracle satisfies \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\{a_+,a_-\}}\langle g_\delta,a\rangle=\begin{cases}\{a_-\},&\delta>0,\\ \{a_+\},&\delta<0,\\ \{a_+,a_-\},&\delta=0.\end{cases}\] Although \(g_\delta\to g_0\), the uniquely selected atom jumps by Euclidean distance \(2\) across \(\delta=0\). Thus active atoms need not vary continuously near an exposed-face tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a tied face, an arbitrarily small gradient perturbation can switch the oracle output between atoms a fixed positive distance apart.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns an exact minimizer of the linear objective.
No tie-breaking rule enforces continuity across objective perturbations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\delta\) crosses \(0\), the unique oracle atom switches between \(a_-\) and \(a_+\), whose distance is \(2\).

notation.meaning: objective vector exposing the tied face

children.title: Norm-Dependent Scaling Failures
children.top_down_role: Degradation obscured by poorly scaled, non-affine-invariant models.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Dependent Scaling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of norm-dependent rate surrogates under an ill-scaled affine parametrization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-1,1]^2\) and \(f(x)=x_1^2/2\). Under the reparametrization \(x=T_Mz\), where \(T_M=\operatorname{diag}(1,M^{-1})\), the transformed domain is \(C_M=[-1,1]\times[-M,M]\) and \(f(T_Mz)=z_1^2/2\). Its Euclidean smoothness constant is \(L_M=1\), while \(\operatorname{diam}_2(C_M)^2=4(1+M^2)\). Hence the norm-dependent surrogate \(L_M\operatorname{diam}_2(C_M)^2\) diverges as \(M\to\infty\), although the optimization problem and affine-invariant Frank--Wolfe curvature are unchanged. Bounds expressed only through a fixed-coordinate norm can therefore report arbitrarily poor conditioning caused solely by scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine rescaling can make the usual smoothness-times-diameter bound arbitrarily large even though the underlying conditional-gradient problem and its affine-invariant curvature are unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Smoothness and diameter are measured in the Euclidean norm of the displayed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_M\operatorname{diam}_2(C_M)^2=4(1+M^2)\to\infty\), while the affine-invariant problem is unchanged.

children.title: Linear-Oracle Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability limits caused by unavailable, unbounded, intractable, or insufficiently accurate linear minimization.

children.title: Unbounded Linear Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Failure of the standard oracle model on unsuitable noncompact domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite but unattained linear infimum on a closed noncompact convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\geq e^u\},\qquad c=(0,1).\] Then \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and noncompact. Moreover, \(\inf_{z\in C}\langle c,z\rangle=0\), but no point of \(C\) has second coordinate zero, so the argmin is empty. Every \(d\in C^\infty\) satisfies \(\langle c,d\rangle\geq0\); hence absence of a strictly decreasing recession direction does not ensure attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective over the closed exponential epigraph has finite infimum zero but no minimizer, although no recession direction decreases it.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^2\) is the epigraph of the exponential function.
The linear cost is \(c=(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Nonattained Linear Infimum
Unbounded Linear Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment or value divergence of the conditional-gradient linear minimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable objective \(f:C	o\mathbb{R}\), the standard conditional-gradient oracle at \(x\in C\) requires an element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x),sangle\). The oracle is undefined if this set is empty. In particular, if the recession cone \(C^\infty\) contains a direction \(d\) satisfying \(\langle
abla f(x),dangle<0\), then \(\inf_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x),sangle=-\infty\). Thus a noncompact feasible set lies outside the standard oracle model whenever the current gradient exposes a decreasing recession direction; boundedness of the original objective alone does not supply an oracle solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear oracle fails when a feasible recession direction has negative gradient pairing, because its linear subproblem then has value minus infinity and no minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(d\in C^\infty\) and \(\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle<0\), then the standard linear minimization oracle has no output.

children.title: Intractable Linear Oracles
children.top_down_role: Domains for which linear optimization provides no computational advantage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete implicitly represented compact polytopes with NP-hard exact linear minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), let \[C_G=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S\in\{0,1\}^{V}:S\subseteq V\text{ is a stable set of }G\}.\] Given nonnegative rational weights \(w\), \[\min_{s\in C_G}\langle-w,s\rangle=-\max_{S\text{ stable}}\sum_{i\in S}w_i=-\alpha_w(G).\] Thus an exact linear minimization call over the graph-represented family \(C_G\) solves maximum-weight independent set. Consequently, exact conditional-gradient iterations over this family are not polynomial-time in the worst case unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), despite every \(C_G\) being compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear minimization over a graph-represented stable-set polytope solves maximum-weight independent set and is NP-hard in the worst case.
assumptions_latex: The graph \(G=(V,E)\) and rational weights \(w\in\mathbb Q_+^V\) are explicitly supplied.
The stable-set polytope is accessed through the graph representation, not an explicit vertex list.
\(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{s\in C_G}\langle-w,s\rangle=-\alpha_w(G)\), so the exact linear oracle is NP-hard in the worst case.

notation.meaning: convex hull of stable-set incidence vectors
maximum weight of a stable set

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Set Oracle Hardness
Intractable Linear Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary when linear minimization over the feasible family is itself hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{C_n\}_{n\geq1}\) be a family of compact feasible sets represented with input size polynomial in \(n\). Suppose the decision problem \(\min_{s\in C_n}\langle c,s\rangle\leq q\), for rational \(c\) and \(q\), is NP-hard. An exact conditional-gradient iteration requiring \(s_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C_n}\langle g_t,s\rangle\) then contains an NP-hard subproblem in the worst case. Consequently, unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), the projection-free form of the update does not yield a polynomial-time iteration for this representation of \(C_n\); tractability must instead come from special structure or an explicitly controlled approximate oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If linear optimization over the represented feasible family is NP-hard, an exact conditional-gradient step is also worst-case intractable despite avoiding projections.
assumptions_latex: The feasible-set representation permits polynomial-size rational oracle inputs.
The method requires an exact linear minimizer.
\(\mathrm{P}\neq\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No polynomial-time implementation of every exact oracle call exists for the family \(\{C_n\}\), unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).

children.title: Persistent Oracle Error
children.top_down_role: Accuracy floors and certificate ambiguity under uncontrolled oracle error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the additive correction in an approximate Frank–Wolfe gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,1]\), \(f(u)=u\), and evaluate the oracle at \(x=\delta\), where \(0<\delta\leq1\). The exact minimizer is \(s^*=0\), but an additive-error oracle may return \(\tilde s=x\), since \(\langle1,\tilde s\rangle=\min_{s\in C}\langle1,s\rangle+\delta\). Then \(\tilde g=\langle1,x-\tilde s\rangle=0\), whereas the exact gap and objective suboptimality both equal \(\delta\). Hence the additive correction cannot generally be reduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error oracle can report zero gap at a point whose exact gap and suboptimality equal the full error tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\delta\leq1\).
The linear oracle permits additive error \(\delta\).

notation.meaning: gap computed from the approximate output

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Additive-Gap Ambiguity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective recursion and asymptotic floor for additive-error conditional-gradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_t=f(x_t)-f^*\). Under the stated curvature and additive-oracle assumptions, \[h_{t+1}\leq(1-\gamma_t)h_t+\gamma_t\delta_t+\frac{C_f}{2}\gamma_t^2.\] If \(\sum_t\gamma_t=\infty\), \(\gamma_t\to0\), and \(\delta_t\to0\), then \(h_t\to0\). Under the same stepsize conditions, if only \(0\leq\delta_t\leq\bar\delta\), then \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}h_t\leq\bar\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive linear-oracle error enters Frank–Wolfe progress linearly: vanishing error preserves convergence, while persistent bounded error permits an objective floor.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(C\), with Frank–Wolfe curvature at most \(C_f<\infty\).
\(\langle\nabla f(x_t),\tilde s_t\rangle\leq\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x_t),s\rangle+\delta_t\).
\(x_{t+1}=x_t+\gamma_t(\tilde s_t-x_t)\), where \(0<\gamma_t\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Frank–Wolfe Error Recursion
Persistent Oracle Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive linear-oracle error imposes an equally sized certificate uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be compact and convex, let \(f\) be differentiable and convex, and let \(x\in C\). Suppose an approximate oracle returns \(	ilde s\in C\) satisfying \(\langle
abla f(x),	ilde sangle\leq\min_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x),sangle+\delta\). Define the reported gap \(	ilde g=\langle
abla f(x),x-	ilde sangle\) and the exact Frank--Wolfe gap \(g=\max_{s\in C}\langle
abla f(x),x-sangle\). Then \(f(x)-\min_C f\leq g\leq	ilde g+\delta\). Therefore a fixed, uncontrolled \(\delta>0\) prevents \(	ilde g\) alone from certifying accuracy below \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With additive oracle error delta, the reported gap certifies suboptimality only up to an added delta, creating an accuracy floor unless the error vanishes or is controlled.

\(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex.
\(\delta\geq0\).

children.title: Active-Representation Maintenance Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Costs arising from growing active sets and increasingly expensive corrections.

children.title: Uncontrolled Active-Set Growth
children.top_down_role: Storage and per-iteration cost growth under long atomic expansions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear stored-support growth implies linear storage, but processing growth requires an operation that touches a growing portion of the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an unrecompressed representation satisfies |A_t|=|A_0|+t and each stored atom requires at least c_{\mathrm{store}}>0 units of storage, then storage at iteration t is \Theta(t). A per-iteration representation-processing cost of \Theta(t) follows only under an additional access model requiring \Theta(|A_t|) atom or coefficient operations; support growth alone does not imply that processing bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear support growth always gives linear storage under constant per-atom storage, whereas linear per-iteration processing cost additionally requires operations that scan a linear portion of the support.
assumptions_latex: Each stored atom and coefficient uses storage bounded above and below by positive constants.
The processing conclusion is invoked only when an iteration performs \(\Theta(|A_t|)\) representation operations.

notation.meaning: storage used by the active representation

knowledge_statements.title: Storage–Processing Cost Boundary
Uncontrolled Active-Set Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case linear growth of an unrecompressed atomic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\in\operatorname{conv}(A_0)\), where \(A_0\) is a finite active set, and consider conditional-gradient updates \(x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)x_t+\gamma_t s_t\) with \(s_t\) an atom and \(0<\gamma_t<1\). Without deletion, aggregation, or recompression, the natural representation satisfies \(A_{t+1}=A_t\cup\{s_t\}\), so \(|A_t|\leq |A_0|+t\). Equality occurs whenever every selected atom is new and every previous coefficient remains positive. Thus iteration complexity alone can conceal \(\Theta(t)\) storage and representation-processing costs after \(t\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without pruning or recompression, one new atom may survive each iteration, producing linear active-set size, storage, and representation-processing growth.
assumptions_latex: Every step size satisfies \(0<\gamma_t<1\).
The implementation retains all atoms with positive coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active-set size can satisfy \(|A_t|=|A_0|+t\), so representation storage is \(\Theta(t)\).

children.title: Expensive Corrective Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Loss of computational advantage when active-hull corrections dominate.

knowledge_statements.title: Expensive Corrective Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-hull correction can erase the low-cost advantage of one linear-oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given active atoms \(A_t=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\), a fully corrective conditional-gradient step solves \(\min_{\alpha\in\Delta_m} f(\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i a_i)\), where \(\Delta_m=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^m:\sum_i\alpha_i=1\}\). Let \(T_{\mathrm{corr}}(m,\eta)\) denote the cost of producing an \(\eta\)-accurate solution and let \(T_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) denote one linear-oracle cost. Whenever \(T_{\mathrm{corr}}(m,
\eta)\) grows without bound relative to \(T_{\mathrm{LMO}}\) along the generated active sets, the per-iteration cost is correction-dominated. Projection avoidance then provides no uniform computational advantage unless correction frequency, active-set size, or correction accuracy is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully corrective step optimizes over the active simplex; if that solve outgrows the linear oracle, corrections erase the method’s cheap-iteration advantage.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on \(\operatorname{conv}(A_t)\).
Correction accuracy is measured by active-hull objective suboptimality \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(T_{\mathrm{corr}}(m,\eta)/T_{\mathrm{LMO}}\to\infty\), corrective work asymptotically dominates the iteration.

notation.meaning: cost of an eta-accurate active-hull correction
cost of one linear minimization oracle call

children.title: Maintenance-Dominated Iterations
children.top_down_role: Practical slowdown when representation updates dominate productive progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Maintenance-Dominated Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized representation maintenance can dominate gradient and oracle work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration \(t\), decompose runtime as \(T_t=T_t^{\mathrm{grad}}+T_t^{\mathrm{LMO}}+T_t^{\mathrm{maint}}\), where maintenance includes coefficient updates, atom lookup, pruning, and recompression. For the first \(N\) iterations define \(R_N=\sum_{t<N}T_t^{\mathrm{maint}}/\sum_{t<N}(T_t^{\mathrm{grad}}+T_t^{\mathrm{LMO}})\). The implementation is maintenance-dominated along a run when \(R_N\to\infty\). In that regime, a bound on gradient evaluations and linear-oracle calls does not bound total runtime within a constant factor; meaningful complexity accounting must include the active-representation operations or impose a uniform amortized maintenance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When accumulated active-representation work grows faster than gradient and oracle work, oracle-count complexity no longer predicts runtime within a constant factor.
assumptions_latex: All runtime components are nonnegative.
The denominator defining \(R_N\) is positive for sufficiently large \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_N\to\infty\), total runtime is not within any fixed constant multiple of gradient-plus-oracle runtime.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit amortized-cost definition and its immediate runtime implication
